segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: It’s bad that they’re like that.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Isn’t it?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎣᏏ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎤᏬᏂᏒ ᏱᎨᏎ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ Ᏼ’ᎠᏛᎬᎦ, ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎤᏬᏂᏌ, ᏣᎳᎩ,--ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎨᎲ … Nicut Ꮒ,ᏓᏳᏂᎩᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᏧᏢᏨ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ Old Folks’ Home-Ꭲ ᏧᏂᏴ,ᏔᏅ ᏲᏁᎦᎭ ᎦᏬᏂᎲ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏣᎳᎩ,--ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏴᎭᏛᎬᎦ, ᎤᏓᏁᏟᏴᏒ ᎩᎳ, ᏳᏟᏢ
segments.transliteration: osi, tsigehv usdayvhvsgi, tla ilvhiyu yonega, uwonisv yigese tla ilvhiyu yv’advgvga, yonega, uwonisa, tsalagi,--atsalagiha gehv … Nicut ni,dayunigida, gehv tsutlvtsv sgi tsinuli,sdanelv Old Folks’ Home-i tsuniyv,tanv yonegaha gawonihv tla ilvhiyu tsalagi,--tsalagi, yvhadvgvga, udanetliyvsv gila, yutlitlv
segments.translation: Osi’s wife, had never spoke English before. You could never hear her talk in English; it was all in Cherokee. She was from Nicut. When that sickness happened to her, they put her in the old folks home. She spoke in all English. You would never hear her speak Cherokee. It changed all of a sudden.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: What was her name?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Wonid, Juanita.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Wow… Ꮎ’Ꮫ Mama ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏲᎦᎵ,Ꭸ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏥᏬᏍᏗᏯᏂᎲ Daddy once a week. ‘ᎸᏢ ᎣᏍᏓᏘᏂᏙᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎨᏯ, ᏣᎨᎵᏏᎲ Daddy
segments.transliteration: Wow… na’dv Mama gehv tla yogali,ge asenv, tsiwosdiyanihv Daddy once a week. ‘lvtlv osdatinidohv nigohilv hena, ageya, tsagelisihv Daddy
segments.translation: Wow… As for Mama, she didn’t know us. But me and Daddy would go get her once a week. We would take her somewhere, she always thought Daddy was a woman.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᎠᏩᏅᏔ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) Ꮭ ᏍᎪᏂ Pantyhose ᏱᏗᏣᏑᎳ ᏓᏥᏲᎮᎵ ᎢᏥᎪᎥ.
segments.transliteration: (uyetsi,sgv) gohu,sdi,’e awanvta (uniyetsi,sgv) tla sgoni Pantyhose yiditsasula datsiyoheli itsigov.
segments.translation: [Laughs] I know something [Laughter] “You’re not wearing panty hose,” I’m going to tell him next time I see him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Well, ᏓᏍᏛᏯᏛᏛᎮᏢᏂ, ᏄᏍᏛ ᎤᏃᏪᎳ ᎯᎢ, … ᎠᎾᎵ,ᏒᎯᎲ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎠᏍᎪᎸᏍᏗ, ᏂᎨᏒᎾ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᎯᎢ, ᏥᏓᎾ,ᏕᎶᏆᎠ, … ᏍᏗᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎡᎵᏭ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏯᎾᏕᏠᎦ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎯᎢᏃ ᏄᏰᎵ,Ꮫ … ᏗᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ’Ꭸ? ᏍᏓᏝᏅᏢ’Ꭱ?
segments.transliteration: Well, dasdvyadvdvhetlvni, nusdv unowela hii, … anali,svhihv tsalagi, gohu,sdi, asgolvsdi, nigesvna, nowule hii, tsidana,deloquaa, … sdiwonisgv eliwu, gohu,sdi, yanadetloga, atsalagi, hiino nuyeli,dv … disdadanvtli’ge? sdatlanvtlv’e?
segments.translation: Well, I’m going to ask you two what they have written here. They’re fighting for the Cherokee language to not fade away. And also, they would hear this conversation, and they would learn something here at this school. That is the reason. Is this your brother, or your sibling?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: No, we’re just friends, we work together.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, your friend. That must be why you joke around with him. [laughs]

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: I’m just beating him to it. [Laughter]
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ‘ᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏗ, ᏕᏍᏓᏙᎠ ᏳᏁᎦ, ᎬᏗ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ’Ꮓ ᎬᏗ,?
segments.transliteration: ‘dohv usdi, desdadoa yunega, gvdi, atsalagi’no gvdi,?
segments.translation: What are your two names in English and in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: For me, Mack Flynn is my name.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Max Vann.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Flynn.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Flynn.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Mack Flynn ᏓᏩᏙᎠ, ᏣᎳᎩ ᎬᏗ, ᎤᏥᏣᏗ, ᏓᏩᏙᎠ,
segments.transliteration: Mack Flynn dawadoa, tsalagi gvdi, utsitsadi, dawadoa,
segments.translation: My name is Mack Flynn. In Cherokee, Utsitsad(i) is my name.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What was it?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Utsitsad(i).

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What is the meaning for that name?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏎᎷ ᎮᎾ, ᏣᏥᏣᏛᏍᎪ “plentiful” ᏌᏭ ᎮᎾ, ᏂᏓᏳᏓᎴᏅᏓ, ᏎᎷ Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: selu hena, tsatsitsadvsgo “plentiful” sawu hena, nidayudalenvda, selu tsi,quisdi, nigali,sdisgo
segments.translation: When corn increases—plentiful—starting with one: it brings forth a lot.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It’s a lot, starting from one, it turns into a lot.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Prosperous.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Prosperous… yeah… ᏂᎯ’Ꮓ ‘Ꮩ ᏕᏣᏙᎠ, ᏳᏁᎦ, ᎬᏗ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ’Ꮕ?
segments.transliteration: Prosperous… yeah… nihi’no ‘do detsadoa, yunega, gvdi, atsalagi’nv?
segments.translation: Prosperous… Yeah… And you, what’s your name in English and Cherokee?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.text: Eddie Bunch ᏓᏩᏙᎠ, ᎠᏓᎨᎮᎦ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏗ,
segments.transliteration: Eddie Bunch dawadoa, adagehega, tsalagi, gvdi,
segments.translation: Eddie Bunch is my name. And in Cherokee it’s Adekeheg(a).

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Eddie Bunch, yeah, and in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Adakeheg(a).

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Who gave you that Cherokee name?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: I think it was my mother.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So, it was your mom… What about you?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎠᏯ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᎡᏥ Ꮭ-Ꮭ ᎮᎾ,--Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎡᏙᏓ, ᏯᎩᎧᎲ Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᎣᏣᏝᏅᏢ ᏯᎩᎧᎲ ᎠᏮᏌ, ᎮᎾ,
segments.transliteration: aya’dv squu etsi tla-tla hena,--tla hena, ilvhiyu edoda, yagikahv tla squu otsatlanvtlv yagikahv awvsa, hena,
segments.translation: It was also my mom. I never had a dad. Also, I never had siblings. It was just me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So, your mom raised you by herself?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎯᎳ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏌᏗᏒ ᏣᎷᏤ ᎡᎶᎯ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᎭᏢ ᎨᎮ ᏣᏅᎪᏥᏞ?
segments.transliteration: hila tsudetiyvsadisv tsalutse elohi, nowule hatlv gehe tsanvgotsitle?
segments.translation: What year did you come to this earth? And, where at did you come to be born?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏓᎵᏆ, ᎤᏪᏘ, Hospital ᏥᎪᏢᏒ 1962 June ᎧᎸ ᏔᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯᏁᎢ,
segments.transliteration: daliqua, uweti, Hospital tsigotlvsv 1962 June kalv tali,sgohinei,
segments.translation: The old hospital in Tahlequah, June 20, 1962.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: We’re the same age.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Don’t be saying that, we’re getting old.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: We’re getting old.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And you? Where did you arrive?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: There, too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So, you came in the same way. What year was it?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: He’s still little.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: He’s still just a boy.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: I wish I was just that age.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Where did you grow up at?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Bell.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Bell-Ꭲ’ᏭᏍᎪ,? … ᏥᏈ,ᏍᏗ,’Ꭸ … ᏓᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏁᎯ’Ꭸ Ꮭ’Ꭸ? ᎾᎥ ᏥᏣᏛᏏᏗᏒ?
segments.transliteration: Bell-i’wusgo,? … tsiqui,sdi,’ge … dadanelv anehi’ge tla’ge? nav tsitsadvsidisv?
segments.translation: Bell, yeah. Were there a lot of houses back then, where you were growing up?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎡᏥ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎠᎾᏓᎸᎢᏴ ᏗᎬᎩᏠᎩ, ᏌᏭ’Ꮕ, Maude ᎠᏃᏎᎲ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᏐᏁᎳ, ᎾᏂᎥ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏚᏩᎧᎲ ᎡᏥ ᎠᏂᏔᎵ, Ꮟ ᏗᎬᎵᏏ,--Ꮧ-ᏗᎬᎩᏠᎩ’Ꮫ ᎤᏲᎱᏌ, ᏚᏂᏯᏅᎲ Ꮎ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏌᏭ ᏙᎦᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ
segments.transliteration: vv etsi’dv tsigehv … anadalviyv digvgitlogi, sawu’nv, Maude anosehv tsuyohusv sonela, naniv diniyotli, duwakahv etsi anitali, si digvlisi,--di-digvgitlogi’dv uyohusa, duniyanvhv na diniyotli, nigada, sawu dogadvhistanv
segments.translation: Yeah. My mom, and her sisters—my aunts, there was one they called Maude. She passed away, and she had nine children. My mom and two of my grandmothers—I mean, two of my aunts—when she [Maude] passed away, they took those kids in, and we were raised as one family.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: She was kind.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᎠᏮᏌ, ᏥᏲᏁᎦ, ᎨᎲ ᏭᏅᎦ,Ꮫ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏑᏓᎵ, ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎩᎳ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᎩᏬᏂᏌ, … ᏙᏣᏟᎲ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏱᏙᏣᏓᏙᎵ,ᏤᎮ Tom ᏧᏪᏥ, ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᏱᎨ--Ᏹ--ᏱᏚᏂ,ᏘᏃᏝ, Ꮭ ᏲᏦᎵᎨ ᏃᏥᏪᏍᎬ ᎡᏚᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏠᎩ’Ꮕ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᎵ--ᎥᎥ ᎡᏠᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎬᏩ--ᎬᎩᏘᏴ ᎦᏛᏍᎬ ᎡᏥ’Ꮕ, Decatur ᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ Bentonville-Ꭲ bus-Ꭲ ᎠᏣᎥ,ᏍᎬ ᏦᎢ ᎨᎲ ᏑᎾᎴ ᎠᎾᏂᎩᏍᎬ Artie Green ᏥᎨᎲ ᏓᏘᏁᎬ bus-Ꭲ ᏒᎯᏰ ᎯᏍᎩ, ᏑᏓᎵ, ‘ᎸᏢ ᎩᎳ, ᎠᏂᎷᎬ “And one morning,” ᎤᏛᏅ “One evening,” ᎤᏛᏅ ᎡᏥ ᎢᎤᎷᏣ, ᏑᏓᎵ, ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎡᏚᏣ ᎡᏠᎩ Ꮭ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ, ᏱᎨᎮ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᏓᏍᏛ “Then one day,” ᎡᏥ “bus-Ꭲ ᎠᏩᏠᏒ ᎠᎩᎷᏣ,” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎠᏭ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏂᏣᏬᏂᏒ” ᎾᎯᏳ’Ꮓ ᏂᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏣᎳᎩ,
segments.transliteration: aya awvsa, tsiyonega, gehv wunvga,dv tsalagi, sudali, yawadetiyvda, gehv gila, tsalagi, agiwonisa, … dotsatlihv yigohida, gehv tla yidotsadadoli,tsehe Tom tsuwetsi, anitsutsa, yige--yi--yiduni,tinotla, tla yotsolige notsiwesgv edutsi tsigehv etlogi’nv, tsigehv eli--vv etlogi tsigehv gvwa--gvgitiyv gadvsgv etsi’nv, Decatur dulvwi,sdanehv Bentonville-i bus-i atsav,sgv tsoi gehv sunale ananigisgv Artie Green tsigehv datinegv bus-i svhiye hisgi, sudali, ‘lvtlv gila, anilugv “And one morning,” udvnv “One evening,” udvnv etsi iulutsa, sudali, yawadetiyvda, gehv edutsa etlogi tla yonega, aniwonisgv, yigehe tsalagiha aniwonisgv sgina aqua,dvdasdv “Then one day,” etsi “bus-i awatlosv agilutsa,” tsadihv “awu tsalagi, nitsawonisv” nahiyu’no nitsiwonisgv tsalagi,
segments.translation: I was the only one that was White, and the rest of them were Cherokee. It wasn’t until I was six years old that I spoke Cherokee. I was always fighting with Tom’s boys, because we couldn’t understand each other. When they would bring them, we didn’t understand what we were saying. My uncle and my aunt—my aunt watched out for me growing up. My mom worked in Decatur and got on the bus in Bentonville. They left at three in the morning. Artie Green drove the bus. And in the evening, they got back around five or six. And one morning… one evening Mom said, when she came back… I was six years old, my uncle and my aunt didn’t speak English, they only spoke Cherokee. I was listening to that. And Mom said, “One day when I got off the bus, all of a sudden you spoke Cherokee.” I was speaking Cherokee ever since.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᎮ ᎠᎯᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏣᏕᏠ,ᏆᎥ ᏙᎲ? ᎠᏣᎳᎩ,
segments.transliteration: ahe ahidi yusdi, tsadetlo,quav dohv? atsalagi,
segments.translation: So, you must’ve learned Cherokee pretty easy?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎠᎮᏗ ᏣᎳᎩ Ꮹ-ᏩᏍᏓᏴ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ ᏗᎦᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗᎲ there’s too many words that mean the same thing.
segments.transliteration: ahedi tsalagi wa-wasdayv gehv adelo,quasdi digali,sdodihv there’s too many words that mean the same thing.
segments.translation: I guess so. Cherokee’s the hardest to learn, the reason is there’s too many words that mean the same thing. That’s why it’s so hard to learn.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That’s true.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: That’s why it’s hard to learn.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That’s true. ‘Cause one word…

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: It has several meanings.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏂᎦᏓ,Ꭺ … Ꮎ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎩᏂᏭᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎾᎥ ᏧᏂᎳᏫ,ᏍᏗ ᏗᏥᎦᏘᏯ, … ᏧᏂᏬᏂᏒ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᎠᎨᏯ, ᎠᏂᏁᎳ, ᏓᎾ,ᏓᎬᎵᎲᏭ, ᏍᏊ “ᎾᏛ ᏧᏬᏢ ᎠᎨᏯ, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏣᎩ,ᎨᎯᏙᎲ” ᏣᏗᎲ ᎾᎾ ᎠᏓᎨᎯᏙᎲ … ᎠᎨᏯ, “ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᏨᎯᎷᎬ ᏱᎬᎨᎯᏙᎳ,” ᏣᎪᎮᎸ Ꮎ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏔᎵ, ᎮᎾ,’Ꮓ ᏂᏚᏓᎴᎩ, “ᎠᎨᎯᏙᎯ,” ᏯᏛᎾ, ᏃᏭ ᎩᎶ …
segments.transliteration: nigada,go … na sawu yuwaga,da, giniwudi, hena, nav tsunilawi,sdi ditsigatiya, … tsuniwonisv sawu yuwaga,da, asgaya, nowule ageya, aninela, dana,dagvlihvwu, squu “nadv tsuwotlv ageya, nigohilv tsagi,gehidohv” tsadihv nana adagehidohv … ageya, “doyu’dv tsvhilugv yigvgehidola,” tsagohelv na tsadihv tali, hena,’no nidudalegi, “agehidohi,” yadvna, nowu gilo …
segments.translation: It has several meanings, yeah… One time, I pastor at a church near Kenwood, they had a talk one time [in Cherokee]. A man and a woman who were married. And they were just joking. He said, “That woman right there was always chasing me.” and she said, “That’s true, when I chase you off, you would always come back.” Like you said, there’s two different meanings if you say “akehidoh(i)” and then someone --

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It drives them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏃᏭᎴ ᎩᎶ ᏗᏓᎨᎯᏙᎯ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᏣᏓᎨᎯᏙᎯ, ᏍᎩᏃ ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᎰ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎩᎳᏴ … “ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏨᎯᎷᎬ” ᏣᎪᏎᎸ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎠᏢᏈ,ᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, ᎠᎨᏯ ᎤᎨᎯᏙᎸ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: Yeah, nowule gilo didagehidohi, nowule tsadagehidohi, sgino nigali,sdiho tsadihv gilayv … “doyu’dv nigohilv tsvhilugv” tsagoselv (uyetsi,sgv) atlvqui,sgv na asgaya, ageya ugehidolv (uniyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: --Yeah, or when you say Didakehidoh(i), ‘s/he chases’ and then you say Tsadakehidoh(i), ‘s/he is chasing it.’ “That’s right, but you would always come back,” she told him. [laughs] That man was bragging about that woman chasing him. [laughter]

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Ꮟ let’s see, ᎪᎯᎬ Lawrence Eagle revival ᏃᎩᏅᏁᎸ Cherokee, North Carolina ᎣᎩᏁᏅᏒ ᏒᎾ,ᏙᏓᏩᏍᏗ, ᏬᎩᏁᏙᎸ Cherokee, North Carolina ᏬᎩᏂᎷᏣ, ᎢᏳᏃ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏂᏣ,ᏛᏓᏍᏛᎾ, ᏱᎩ, ᏍᏓᏱ ᎨᎲ ᎪᏟᏍᏗ ᎾᎮᎾ, Ꮟ ᎤᏪᏘ, ᎮᎾ, Ꮟ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᎯ, ᏄᎲ “ᏴᏓ” ᏥᏲᏎᎲ “ᏗᎦ,ᏚᎴᏂ,” ᏱᎦᏛᎾ, ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᎢᎦᏅ,Ꮤ, “Headlight[s]” - ᏗᎦ,ᏚᎴᏂ, that’s what it—that’s what it amounts to. We’re talking about its headlights – dig(a)tulen(i). ᏴᎭᏂᎦ, “ᎠᏜ ᏗᏝ” ᏯᎾᏓ, … ᎠᎭᏂ’Ꮕ, “What time is it?” ᏱᎦᏛᎾ, “ᎯᎳᎦ, ᎠᏟᎢᎵ,? ᎤᎿ “ᎯᎳ ᏳᏩᏂᎸ?” ᏯᎾᏓ,
segments.transliteration: si let’s see, gohigv Lawrence Eagle revival noginvnelv Cherokee, North Carolina oginenvsv svna,dodawasdi, woginedolv Cherokee, North Carolina woginilutsa, iyuno, osda, nitsa,dvdasdvna, yigi, sdayi gehv gotlisdi nahena, si uweti, hena, si aniwonihi, nuhv “yvda” tsiyosehv “diga,duleni,” yigadvna, gayu,la, iganv,ta, “Headlight[s]” - diga,duleni, that’s what it—that’s what it amounts to. We’re talking about its headlights – dig(a)tulen(i). yvhaniga, “adla ditla” yanada, … ahani’nv, “What time is it?” yigadvna, “hilaga, atliili,? uhna “hila yuwanilv?” yanada,
segments.translation: Let’s see. A long time ago, me and Lawrence Eagle went to Cherokee, North Carolina and had a revival for a week. When we got to Cherokee, North Carolina, if you weren’t listening well, it was hard to understand. They still speak that old dialect, “like for instance,” I was telling him. “If we say car as we know it—big eyes. Headlights, that’s what it, that’s what it amounts to. We’re talking about its headlights, dig(a)tulen(i).” Over there it’s adladidla, ᎠᏜᏗᏜ. And, here [Oklahoma Cherokee say] “What time is it?” Hila atliili, ᎯᎳ ᎠᏟᎢᎵ? Over there [Eastern Band Cherokee] it’s “How many times did it tick?” Hila iyuwanilv, ᎯᎳ ᏳᏩᏂᎸ? Oklahoma Cherokee word for ‘car’ / ᏗᎦᏚᎴᏂ / diktulen / “big eyes”. Eastern Band Cherokee word for Car / ᎠᏜᏗᏜ / adladidla. Oklahoma Cherokee for ‘what time is it?’ / ᎯᎳ ᎠᏟᎢᎵ / hila atliili? Eastern Band Cherokee for the same question is ‘how many times did it tick?’ / ᎯᎳ ᏳᏩᏂᎸ / hila iyuwanilv?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s what he says.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: That’s what this one says. [indicating Guy]

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s what they would say.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᏍᏊ ᏕᏥ-ᏕᏥᏃᏎᎲ ᏴᏫ, ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮫ ᏦᎨᏅᏒ ᎥᎾ’Ᏼ ‘ᎧᎸᎬ ᏗᏢ, … ᎤᎶᏒᏍᏗ ᏔᎵᏍᎪᎯ, ᎾᏕᏘᏱᏍᎬ ᎨᎲ … ᎤᎾ ᏦᎩᎷᏨ Boy, Ꭳ-Ꭳ-Ꭳ-Ꭳ-ᎣᏣ-ᎣᏣᎦ,ᏖᏃᎴᏙᎲ Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏭ ᏯᏁᎲ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏂᏬᏂᎯ, ᎤᎾ ᏗᏢ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᏗᏢ ᎨᎲ … ᎤᎾ ᎣᏣᏂᎩᏍᎬ … ᎤᎾ ᎾᎥᏂᎨᏍᏗ, ᏧᎶᏒ ᎠᏴᏫᏯ ᏗᎧᎾ,Ꮧ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ, ᏃᏭ ᏧᎷᏨ Ꮶ-ᏦᎦᎴᏅᎲ ᎣᏍᏗᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏃᏭ, ᏦᎦᏕᎳᎰᏒ Ꮎ ᎧᏁᎬ ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᎯᎾᎾ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᏦᎦᎴᏅᎲ ᏗᏥ,-ᏗᏥ,-ᏗᏥ,- ᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᎩᎳ ᏧᎴᏅᎲ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏥᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ … ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ ᎧᎵ ᎦᏥᏲᎵᏤᎴ ᏍᏗ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏥᏂ,ᎬᏁᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎨᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᎥᏍᎩ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᎥᏍᎩᎾᎾ ‘ᎧᎸᎬ ᏗᏢ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, … ᎧᎵ ᎦᏥᏲᎵᏤᎴ ᏥᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, Ꮟ ᎡᎯ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ, ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎨᏒ that--ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ,-ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ, ᏕᏥᏃᏎᎰ ᏴᏫ, ᎣᏂ ᏗᏁᎬ, … ᏍᏗ ᏄᏓᎴ ᎾᏅᏁᎲ ᏏᎾ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᏬᏂᏒ ᏍᏓᏱ ᎪᏟᏍᏗ that-that-that next generation. ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎠᏩᏓᎴᏤ ᏳᏓᎭ I can’t understand what they’re saying ᏳᏓᎭ
segments.transliteration: nadv squu detsi-detsinosehv yvwi, sawu yuwaga,dv tsogenvsv vna’yv ‘kalvgv ditlv, … ulosvsdi talisgohi, nadetiyisgv gehv … una tsogilutsv Boy, o-o-o-o-otsa-otsaga,tenoledohv tla squu awu yanehv tsalagi, aniwonihi, una ditlv digaduhv ditlv gehv … una otsanigisgv … una navnigesdi, tsulosv ayvwiya dikana,di asgaya, nowu tsulutsv tso-tsogalenvhv osdiwonisgv nowu, tsogadelahosv na kanegv doyu, hena, tsalagi, gawonisgi, hinana udvhisdi, nowule tsogalenvhv ditsi,-ditsi,-ditsi,- tsiwonisgv tsalagi, nowule gila tsulenvhv tsalagiha tsigawonisgv … doyu, hena kali gatsiyolitsele sdi nudale tsini,gvnehv nahiyu tsigesv asenv, gesdi,’e vsgi agvyi aqua,dvganv vsginana ‘kalvgv ditlv, tsalagi, aniwonisgi, … kali gatsiyolitsele tsigawonisgv gohi tsigi, si ehi, sgina udvhisdi, asenv, gesv that--sgiyusdi,-sgiyusdi, detsinoseho yvwi, oni dinegv, … sdi nudale nanvnehv sina, sgina tsuwonisv sdayi gotlisdi that-that-that next generation. sginana awadaletse yudaha I can’t understand what they’re saying yudaha
segments.translation: I was telling some people this: we went towards the Rising of the Sun (North Carolina) one time. It was over 20 years ago. When we got there, we were looking around. There weren’t hardly any Cherokee speakers there in town. And when we were leaving there, there was a man that passed by that looked native. He came and we started talking. And then I noticed this old man really speaks Cherokee. Then I started speaking Cherokee and immediately he started replying in Cherokee. I could understand him fully, he was putting it a little different, but that was the first time I heard somebody speaking in the East. I could understand him fully. And still to this day, that old man is still alive. And that’s what I was telling people—the younger ones do it a little different than the way he spoke. That next generation is hard to understand. I was having difficulties, sometimes I can’t understand what they’re saying.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏣᏅ,ᏔᏍᎪ, ᏂᎨᎵᏍᎬ ᎠᏯ,? ᎠᏯ,-ᎠᏯ, ᎠᏮᏌᏭ, ᎨᏒ ᏂᎨᎵᏍᎬ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏄᏰᎵ,Ꮫ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏕᎦᏓᎴᏤᎿ Ꮒ ᎤᎿ ᎮᎾ, ᏗᏢ, ᏗᎦᏂᎩᏍᎬ, ᏕᎩᎨᎯᏙᎸ ᎠᏯ, ᎮᎾ, -- ᎠᏯ ᎮᎾ, Ꭸ’Ᏼ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎤᎪᏗ ᎢᎩᎪᎠ, ᎤᎪᏗ, ᎢᎩᎦ,ᏛᎦᎾ, ᏏᎾ ᎣᏂ, they didn’t have to travel as far as we did, they didn’t get to see what we seen, they didn’t get to hear what we heard, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ, they didn’t get to travel so far, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏳᏍᏗ ᎤᏪᏘ, ᎠᏂᏬᏂᎯ, ᎠᏯ, further down ᏱᎯᎷᏨ ᎤᎪᏗ, ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᏳᏍᏗ, we got that little slang. ᏍᏆᎳᎮᏍᏗ ᏱᎬᏁᎸ ᏥᏗᏬᏂᎯ, cause ᎤᎪᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎦᏕᎶ,ᏆᎥ that’s-that’s what I think, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎰᏩ ᏱᎩ, but that’s what I think. ᎠᏯ, ᎨᏒ
segments.transliteration: tsanv,tasgo, nigelisgv aya,? aya,-aya, awvsawu, gesv nigelisgv yusdi, nuyeli,dv sgi tsidegadaletsehna ni uhna hena, ditlv, diganigisgv, degigehidolv aya, hena, -- aya hena, ge’yv agvyi ugodi igigoa, ugodi, igiga,dvgana, sina oni, they didn’t have to travel as far as we did, they didn’t get to see what we seen, they didn’t get to hear what we heard, sgina yusdi, they didn’t get to travel so far, sgina, yusdi uweti, aniwonihi, aya, further down yihilutsv ugodi, sgi hena, yusdi, we got that little slang. squalahesdi yigvnelv tsidiwonihi, cause ugodi, hena, igadelo,quav that’s-that’s what I think, tla yawanv,ta, howa yigi, but that’s what I think. aya, gesv
segments.translation: You know what I think? As for myself, the reason why we are different. Look, we got chased off from there. We have heard a lot more than the ones behind us. They didn’t have to travel as far as we did. They didn’t get to see what we seen. They didn't get to hear what we heard. They didn’t get to travel so far. That’s the reason they still talk the old language, that’s just what I think. We came further down, that’s why we got that little slang. We’ve shortened it down. ‘Cause we have learned more. That’s just what I think, I don’t know if that’s true, but that’s what I think. Yes, it is.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏥᎦᏗᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎦᏥᏲᎵᏤᎲ Ꮭ ᎤᏟ ᎢᎦ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏱᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎨᏍᏗ, Ꮎ that second generation, Ꮎ ᎠᏓᏁᏟ--ᎤᏓᏁᏟᏴᏓᏭ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎾᏅᏗᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: asenv, tsigadisgv sgina udvhisdi, osda, gatsiyolitsehv tla utli iga nudale yigawonisgv nahiyu asenv, gesdi, na that second generation, na adanetli--udanetliyvdawu, yusdi, nanvdisgo
segments.translation: But like I was thinking… When that old man was talking, I could understand him good. He really didn’t talk that much differently. but that second generation has changed it.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᎤᏪᏘ, ᏣᏂᏬᏂᎯ, ᏥᎦᏗ ᎪᏪᎳ, ᎤᎭᎨᏗ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏱᏣᎪᎵᏰᎠ, Ꮎ “ᎥᏝ” ᏣᏂᏍᏗᏟ,ᏔᏂᏙᎲ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, Ꮟ ᎠᏅ,Ꮧ Ꮎ’Ꮕ, ᎠᏯ, ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, “ᏏᏲ” ᏴᏓᎾ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, “ᎣᏏᏲ” ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎦᏅᎯᏗ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏯ, ᎢᏗᏍᏆᎳᎲᏍᏔᎾ,
segments.transliteration: na’dv uweti, tsaniwonihi, tsigadi gowela, uhagedi tsalagi, yitsagoliyea, na “vtla” tsanisditli,tanidohv sgi hena, si anv,di na’nv, aya, gohi tsigi, “siyo” yvdana, nowu’nv, “osiyo” tsanv,ta, ganvhidi hena, aya, idisqualahvstana,
segments.translation: That old language that I said that they speak—if you read that in the Cherokee Bible, when they say “Vtla, ᎥᏝ,” when they add that in there, they still use that. Just like for instance nowadays, we say “Si⁠yo, ᏏᏲ,” they say “O⁠si⁠yo, ᎣᏏᏲ.” Theirs is longer, and we’ve shortened it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ “ᎥᏝ” ᏣᏗᏍᎬ Ꭲ--ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎠᏂᏁᎬ … Ꮟ ᏓᏅ,ᏗᏍᎬ ᎤᎾ … ᎦᏘᏲ ᏥᎨᎳ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎠᎾ,ᏗᏍᎬ “ᎥᏝ” ᏯᎾᏓ, … ᎢᎦᏓ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎦᏴᎳ, ᎤᏂᏪᏓ, ᏯᏂᏁᏍᏓ, ᏳᏓᎵᎭ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎠᎩ-ᎠᎩᎦ,ᏛᎲᏍᎪ, “’ᏙᎩ ᏥᏂᏩ,? Ꮭ ᏱᎪᎵᎦ,” ᎾᏃ ᏯᎩᏃᎯᏏ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎢᎦ ᏄᏪᏒ … ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎨᏒ … ᎯᎾ ᏥᎦᏗᏍᎬ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏣᏩᎴᏅᏓ, ᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎤᎾ Ft. Smith – Baldor ᏥᎨᏒ ᎤᎪᏗ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, ᏥᏚᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎯ, ᏥᎨᏒ ᎤᎪᏗ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᏗᏢ, … Ꭴ-Ꭴ-ᏧᏂᎶᏒ ᏃᏭᎴ Dave Killer ᏣᎨᎸ … ᏃᏭᎴ ᎣᏂ ᏣᎩ,ᏑᎵ,ᎪᏨ October – last year ᏥᎨᏒ ᏙᎯ, ᏥᎾᏮᏁᎸ … ᏌᏭ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ, Ꮟ ᏤᎲ just one.
segments.transliteration: sgina “vtla” tsadisgv i--aqua,dvganv squu tsuna,tana yusdi, aninegv … si danv,disgv una … gatiyo tsigela, sginana ana,disgv “vtla” yanada, … igada hena, agayvla, uniweda, yaninesda, yudaliha yudaha agi-agiga,dvhvsgo, “’dogi tsiniwa,? tla yigoliga,” nano yaginohisi, yusdi, iga nuwesv … asenv, gesv … hina tsigadisgv agvyi tsawalenvda, dagilvwi,sdanehv una Ft. Smith – Baldor tsigesv ugodi anitsalagi, tsidunilvwi,sdanehi, tsigesv ugodi tsuyohusv ditlv, … u-u-tsunilosv nowule Dave Killer tsagelv … nowule oni tsagi,suli,gotsv October – last year tsigesv dohi, tsinawvnelv … sawu tsalagi, gawonisgi, si tsehv just one.
segments.translation: That ‘vtla, no’ you’re saying. I’ve heard some of the older ones saying it. They’re using it at the Stompground, where I’m a member. They’ll say “Vtla.” Sometimes the old people will mention an older word and sometimes I’ll ask, “What did you say? I don’t understand.” Then they’ll tell me what they said. That is what it was. This is what I’m talking about. When we first started working, in Fort Smith where [the company] Baldor used to be, there were a lot of Cherokee working there. A lot of them came from Belfonte. And Dave Killer was with them. When I quit last October, they laid me off. There was still one Cherokee speaker there. Just one. One left. Back then, whenever I walked into any office I could talk to somebody in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: There was just one left.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏌᏭ ᎢᎦ Ꭰ--ᎤᏘᏴ ᎨᎲ … ᎤᎬᏱ ᎨᎲ ᏍᏊ-ᏍᏊ ᎯᎳᏴ ‘ᏙᏭ ᎤᏍᏗ,--‘ᏙᏭ ᎤᏍᏗ department ᏯᎩᏴᏟᏝ, ᎡᎵᏭ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏱᏥᎵᏃᎮᏓ, ᎩᎶ
segments.transliteration: sawu iga a--utiyv gehv … ugvyi gehv squu-squu hilayv ‘dowu usdi,--‘dowu usdi department yagiyvtlitla, eliwu tsalagi, yitsilinoheda, gilo
segments.translation: There was one left. At first, back then, whenever I walked into any office I could talk to somebody in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Ꮒ ᎠᎭᏂ’Ꮽ ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎩ, ᏂᎯ ᎮᎾ, ᏄᏓᎴ ᎯᏬᏂᎯ, ᏏᎾ, ᎠᏯ, ᎨᎲ … ᎤᏠᏱᏭ,--ᎤᏠᏱᏭ, Bell-Ꭲ - Candy Mink Springs ᏱᏫ,ᏣᎷᏣ, ᎠᏂ-Diver-Ꭲ ᏱᏣᎷᏣ, ᎤᎿ ᏴᏕᎳᎰ ᎤᏓᏁᏟᏴᏍᎩ, ᎯᎢ’Ꮫ ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎲ … “Ꭰ’ᎢᎸᏒ” ᏱᎦᏛᎾ, ᎤᎾ Candy Mink Springs ᏱᏫ,ᏣᎶᏐᎾ, “ᎠᎩᎸᏒ” ᏯᎾ,Ꮧ “ᎠᎩᎳᎲᏒ” ᏯᎾᏓ, “ᎠᎩᎳᎰᏒ” ᏯᎾᏗ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏱᎶᏌ,
segments.transliteration: ni ahani’wu hena, tsigi, nihi hena, nudale hiwonihi, sina, aya, gehv … utloyiwu,--utloyiwu, Bell-i - Candy Mink Springs yiwi,tsalutsa, ani-Diver-i yitsalutsa, uhna yvdelaho udanetliyvsgi, hii’dv gatsiyosehv … “a’ilvsv” yigadvna, una Candy Mink Springs yiwi,tsalosona, “agilvsv” yana,di “agilahvsv” yanada, “agilahosv” yanadi nowunv yilosa,
segments.translation: Look, even here, you are talking different than I do. It’s the same in Bell. If you get to Candy Mink Springs [in Stilwell], if you go to the Diver’s, you can tell it’s changing. This is what I was telling them: we say, “A(g)ilvsv,” then when you pass Candy Mink Springs, then they say “Agilahvsv,” and then they will say “Agilahosv.”

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, “ᎠᎩᎴᏃᏙᏗ” ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎲ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏃᏭᎴ Bell-Ꭲ ᏗᏢ, “ᎠᎩᎴᏂ,Ꮧ”
segments.transliteration: na squu tsanv,ta, “agilenododi” tsana,dihv tsanv,ta, nowule Bell-i ditlv, “agileni,di”
segments.translation: And also, you know, when they say “Agilenotodi” and then in Bell they say “Agileyndi.”

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Agileyndi.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Agileyndi.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎾᎮᎾ, Rick Duncan ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ “Ꮭ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᏂᏪ!” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ “ᏂᎯ! Ꮭ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᏂᏪ!” – “ᎠᎩᎴ--ᎤᎴᏃᏙᏗ” ᎦᏗᏍᎬ “ᎤᎴᏱ,Ꮒ,Ꮧ” ᏣᏗᎲ so that’s…
segments.transliteration: nahena, Rick Duncan nigohilv sgina “tla osda, yiniwe!” tsitsiyohelv nigohilv “nihi! tla osda, yiniwe!” – “agile--ulenododi” gadisgv “uleyi,ni,di” tsadihv so that’s…
segments.translation: That Rick Duncan. Every time, I’d tell him, “You’re not saying it right!” and then he’d say, “You’re not saying it right!” I’d say “Agileno–ulenotodi” and then he was saying “Uleyndi.” So that’s --

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᏣᏗ “ᎠᎩᏠᏒ” ‘ᏙᏳ,’Ꮫ ᏣᎾ,Ꮧ ᏗᎨᎬ “ᎠᎩᎿᎷᏒ” ᏯᏓ ᏗᎨᎬ ᏗᏢ, Ꮎ’Ꮫ “ᏣᎩᎿᎷᏒ” ᏯᏓ, Ꮎ ᏣᏗ Ꮎ’Ꮫ “ᏣᎩᎴᏒ” ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎦ ᏚᏓᎴᎿᏓ, ᎠᏭ Jay-Ꭲ ᏗᏥᏁᎳ, - ᏜᏱᎪ
segments.transliteration: nana tsadi “agitlosv” ‘doyu,’dv tsana,di digegv “agihnalusv” yada digegv ditlv, na’dv “tsagihnalusv” yada, na tsadi na’dv “tsagilesv” sgi hena, sgi hena, iga dudalehnada, awu Jay-i ditsinela, - dlayigo
segments.translation: What you’re saying, when you say “Akitlosv” I am from toward Jay, and they say “Akihnalusv” where I’m from. Then you can say “Tsakihnalusv”, then you say “Tsagilesv” that’s how different they are. I live in Jay – Dlayigo.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: I guess you know Richard Pickup well?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Oh, yeah! ᎢᎦ ᏚᏓᎴᎿᏓ, - ᏚᏓᎴᎿᏓ,’Ꮥ ᎢᎩᏬᏂᏒ ᏃᏭᎴ Salem-Ꭲ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏃᏭᎴ
segments.transliteration: Oh, yeah! iga dudalehnada, - dudalehnada,’de igiwonisv nowule Salem-i tsadihv nowule
segments.translation: Oh yeah! It’s really different. Different communities do talk different from each other. Say like, Salem.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Yeah, just right down the road Cherry Tree ᏄᏓᎴ and … Peavine-Ꭲ ᏗᏢ, ᏃᎴ ᏏᏭ ᏄᏓᎴ Nicut ᏏᏭ ᏄᏓᎴ Oak Ridge-Ꮽ ᏥᎩ, ᏏᏭ ᏄᏓᎴ Oak Ridge and Nicut’Ᏺ they pretty much ᎤᏠᏱ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᎯ,
segments.transliteration: Yeah, just right down the road Cherry Tree nudale and … Peavine-i ditlv, nole siwu nudale Nicut siwu nudale Oak Ridge-wu tsigi, siwu nudale Oak Ridge and Nicut’yo they pretty much utloyi aniwonihi,
segments.translation: And then right down the road is Cherry Tree. And they’re different. Then in Peavine, it’s different, too. Then Nicut, different, too. Oak Ridge, it’s different, too. Oak Ridge and Nicut—they pretty much speak the same.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꭱ Leo Duncan ᏲᎩᎾ,ᏝᏃᎮᏝ, ᏄᏓᎴ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏍᏊ ᎦᏬᏂᎰ
segments.transliteration: na’e Leo Duncan yogina,tlanohetla, nudale yusdi, squu gawoniho
segments.translation: When I talked to Leo Duncan, he talks different.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: He’s from around Bell, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: mhmm. Yeah.

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.text: ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏥᎨᎲ he always came to the house.
segments.transliteration: nigohilv tsigehv he always came to the house.
segments.translation: He always came to the house all the time.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎪᎵᎬ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎾᏂᏪᏍᎬ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎭᏢᏭ ᎤᏪᏙᎸ ᎪᎵᎦ’Ꮫ
segments.transliteration: asesgini, goligv nusdv naniwesgv nigada hatlvwu uwedolv goliga’dv
segments.translation: But I understand it all, no matter where they’re from.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎠᏯ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᎪᎵᎦ ᎮᎾ, ᎩᎳ’ᏭᏴ ᎠᏩᏅ,Ꮩ ᏄᏓᎴ
segments.transliteration: aya’dv squu goliga hena, gila’wuyv awanv,do nudale
segments.translation: Yeah, I understand it, too. I really know it’s different.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎠᏯ, ᎮᎾ, ᏥᏕᏥᏃᏎᎳ, ᎠᏋᏌ, ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎵᏙᎸ … ᏥᏫᏂ, -- ᎠᏫᏂ, ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ
segments.transliteration: aya, hena, tsidetsinosela, aquvsa, nawali,sdanelidolv … tsiwini, -- awini, nawali,stanv
segments.translation: When I talk about what all happened to me when I was young.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: I thought you were saying “Hawin awasul(o), I’m wearing underwear.”
[laughter]

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏙᎯ, Ꮵ-ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏔᏅ ᏥᎦᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᎬ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏏᏭ ᎩᎳ ᎤᎪᏗ, ᎦᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᎬ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, ᏏᎾ, Ꮵ-ᏥᏁᏛ
segments.transliteration: dohi, tsi-tsinulistanv tsigadelo,quasgv tsalagi aniwonisgi, sgina siwu gila ugodi, gadelo,quasgv gohi tsigi, sina, tsi-tsinedv
segments.translation: I stopped speaking Cherokee while I was going to school. I learn more today, than before.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏏᏛ ᎯᎳᏴ ᏥᎩ, ᎬᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ, ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎬᎩ,ᏛᏛᏅ “basket” ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ, -- “‘Ꮩ ᎠᏓ, ᏣᎳᎩ ᎬᏗ, basket-Ꭲ?” Man! ᏍᎩ’ᏛᏲ ᎠᏩᏓᏅ,ᏖᏢ ᏎᎦᏨ ᎬᏅᎯᏗ ᏩᏩᏓᏅ,ᏖᏢ “ᏔᎷᏣ,”
segments.transliteration: sidv hilayv tsigi, gvdelo,quasdi, sawu yuwaga,da, gvgi,dvdvnv “basket” ‘do usdi, -- “‘do ada, tsalagi gvdi, basket-i?” Man! sgi’dvyo awadanv,tetlv segatsv gvnvhidi wawadanv,tetlv “talutsa,”
segments.translation: Still yet I’m learning. Not long ago, they asked me how to say ‘basket’ in Cherokee. Man! I really had to think about it. It’s just one word, and I thought about it for a while—‘Taluts(a).’

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Basket.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, … you’re never too old ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎠᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: tsanv,ta, … you’re never too old gohu,sdi, adelo,quasdi
segments.translation: You know, you’re never too old to learn something.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏙᏳ’Ꭲ ᏙᏳ’Ꭲ yeah, ᏍᎩᎾ … Ᏻ-ᏳᏓᎭ ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎾᎩᏪᏍᏗ My tongue, it just don’t work right sometimes. ᏳᏓᎭ Ꭰ-ᏯᏩᏓᎴᏥᏏ, y’know, ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ,--ᏍᎩ ᏄᏰᎵ,Ꮫ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎠᏆᏅ,Ꮤ ᎦᏕᎳᎰᏍᎬ, “Gah! ᏥᏄᏍᏗ, Ꮵ-ᏥᏂ,-ᏥᏂ,-ᏥᏂ,ᏥᏫ”
segments.transliteration: doyu’i doyu’i yeah, sgina … yu-yudaha aginulvhvsgv, osda, nagiwesdi My tongue, it just don’t work right sometimes. yudaha a-yawadaletsisi, y’know, sgi hena,--sgi nuyeli,dv nudale yusdi, tsiwonisgv yudaha aquanv,ta gadelahosgv, “Gah! tsinusdi, tsi-tsini,-tsini,-tsini,tsiwi”
segments.translation: That is right, that’s true. And sometimes I struggle to say things right. My tongue, it just don’t work right sometimes. I can’t say it right. That’s why I speak different sometimes and I realize it, I’ll say, “Gah! What did I say?”

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ, ᏥᎾᎾ,ᏛᏁ ᏱᏂ,ᏣᏛᏁᎳ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎯᏬᏂᎯ, … ᏍᏗᏭ wine ᏱᏫᏅᏁᎳ, ᏭᏚᎩᏍᏔᎾ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎦᏬᏂᎮᏍᏗ, -- (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) Kim Lively ᏧᏙᎢᏓ, ᎡᎯ, West Virginia Ꮒ,ᏓᏳᏂᎩᏓ, ᏅᎩ,ᏍᎪᎯ,’Ꮫ ᎯᎩ,ᏍᎪᎯ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, Ꮎ- Ꭿ-… ᎠᏯ’Ꮫ ᏑᏓᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏔᎵ, … ᎲᎾ ᏣᏁᎳ, ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᏧᏂᎷᏨ Bell-Ꭲ ᏗᏢ, ᏧᎾ,ᏕᏂᏢ ᎯᏃ ᏍᎩ ᏫᏯᏘᏅᏍᏔᎾ, beer ᏫᏅᏁᎳ, ᏅᏃᎯ, ᏙᏍᏓᏟᏒ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏗ, ᏴᎧᏃᎩ, … George Jones ᎤᏃᎩᏍᏛ, (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: na’dv aniyonega, tsinana,dvne yini,tsadvnela, tsalagi, hiwonihi, … sdiwu wine yiwinvnela, wudugistana, atsalagiha gawonihesdi, -- (uniyetsi,sgv) Kim Lively tsudoida, ehi, West Virginia ni,dayunigida, nvgi,sgohi,’dv higi,sgohi,’le yigi, na- hi-… aya’dv sudali,sgohi, tali, … hvna tsanela, yawadetiyvda, gehv tsunilutsv Bell-i ditlv, tsuna,denitlv hino sgi wiyatinvstana, beer winvnela, nvnohi, dosdatlisv tsalagi, gvdi, yvkanogi, … George Jones unogisdv, (uniyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: Just do what the White people do when you’re talking Cherokee. If you give him a little wine, and let him drink it, he’ll be speaking all in Cherokee. [laughter] That Kim Lively is his name, who came from West Virginia. He’s about 40 or 50… Let’s see, I’m 62. When I was about eight years old was when they arrived at Bell to live. If you give him a little beer, running down the road, he’ll probably sing in Cherokee. He would sing George Jones’ songs. [laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏜᏱᎪ ᏗᏢ, ᏤᎲ ᎤᏛᏐᏅ ᎤᏄᎸᎲᏍᎪ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎤᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ … ᎭᏕ ᏲᎪᎵ,Ꭼ, ᎨᎲ “Mi-mi-mi” ᏣᏗᎰ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏅ ᎠᏰᏟ, ᎤᏚᎩᏓ, ᏱᎩ, ᏙᏳ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᏗᎦᏬᏂᎲ … … ᏂᎯ’Ꮓ ᎭᏢ ᏣᏛᏏᏙᎸ?
segments.transliteration: dlayigo ditlv, tsehv udvsonv unulvhvsgo osda, uwonihisdi … hade yogoli,gv, gehv “Mi-mi-mi” tsadiho yusdi, tsigehv nonv ayetli, udugida, yigi, doyu osda, atsalagi, digawonihv … … nihi’no hatlv tsadvsidolv?
segments.translation: There was an old man who lived in Jay, he had trouble talking Cherokee. You couldn’t hardly understand him. He’d be saying like, “Mi-mi-mi.” But if he was half-drunk, he’ll be talking Cherokee real well. And how about you? Where did you grow up?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: In Greasy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎪᎢ ᏗᏢ, … ᏚᏓᎴᎿᏓ,’Ꮫ ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ, ᏙᎲ ᏥᏣᏛᏏᏙᎸ?
segments.transliteration: goi ditlv, … dudalehnada,’dv nowu tsigi, dohv tsitsadvsidolv?
segments.translation: In Greasy? Yeah, it’s really different there now, where you grew up.

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏗ, ᏩᏓᏅ,ᏖᏍᎪ ᏱᏭᏪᏙᎳ, ᎭᏓᏅ,ᏖᏍᎬ ᏥᏣᏛᏏᏙᎸ?
segments.transliteration: dohv usdi, wadanv,tesgo yiwuwedola, hadanv,tesgv tsitsadvsidolv?
segments.translation: What do you think about when you go back down there? Where you grew up.

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: I try not to think.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Were there a lot of people living around near where you grew up?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Not really.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: XXX

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did your kinfolk live nearby?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I guess you all were helping each other?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Yeah. Most of them have passed on now.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, really a lot of them have gone.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ Ꮎ ᎯᎸᏍᎩ, ᏄᎲ ᎤᎾ ᏗᏢ, ᏥᏩᎩᎶᏒ ᎪᎯᏗ, ᎬᏩᎩᎶᏒ ᎤᎾ ᎤᏛᏒ “ᎤᎯᏐᏛ’Ꮽ,” ᏥᏥᏲᎮᎲ Daddy. ᏂᎦᏓ’Ꮽ, ᏳᏍᏗ,…
segments.transliteration: doyu’dv squu na hilvsgi, nuhv una ditlv, tsiwagilosv gohidi, gvwagilosv una udvsv “uhisodv’wu,” tsitsiyohehv Daddy. nigada’wu, yusdi,…
segments.translation: I went through that way not long ago, where he grew up. “It was a sad looking place.” I told Daddy. Just about…

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏓᏤᏢ, Bell-Ꭲ ᏗᏩ-ᏗᏩᏓᏅᏌ, … Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏔᎵ,Ꮑ ᏯᏩᏚᎸᎲ ᏗᎦᏪᏅᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ, ᏧᎾᎵ,ᏒᏃᏅ ᎣᏂ, ᏧᎾ,ᏛᏒ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, Ꭲ-ᎢᎦ ᏄᎾ,ᏓᎴ
segments.transliteration: datsetlv, Bell-i diwa-diwadanvsa, … tla ilvhiyu tali,ne yawadulvhv digawenvsdi na anigayvla, tsunali,svnonv oni, tsuna,dvsv diniyotli, i-iga nuna,dale
segments.translation: It was better when I moved away from Bell. I never wanted to go back. The old ones are all gone. Their kids are all grown now and they’re different.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They are different, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: They’ve stolen from me a few times.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Their way of thinking.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: That’s why I just go back there sometimes. I go visit Blacky.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏱᏍᏓᏓᏅ,ᏖᏝ, … ᏗᏣᏓᏩᏛᎯᏙᎯ’Ꭸ ᎨᎲ Ꮧ-ᏕᏍᏓᏛᏏᏗᏒ?
segments.transliteration: nahiyu tsigesv yisdadanv,tetla, … ditsadawadvhidohi’ge gehv di-desdadvsidisv?
segments.translation: When you all think about back then, did people visit each other?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏧᏍᏗ ᏙᎩᏅᏅ ᏂᎬ ᎡᎳᏗ, ᏙᏣᏏᏰᎲ after school, Friday ᏱᎩ, ᎣᏣᏂᎩᏍᎬ “ᏧᎵᏲ” ᏓᏃᏎᎲ Jodie Sawney, ᏌᎻ’Ꮕ, ᎣᏣᎴᏫᏍᏗᎲ ᎠᏯ, Ꭰ’ᎢᏥ … ᎠᎨᏳᏥ’Ꮕ, ᎣᏍᏓᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ -- ᎣᏍᏓᏘᏂᏒ ᎯᎢ ᎡᎳᏗ ᎣᏣᎢᏐ ᎨᎲ Friday ᏱᎩ, Sunday-ᎢᏅ, ᏒᎯᏰ ᏃᏭ ᏱᏩᏩᏕᏯᎳ, ᏔᎵᎭ ᏄᏙᏢᏒ ᎣᎩᏒᏢ ᎨᎰ ᏃᏭ ᏗᎣᏣᎢᏐ ᎨᎲ ᎩᎳ, ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᎣᏥᎷᎬ
segments.transliteration: tsusdi doginvnv nigv eladi, dotsasiyehv after school, Friday yigi, otsanigisgv “tsuliyo” danosehv Jodie Sawney, sami’nv, otsalewisdihv aya, a’itsi … ageyutsi’nv, osdadvhistanv -- osdatinisv hii eladi otsaiso gehv Friday yigi, Sunday-inv, svhiye nowu yiwawadeyala, taliha nudotlvsv ogisvtlv geho nowu diotsaiso gehv gila, adanelv otsilugv
segments.translation: We had visited everywhere, we were walking after school on Fridays. Julio, they call him, Jodie Sawney. And, Sami. We would stop at my mom’s house. We had a girl that we raised, with us. We would walk on foot, if it was Friday. Then on Sunday evenings, we had spent two days there, and now we were walking back until we got home.

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Yeah!

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Every weekend, ᏍᎩ ᏃᏣᏛᏁᎲ ᏙᏣᏓᏩᏛᎯᏙᎲ … dominoes’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏥᏓᏁᎶᎲᏍᎪ ᎨᎲ ᏓᏂᏆᏲᎯᎰ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᎨᎲ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ … ᏒᏃᏱ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᏯᎾᏅᎦ, ᎨᎲ ᎤᎷᏗ,’Ꭱ ᏥᎨᎲ flat-bed truck, ’50 model ᎤᎲ Ꭱ-rough ᎠᏦᏙᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᏌᎵ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᏚ ᎠᏃᏎᎲ ᎤᎾ,ᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᎤᏂᎧᎲ ᏳᏆᎷᏓ,’Ꮫ ᎨᎲ ᏳᏪᎾ, ᎠᎯᎸᏍᏗ, *ᎯᎢ* ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᎲ plane ᏄᏍᏛ ᏯᏂᏍᏆᎾᎵ’Ꮕ, ᎨᎲ truck-Ꭲ ᏳᎾ,ᏦᏓ, ᏙᏣᏓᏩᏛᎯᏙᎲ ᎠᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ, ᏴᏫ ᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎯᎢ ᎪᎯ, ᏥᎩ, Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᏯᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ, ᎦᏛᏏᏙᎲ ᎡᏠᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏏᎵ, - ᏏᎵ, ᏚᏙᎥ ᎠᎵᏥ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᎢᎿ ᎠᏩᏛᏒ ᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ … Decatur ᎮᎾ, ᏚᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎠᎵᏥ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏪᏥ’Ꮕ, ᎠᎨᏳᏣ, ᏗᏗ ᎠᏃᏎᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ Lucinda. ᏦᎢ ᎨᎲ ᏳᎾᏂ’ᎢᏌ, ᏏᎵ, ᏙᏍᏓᏗᏗᏍᎪ ᎨᎲ living room-Ꭲ ᏂᎬᏃ *ᎯᎢ* ᏄᏍᏛ ᎦᏌᎾᎵ, ᏗᏰᎦᏟ, ᏧᏬᏢᏗ … “Ꭷ” ᎠᏬᏎᎰ ᎨᎲ “ᎭᏗᏗ!” ᏯᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᏦᎢ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᏰᎢ,ᏍᏗᎲ ᎠᏪᏲᎲᏍᎬ … ᏯᏮᏁ,Ꮧ … ᏛᏩᏨᏍᏔᎾ, ᎦᎵ,ᏉᎩ, Ꮣ’ᎢᎾ, ᏗᏰᎦᏟ, ᎠᏮᏌ, ᏗᏬᏢᏔᏅ … ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏪᏲᎲᏍᎬ ᎠᏩᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ “ᎢᏳ -- ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏣᏓᎵ,Ꭼ, ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅᎾ, ᏱᎩ, ᎢᏳᏍᏗᏭ ᏥᎩ, ᎯᎦ,ᏔᎭ ᎨᎲ ᏣᏰᏫ,ᏒᏗ ᏣᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ Ꮭ ᎠᎪᎾ, ᏱᏂ,ᏓᏣᎵ,-- ᏱᏕᏣᏨᏱ,ᏍᏗ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏱᏙᏣ,ᎩᏯ, ᎠᎬᏱ ᏱᏙᎭᎦᎴᎾ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ,” ᎠᏬᏎᎲ “Ꮭ ᎠᏎ ᎩᎶ Ꭿ-Ꭿ-ᎯᏯ,ᏦᏎᏙᏗᏭ, ᏱᎩ, ᏱᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏱᏣᏛᏁ,Ꮧ” ᎬᏪᏲᏅ …
segments.transliteration: Every weekend, sgi notsadvnehv dotsadawadvhidohv … dominoes’le yigi, tsidanelohvsgo gehv daniquayohiho’le yigi, gehv ilvhiyu … svnoyi yigohida, yananvga, gehv uludi,’e tsigehv flat-bed truck, ’50 model uhv e-rough atsododi, tsigehv usdayvhvsgi, sali, tsigehv tsudu anosehv una,dvhistanv unikahv yuqualuda,’dv gehv yuwena, ahilvsdi, *hii* nigali,sdihv plane nusdv yanisquanali’nv, gehv truck-i yuna,tsoda, dotsadawadvhidohv ana,dasdayvhvsgv, yvwi gehv nahiyu hii gohi, tsigi, tla gilo yadasdayvhvsgv, gadvsidohv etlogi, tsigehv sili, - sili, dudov alitsi, tsigehv usdayvhvsgi, ihna awadvsv dagilvwi,sdanehv … Decatur hena, dunilvwi,sdanehv alitsi, tsigehv uwetsi’nv, ageyutsa, didi anosehv tsigehv Lucinda. tsoi gehv yunani’isa, sili, dosdadidisgo gehv living room-i nigvno *hii* nusdv gasanali, diyegatli, tsuwotlvdi … “ka” awoseho gehv “hadidi!” yada, gehv tsoi, gehv agiyei,sdihv aweyohvsgv … yawvne,di … dvwatsvstana, gali,quogi, da’ina, diyegatli, awvsa, diwotlvtanv … etsi tsigehv aweyohvsgv awadasdayv,di “iyu -- ilvhiyu tsadali,gv, nuli,stanvna, yigi, iyusdiwu tsigi, higa,taha gehv tsayewi,svdi tsadasdayv,di tla agona, yini,datsali,-- yidetsatsvyi,sdi’le yigi, yidotsa,giya, agvyi yidohagalena,’le yigi,” awosehv “tla ase gilo hi-hi-hiya,tsosedodiwu, yigi, yitsanv,ta, yitsadvne,di” gvweyonv …
segments.translation: We were doing that every weekend, visiting each other. They would be playing dominoes or playing cards. Sitting there until midnight. The late, Ulud(i) had a ’50 model flatbed truck. It was a rough ride. His wife’s name was Sal(i). The boy they raised—Tsudu they called him. He would be looking out of the truck, driving by, this [gestures] would be happening, like it was a plane [his hand]. They would park it—if they rode in the truck. We were visiting each other. They cooked back then—nobody cooks nowadays—as I was growing up, my late aunt, Sil(i) was her name. She was Alits(i)’s wife. Then I grew up and I was working. They worked in Decatur, Alits(i) and his daughter, Didi—they called her Lucinda. When they would leave at three o’clock, then Sil(i) and I would get up. And in the living room, there hanging on the ceiling was where she made quilts. “Kam,” she’d say to me. “Get up!” she’d say. She’d wake me up at three am. She was teaching me how to sew quilts. When I got married, I had seven quilts that I had made myself. My mom was teaching me to cook. “If you don’t ever get married, at least you’ll know how to sew and cook, so you won’t be starving. Or you might get married, and she might die before you. Or if you get divorced, you will not have to bother anyone. You would know how to take care of yourself,” that’s what they taught me.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You learned.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎢᏳᏍᏗᏭ, ᏥᎩ, ᏱᏥ-ᏱᏥ-ᏱᏥᏰᏫ, ᏃᏭᎴ Ᏹ’ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᎦ, ᎯᎢ ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ, ᎠᏮᏌ, ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᎲᏭ ᎦᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ, … ᎤᏒᎯ’Ꮕ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏄᎾ, ᏓᎩᏁ’ᎠᎸᎲ ᎠᏫ, ᎭᏫᏯ, ᎠᏮᏂᏍᏔᏅ ᎦᏚ’ᎢᏅ, ᏓᎩ,ᏒᏂ,ᏔᏅ ‘Ꮳ,ᎦᏍᏗ -- ‘Ꮳ,ᎦᏍᏗ’Ꮫ ᎠᏩᏓᏍᏓᏴᏅ
segments.transliteration: iyusdiwu, tsigi, yitsi-yitsi-yitsiyewi, nowule yi’adasdayvhvga, hii nowu tsigi, awvsa, nigali,sdihvwu gadasdayvhvsgv, … usvhi’nv, tsigehv nuna, dagine’alvhv awi, hawiya, awvnistanv gadu’inv, dagi,svni,tanv ‘tsa,gasdi -- ‘tsa,gasdi’dv awadasdayvnv
segments.translation: I can sew anything, and cook. Now, I’m by myself, I just cook what I want. Last night, I peeled potatoes and cooked deer meat. And made fried bread. I really cooked a good meal.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: What did you say? Ahwf(i)?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: uh-huh.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Yeah, Ahf.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Ahf – ahwi.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s how they say ahwi in Bell. “Ahf.”

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: That ‘f’ sound. “Ahw(i)” is what we say. Or “Ahawhi”

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: And we say “Ahw(i).”

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: “Ahw(i)” is what we say. Or “Ahawhi”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s what they say, where I’m from. “Ahawi.”

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Wow. That’s where you learned it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: (laughter)

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: XXX

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᏣᏃᎮᏍᎬ … ᏥᏕᎦᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᏕᏍᏓᏛᏏᏗᏒ’Ꮥ … ᎠᏴ,’Ᏺ ᏣᏩᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᎠᏩᏕᎳᎰᏌ, ᏴᏓᎾ, ᎪᎨᏱ ᏱᎩ, ᏙᏣᏓᏩᏛᎯᏙᎲ ᏔᎵᎭ ᏦᎢᎭ ᎢᎦ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, Ꮼ-Ꮼ-Ꮼ-Ꮼ-ᏬᏤᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎩᏙ’Ꮓ ᏙᏥᏩᏛᎯᏙᎲ ᏃᏭᎴ’Ꮓ ᏥᎦᏥᏲᏎᎰ “ᎮᏍᏗ, ᏯᎾ,ᏓᏓᎩ,ᏍᎨ ᎾᎥᎢ ᏴᏫ, (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎤᏂᎸᏉ,Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏩᏛᎯᏓᏍᏗ”
segments.transliteration: na’e tsanohesgv … tsidegadvsidisv desdadvsidisv’de … ayv,’yo tsawadvsidisv awadelahosa, yvdana, gogeyi yigi, dotsadawadvhidohv taliha tsoiha iga,’le yigi, wo-wo-wo-wo-wotseda, tsigehv etsi tsigehv vgido’no dotsiwadvhidohv nowule’no tsigatsiyoseho “hesdi, yana,dadagi,sge navi yvwi, (uyetsi,sgv) unilvquo,dv tsigehv dina,dawadvhidasdi”
segments.translation: What you were talking about, when we all were growing up. Or, when you all were growing up. When I was growing up, I realized that every spring we went and visited. We would go for two or three days. Mom, my sister, and I would go visiting. Now I tell them, “Back then, people didn’t get tired of each other.” [laughs] “They liked to visit one another.”

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏗᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᎢᎦᏓ, ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏍᏭ ᏗᎧᏅᏑᎳ, ᎨᎮ
segments.transliteration: digali,tsode igada, tsanv,ta, swu dikanvsula, gehe
segments.translation: Some of the houses, you know, only had one room.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah!

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Floor-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, ᏓᏰᏍᏓᎣ ᏂᎬ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏂᎬ ᏙᏥᎳ,ᎨᏲ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏴ, ᎣᏣᏝᏅᏝ ᎡᎳᏗ, ᏙᏥᏂ,ᏝᎥ feather bed/ feather mattress.
segments.transliteration: Floor-i’nv, dayesdao nigv diniyotli nigv dotsila,geyo gehv ayv, otsatlanvtla eladi, dotsini,tlav feather bed/ feather mattress.
segments.translation: On the floor we had mats to sleep on. We were just laid out all over, when we stayed overnight somewhere. Feather bed/feather mattress.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s right.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᏌᏭ ᎠᏴᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ, ᏅᎩ, ᏱᏚᏂᏂᏝ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏦᎢ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ,
segments.transliteration: na squu sawu ayvsdi yigi, nvgi, yiduninitla, tsigehv tsoi’le yigi,
segments.translation: And that one room house, they would even have four or three beds.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏂᏥᎦ,ᏙᎲᏒ ᏱᎩ, ᎠᏴ ᏗᏩᏛᏒ ᎤᎾᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᏗᏢ, ᎦᏓ,-ᎦᏓ,-ᎦᏓ,-ᎦᏓ’ᏭᎡ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᏓᏭ ᎮᏍᏗ, ᏗᏯᏖᎾ, ᏱᏗᎦᎾᎴ ᎦᏓᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ ᎪᎳ, ᏳᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴᎾ, ᎠᏓ, ᏗᎪᏙᏗ, ᏳᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴᎾ, ᎤᎦᎾᏩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᏙᎯ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᎢᎦᏓ, ᏣᏂᏅᏒᏍᎬ ᏣᏂᏅᏁᎲ ᏞᎦ,
segments.transliteration: tla yawanv,ta, sgi yusdi, nitsiga,dohvsv yigi, ayv diwadvsv unadasdayv,di ditlv, gada,-gada,-gada,-gada’wue tsigehv gadawu hesdi, diyatena, yidiganale gadawu tsigehv nowu gola, yuna,dasdayvna, ada, digododi, yuna,dasdayvna, uganawa, tsigehv gadohi, nowule igada, tsaninvsvsgv tsaninvnehv tlega,
segments.translation: I don’t know if you all have had it, where I grew up in the kitchen, it was just the ground. There weren’t any boards there. It was just dirt. Then, when they would cook, the ground would get really warm. Some of them were laying down there, or sitting there for a little while.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It was hard.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, it was hard.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎦᏅᏓᏗ ᎾᎥ ᏣᏂᏁᎸ ᏴᏫ, ᏍᎩᎾ wood--ᎦᏓᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ganvdadi nav tsaninelv yvwi, sgina wood--gadawu tsigehv
segments.translation: I remember people living by us—their floor was dirt.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᎭᏛ -- ᎣᏂ ᎠᏩᏛᏒ Ꮭ-Ꮭ ᎠᎩᎪᎲ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎩᎳ, ᎤᏍᏛ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎦᏁᎸ ᏑᏓᎴᎩ, ᏱᏂ,ᏥᏫ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎦᏥᏪᏎᎰ ᎪᎯ, ᏥᎩ, ᏗᎬᎩᎵᏏ ᏥᎩ, ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ, “ᏍᎩᏪᏍᏗ, ᏃᏭ ᎢᏣᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᎬᏃᏌᏍᏗ ᎢᏨ,ᏙᏗ” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv squu hadv -- oni awadvsv tla-tla agigohv yigehe gila, usdv nusdv ganelv sudalegi, yini,tsiwi, gehv sgina, gatsiweseho gohi, tsigi, digvgilisi tsigi, diniyotli, anigeyutsa, “sgiwesdi, nowu itsadelo,quasdi na gvnosasdi itsv,dodi” gatsiyohehv
segments.translation: Me too. I grew up later, I didn’t see that kind of house. I’ll tell you one thing. That’s what I tell my granddaughters today, “Y’all are gonna have to learn to use a broom.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah. Yeah, ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᎤᏓᏁᏟᏴᏌ, ᎮᎾ, ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎩ, ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏥᏓᏗᎲ ᎠᏓᎨᏳ,Ꮧ, ᎡᎲ ᎬᏃᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᏓᎨᏳ,Ꮧ, ᏃᏭ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎩ, Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᎤᏟᏂᎩᏓ, ᏰᏙᎯ, ᎠᏓᎨᏳ,Ꮧ,
segments.transliteration: Yeah. Yeah, doyu’dv udanetliyvsa, hena, gohiyv tsigi, nahiyu tsigesv tsidadihv adageyu,di, ehv gvnodi, gehv adageyu,di, nowu sgina, gohiyv tsigi, tla sgi iga utlinigida, yedohi, adageyu,di,
segments.translation: Yeah, it really has changed. Back then, there was love around. Love was alive. Nowadays, love is not as strong as it was.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Also, everything that was. When I grew up…

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꭱ lanolium ᏓᏰᏍᏓᎥ ᎨᎲ ᎡᎵᏭ front door ᏱᏣᏴᏍᏔᏅ ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎦᏅᏅ ᎨᎲ ᎤᎵ,ᏒᏃᏅ ᎨᎲ ᎤᎵ,ᏑᏫᏒ ᎤᏨᏏᏰᎥ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ, ᎤᏓᏅᎦᎸᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏦᎢᎭ’Ꮫ ᏅᎩᎭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏓᏅᏃᏌᏍᎬ ᏃᏭᎴ mop ᎾᏅᏁᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎤᏪᏘ, ᎨᎲ faded out ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎣᏍᏛ from one bedroom to the living room, to the kitchen, ᎣᏍᏛ’Ꮂ ᏧᏍᏗ ᏕᎦᏅᏅ Ꮒ’ᎥᏩ,ᏍᏛ ᎠᏂᏴᏫ, ᎤᎾ,ᏨᏏᏰᎥ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎤᏓᏅᎦᎸᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎰ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎪᎯ, ᏥᎩ, “Ꮭ ᏱᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏄᏍᏛ … ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎠᏕᏗ” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎰ ᎯᎢ ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ, carpet ᏂᎬ ᏕᏥᏰᏍᏓᎥ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏍᏊ Ꮭ-Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏯᏂᎦ,ᏔᎭ, ᎤᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, Last weekend, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ, ᎠᎨᏳᏣ, ᏫᏥᏯᏅᎲ “ᏖᏂ!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Melissa – Sissy” ᏥᏲᏎᎰ ᎠᏪᏥ, ᎠᎨᏳᏣ, “ᏫᏓᏥᏯᏘᎾᏫᏛᎯ, Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ, ᎠᏓᏁᎸ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ -- “ᎥᎥ” [ᎤᏛᏅ] … Ꮶ’ᎠᏚ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, … “Come with me!” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “We’re gonna learn to cook today,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎠᏴ, ᏱᏓᏍᎩ,ᏍᏓᏩᏛᏌ, ᎠᏴ,-ᎠᏴ, ᏓᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴᏂ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Okay, Papa,” [ᎤᏛᏅ] ᎣᎩᎾᏂᎩᏒ ᎤᏙᏓᏩᏓ,’Ꮫ Ꮩ--ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮧ, ᎣᎩᏂᏰᎸᏒ apron-Ꭲ ᎾᏮᏅ ᎠᏩᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ, ᎢᏏ’Ꮕ, ᎣᎩᎾᎵ,ᎪᏛ--ᎣᎩᏂᎵ,ᎨᏲᎥ’Ꮫ ᎣᎩᏂ,--ᎣᎩᏂᏍᏆᏛ ᎣᏍᏓᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ, “Ꭷ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Ꮭ Ᏹ’ᎠᎭᎵ,ᏍᏛᏡᎦ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “You ain’t got time,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎯᏅᎦᎵᎲ ᎣᏂ, -- what we made dirty,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᏂᏣᏛᏁ,Ꮧ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, you ain’t supposed to walk away.” ᏒᏃᏱ Ꮻ-ᏩᏟᎢᎶᏢ ᏦᎩᏅᎨᏩ,Ꮜ, next day, Ꮟ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᏍᏗ dishes’ᎢᏅ, Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ … ᏁᎳᎩ, ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ, ᎨᎲ dishes, they-they did it. ᎠᏂᏅᎦᎸᎲᏍᎬ ᏳᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴᏂ,’Ꮕ ᏳᎵ,ᏘᏴ ᎠᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᏗ, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ table-Ꭲ ᎠᏐᏈᏠ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏁᎩ’Ꮕ, ᏗᎬᎯᏓ, ᏗᎩᏍᎬ ᏯᏂᏍᏚᎲᎦ, -- ᏯᏂᏢᎦ, ᎨᎲ ᎦᏚ ᎩᎶ ᏳᎷᏣ, ᎠᏝᎲᏍᎪ ᏒᏃᏱ’Ꮽ, ᏱᎩ, Butch Eagle’Ꭱ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏥᏰᏣᏍᏔᏅ ᎤᏴᏍᏕᏗ, ᎤᎷᏨ ᏲᎩᎾᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᏃᏅ ᎡᏥ ᏗᎬᏗᏰᏔᏅ ᎩᏟ,--ᎩᏟ, ᏗᎨᏠ;ᏍᏙᏗ, ᏏᏈ’Ꮕ, ᏗᎨᏠ;ᏍᏙᏗ, ᎠᏂᏟᏍᏗᎰ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎾᎵ,ᏑᏱᎲ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, they couldn’t afford feed. ᏗᎬᏗᏰᏔᏅ ᎠᏁᏠ;ᏍᏗᎲ ᎨᎲ ᏏᏆ, ᎩᏟ’Ꮕ, baking pan ᎠᏝᎰ ᎤᎾ ᎦᎴᏍᎬ ᎦᏅᎦᎵᏍᎬ plates. Butch-ᎢᏅ, ᎤᏴᏍᏕᏗ, ᎤᎷᏨ ᏒᏃᏱ ᏫᏚᏃᏴᏟ,ᏍᏔᏅ’Ꮫ ᎤᎾ kitchen-Ꭲ ᎤᎩᏨᏓ, ᏑᎾᎴ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏗᎬᏗᏰᏔᏅ ᎠᏝᎲ ᎠᏰᏟ, ᎤᎪᎳ, ᎨᎲ “Butch-Ꭲ” ᎠᏗᎲ “ᎾᏅᎭ ᏣᏝᎲ ‘Ꮩ ᎲᎩ?” ᎠᎪᏎᎸ “Boy, ᏙᏳ ᎤᏖᏗ, (…)” ᏗᎬᏗᏰᏔᏅ ‘ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᎤᏓᏗᏔᎡᎸ ᎤᏴᏍᏕᏗ,

yuwaga,da, danvnosasgv nowule mop nanvnehv asenv, uweti, gehv faded out yuli,stanv osdv from one bedroom to the living room, to the kitchen, osdv’hv tsusdi deganvnv ni’vwa,sdv aniyvwi, una,tsvsiyev oginanigisv udodawada,’dv do--uwoli,di, oginiyelvsv apron-i nawvnv awadasdayv,di, isi’nv, oginali,godv--oginili,geyov’dv ogini,--oginisquadv osdadasdayvhvsgv, “ka” tsiyohelv “tla yi’ahali,sdvtluga,” nigohilv table-i asoquitlo gehv unegi’nv, digvhida, digisgv yanisduhvga, -- yanitlvga, gehv gadu gilo yulutsa, atlahvsgo svnoyi’wu, yigi, Butch Eagle’e sawu yuwaga,da, tsiyetsastanv uyvsdedi, ulutsv yoginali,sdayvnonv etsi digvdiyetanv gitli,--gitli, digetlo;sdodi, siqui’nv, digetlo;sdodi, anitlisdiho gehv anali,suyihv tsanv,ta, they couldn’t afford feed. digvdiyetanv anetlo;sdihv gehv siqua, gitli’nv, baking pan atlaho una galesgv ganvgalisgv plates. Butch-inv, uyvsdedi, ulutsv svnoyi widunoyvtli,stanv’dv una kitchen-i ugitsvda, sunale sginana digvdiyetanv atlahv ayetli, ugola, gehv “Butch-i” adihv “nanvha tsatlahv ‘do hvgi?” agoselv “Boy, doyu utedi, (…)” digvdiyetanv ‘sgasdi udaditaelv uyvsdedi,
segments.translation: Linoleum covered the floor. When you went in the front door, it was just like a little trail. All the color faded out where they walked. But it was clean. They would sweep it three or four times, and then they’d mop it. But it was old and faded out. It was good, though. From the bedroom to the living room to the kitchen, it was good. There were little trails where people walked. That’s what I was telling the kids. “It’s different now. You don’t know what it was like. That’s how life was,” I tell them. Today, they have carpets all over and they don’t know how to cook. Last weekend, I went and got my granddaughter. “Tammy,” I said. Melissa—I call her Sissy—my daughter, “I’m taking this girl home with me.” “Alright,” [Sissy said]. She’s 13 years old. “Come with me,” I said. “You’re going to learn to cook today,” I told her. “If you go with me, you’re going to cook,” I said. “Okay, Papa,” [Tammy said]. All day, we laughed around, I had an apron on. We had flour all over the place. After we got done cooking, “Kam,” [get up] I said. “You can’t sit down yet. You ain’t got time. You gotta clean what we made dirty,” I told her. “That’s what you need to do. You ain’t supposed to walk away.” It’ll be midnight and we forgot about it. Next day, it’ll still be the same. There was never dirty dishes. They always cleaned. When they cooked, what was leftover, they left it on the table and covered it with a white cloth. If somebody came, the food was on the table even if it was midnight. One time I laughed at Butch Eagle, he showed up drunk. When we got through eating, and washed dishes, we would gather the food scraps to feed the dogs and pigs with. Cause they couldn’t afford feed. They just fed them food scraps. There was a big pan sitting there for cleaning the plates off into. Butch showed up drunk at midnight. He went into the kitchen right away. In the morning, there was only a little bit of those food scraps on the table. “Butch, that food that was sitting here, what’d you do with it?” they asked him. “Boy, that was good!” he said. He ate the food scraps. He was too drunk.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Gah! ᎤᏠᏱ--ᎤᏠᏱ ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎡᎵᏏ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᏬᏤᏙᎲ … ᏔᎵᏁ ᎣᏍᏓᏝᏅᏢ Ꭱ-Ꭱ-ᎡᎵᏏ, ᎤᏪᏥ, ᎠᏧᏣ, ᏧᎵ ᏗᏓᏂ,ᏘᏃᎲ ᎤᏠᏱᏭ, ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎤᏒ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏒᏃᏱ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏧᏂᎷᏨ ᏧᎾ,ᏚᎩᏓ’Ꮫ Yeah, ᎠᏥᏬᎾ,ᏗᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᎠᏧᏣ, “ᏥᎬᏲᏎᎲ’Ꮫ ‘Ꮭ--ᎮᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩ ᎿᏛᏁᎮᏍᏗ, ᏣᏗᏔᎯᏙᎰ!’” ᏣᏓ, ᏃᏭ ᎤᎾᎵ ᎾᎥᎢ ᏗᎦᏙᎬ, … Ꮎ ᎦᏚ ᏩᏞᏍᎬ, ᎠᎢ ᏂᎬᏁᎲ ᎠᎩᏍᎬ “Boy!” ᎵᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᏥᏚᏙᎥ ᎡᎵᏏ, ᏥᎨᎲ “ᎵᏗ, ᏙᏳ’Ꭱ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎰᏢᎾ, soup!” – “ᎣᏍᏓ’Ꭹ? ᎭᏢ ᎯᏁᎩ?” – “ᎠᎭᏂ!” ᎾᏃ ᏥᎬᏗᏰᏔᏅ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎠᏗᏔᏍᎬ (…) ᏃᏭᏃ ᏫᏚᎩ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᏃᏭᎴᏃ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥᏍᎬ) ᎠᎢ ᏗᏢ, ᏧᏃᏴᎬ ᏚᎩ,ᏍᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: Gah! utloyi--utloyi tsinuli,stanv elisi, tsigehv yudaha elisi tsiwotsedohv … taline osdatlanvtlv e-e-elisi, uwetsi, atsutsa, tsuli didani,tinohv utloyiwu, sawu yuwaga,da, usv tsigehv svnoyi yusdi, tsunilutsv tsuna,dugida’dv Yeah, atsiwona,disgv na atsutsa, “tsigvyosehv’dv ‘tla--hesdi, sgi hnadvnehesdi, tsaditahidoho!’” tsada, nowu unali navi digadogv, … na gadu watlesgv, ai nigvnehv agisgv “Boy!” lidi, hena, tsidudov elisi, tsigehv “lidi, doyu’e osda, hotlvna, soup!” – “osda’gi? hatlv hinegi?” – “ahani!” nano tsigvdiyetanv (uniyetsi,sgv) aditasgv (…) nowuno widugi,stanv nowuleno (uniyetsisgv) ai ditlv, tsunoyvgv dugi,sdihv
segments.translation: Gah! The same thing happened at my grandma’s. We used to go to my grandma’s. My second cousin, my grandma’s son, he used to bring his friends. They showed up drunk about midnight and Grandma started in on him, “I told you not to be doing that, drinking around.” One of his friends was standing there, he was picking up the bread and eating it. “Boy! --“ My grandmother’s name was Lid(i). “-- Boy, Lid(i) you sure make good soup!” “Is it really good?” she said. “Where are you getting it?” she asked. “Right here!” he said. And it was the food scraps sitting on the table. [laughter] He was eating it. And then he threw up. [laughter] You could really hear him throwing up!

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: They were really goofy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They really are goofy. Yeah, you can really do crazy things if you are drinking all the time.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏅᎩᎭ ‘ᎸᏢ ᎾᏕᏘᏱ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, ᎨᏥᏩ,ᏛᎯᏓᏍᏗ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎠᏴ, ᎠᏩᏛᏒ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎳ, ᎨᏥᏩ,ᏛᎯᏙᎰ ᎨᎲ … ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮫ ᎠᏆ,ᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎤᎾᏅ,Ꮫ … ᎯᎢ’Ꮕ, ᏣᎩᎷᏨ ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏍᏚᏗ Ꮒ,ᏗᏩᏂᎩᏓ, ᎨᏥᏩ,ᏛᎯᏙᎸ … Ꭱ-Ꭱ-ᎡᎵᏏ, ᎡᏚᏚ ᏚᏃᏢ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ’Ꮕ, ᏅᎩ, ᎯᏍᎩ, ᏑᏓᎵ, ᏧᎾ,ᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎠᎾᏝᏱᏙᎲ ᏲᏁᎦᎭ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ Ꮭ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏯᏂ--ᏯᏃᎵ,Ꭼ Ꮭ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏯᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎡᎵᏏ ᎡᏚᏚ ᏚᏃᏢ ᎠᎭᏂ, Ꮭ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏯᏂᏬᏂᎲ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᎲ ᎬᏩᎵ,Ꮸ ᎤᏃᏟᏍᏗ ᎾᏂᏪᏍᎬ Ꮷ-Ꮷ-ᏧᏂᎵᏏ, ᏧᏂᎵᏏ, ᎬᏩᎵ,Ꮸ ᎡᏚᏚ, ᎡᎵᏏ’Ꮕ, ᎤᏃᏟᏗ ᎾᏂᏪᎲ ᏙᏳ, ᎤᏲᏝ, ᎠᎩᏰᎸᎲ … ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᎢᎦ ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᎢᎩᏲᎱᏎᎸ … Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᎩᎶ ᏃᏭ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᏱᏗᎨᏲᎲᎦ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ, ‘Ᏺ ᎠᏲᏁᎦᎭ ᏫᏛᏝᏃᎮᏔᏂ, ᎠᏲᏟ,
segments.transliteration: nvgiha ‘lvtlv nadetiyi tsigehv anigayvla, hena, agilvquo,di, getsiwa,dvhidasdi nigohilv ayv, awadvsv anigayvla, getsiwa,dvhidoho gehv … agilvquo,dv aqua,dvdasdodi yusdi, unanv,dv … hii’nv, tsagilutsv tsuna,dasdudi ni,diwanigida, getsiwa,dvhidolv … e-e-elisi, edudu dunotlv diniyotli’nv, nvgi, hisgi, sudali, tsuna,detiyvda, anatlayidohv yonegaha aniwonisgv tla tsalagi, yani--yanoli,gv tla tsalagi, yaniwonisgv elisi edudu dunotlv ahani, tla yonega, yaniwonihv tsalagiha aniwonihv gvwali,tsv unotlisdi naniwesgv tsu-tsu-tsunilisi, tsunilisi, gvwali,tsv edudu, elisi’nv, unotlidi naniwehv doyu, uyotla, agiyelvhv … sgi hena, iga gayu,la, igiyohuselv … tla hena, gilo nowu, atsalagi, yidigeyohvga, tsalagi, gawonisgv, ‘yo ayonegaha widvtlanohetani, ayotli,
segments.translation: I guess about four years ago, I like to visit the elders. That’s how I grew up, we visited the elders all the time. I like to listen to what they knew. When I got back here, from prison, I went to visit them. My grandma and grandpa was sitting there and there were children about four, five, or six years old, they were running around. They were speaking all in English. They didn’t understand Cherokee, or speak it. My grandparents were sitting over here and they weren’t speaking English. They were speaking all in Cherokee. The kids couldn’t understand them. And then the kids were talking in English so the grandparents couldn’t understand them. I felt bad about that. We’ve already lost that much. There’s nobody teaching them Cherokee. A person that speaks Cherokee is going to talk English to the kids.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᏣᏩᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏃᏥ--ᏂᎦᏓ, ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ, ᎨᎲ ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏦᎦᏛᏒ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏦᎦᎵ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ’ᏭᏛ ᎣᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayv, hena, tsawadvsidisv atsalagiha notsi--nigada, otsiwonisgv, gehv etsulaha diniyotli, tsogadvsv nowule tsogali squu atsalagiha’wudv otsiwonisgv, tsigehv
segments.translation: Me, when I was growing up, we all spoke Cherokee. Even my friends, we all spoke Cherokee.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ’Ꮽ ᎯᏬᏂᏍᎬ, ᏱᎨᎮᏍᏗ, Boy, Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏔᏅ ᏓᏦᏍᏓᏁᎵ, Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮧ, Ꮵ-ᏥᏃᎮᏍᎪ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏗ, ᏱᎾᎲᎦ, ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎬᏗ, ᏯᎯᏬᏂᎯ, Ꮭ-Ꮭ-Ꮭ-Ꮭ-Ꮭ ᎾᎥ’Ꮽ, ᏱᎬᏂ,ᏍᏗ ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮧ ᎨᎲ “ᏯᏩᏚᎵ, ᎮᎾ, ᎢᏣᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᏗ ᏂᏥᏪᏍᎬ--ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏂᏥᏪᏍᎬ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏗ,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎰ “ᏱᏣᏅ,Ꮫ ᏱᏦᎵ,ᏍᏓᏌ, ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎠᏴᏫᏯ’Ꮽ ‘Ᏺ ᎢᎦ ᏧᏔᎾ, ᎡᏆ ᏧᏬᎵ,ᏓᏁ” ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎰ
segments.transliteration: atsalagiha’wu hiwonisgv, yigehesdi, Boy, tsi,quistanv datsosdaneli, tla hena, uwoli,di, tsi-tsinohesgo gohu,sdi, tsalagi, gvdi, yinahvga, yonega, gvdi, yahiwonihi, tla-tla-tla-tla-tla nav’wu, yigvni,sdi uwoli,di gehv “yawaduli, hena, itsadelo;quasdi nitsiwesgv--yusdi, nitsiwesgv tsalagi, gvdi,” gatsiyoheho “yitsanv,dv yitsoli,sdasa, sgi hena, yusdi, ayvwiya’wu ‘yo iga tsutana, equa tsuwoli,dane” gatsiyoseho
segments.translation: If you are a Cherokee speaker, you’re going to hear funny things. The things you tell in Cherokee that are funny, if you tell it in English, it’s not. It don’t even come close to being funny in English. “I want you all to learn, so you can understand what I’m saying. If you all did, you will know that it’s funny, what we’re saying,” I tell them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎦᏥᏪᏎᎲ ᏑᎾᎴ ᏙᏣᏝᏃᎮᏛ ᏑᎾᎴ ᏥᎨᎲ … “ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎩ,” ᎢᏗᏣᎳᎩ “ᎮᏂ ᏥᎩ, ᎩᎶ ᏳᏭᎾᏍᏆᎶ ᏳᏭᏅᏥ ᏳᏪᏗᏰᏣᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ Ꮟ
segments.transliteration: na gatsiwesehv sunale dotsatlanohedv sunale tsigehv … “atsalagi, hena, tsigi,” iditsalagi “heni tsigi, gilo yuwunasqualo yuwunvtsi yuwediyetsasdi heni si
segments.translation: That’s what I was telling them this morning, we were talking, “Us Cherokee’s, if somebody stubbed their toe and fell down, we would still laugh at them.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: They won’t feel sorry for you.
[laughter]
[Everybody talking]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: If we told someone ‘stubbed their toe’, we will just laugh. [laughter]

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Ꮩ-ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮧ, ᎠᏰᎸᏍᏗ, ᏄᏓᎴᏒ ᏙᎲ? ᏅᏬᏔ ᎮᎾ, ᎣᏍᏕᎸ;ᏙᏗ,
segments.transliteration: do-doyu, hena nvwoti gehv uwoli,di, ayelvsdi, nudalesv dohv? nvwota hena, osdelv;dodi,
segments.translation: It’s medicine. Laughter it is really good medicine. It helps us.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏙᏳᎢ “that’s the best therapy” ᎠᎾ,ᏗᏍᎪ laughter/being happy, that makes—that gives you a long lifespan, ᎠᎾ,ᏗᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: doyui “that’s the best therapy” ana,disgo laughter/being happy, that makes—that gives you a long lifespan, ana,disgo
segments.translation: It is. “Laughter that’s the best therapy,” they say. Laughter, being happy, that makes, that gives you, a long lifespan, they say.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, … ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏪᏒ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎤᏔᎾᏯ ᎤᏛᏐᏅ … “ᏳᏁᎩ’Ꮫ ᏥᎩ,” ᏣᏗ, “ᏧᏍᏙᏒ Ꮎ ᎠᏥᏚᎩ, ᎤᏲ ᏳᏰᎵᏗᏌ,” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎠᏣᎳᎩ’Ꮕ, ᏱᎩ, ᏍᏊ ᎭᎳ ᎢᎦ, Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏗ, ᎠᏥᏚᎩ, Ꮟ’Ꮧ ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏏᏓᏍᏗ, (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) … ᏃᏭ’Ꭱ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏗ, … ᏣᏗᎲ ᎯᎾ “ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎤᏲ ᏳᏓᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎤᏦᏎᏓ, ᏳᏓᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏥᏗᏬᏂᎯ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏱᏭᏩᎨᏩ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏳᏓᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏃᏭ, ᎪᎯᏴ … ᏣᏅ,Ꮨ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎤᏠᏯᏍᏙ” ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎢᎦ ᎣᏏ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᏥᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: doyu, hena, … sgi tsinuwesv sawu yuwaga,da, utanaya udvsonv … “yunegi’dv tsigi,” tsadi, “tsusdosv na atsidugi, uyo yuyelidisa,” tsadihv “atsalagi’nv, yigi, squu hala iga, tsi,quisdi, atsidugi, si’di uyetsi,sidasdi, (uniyetsi,sgv) … nowu’e squu sgi nusdi, … tsadihv hina “ilvhiyu atsalagi, uyo yudanv,ta, utsoseda, yudanv,ta, gohu,sdi, tsidiwonihi, yusdi, yiwuwagewa, osda, yudanv,ta, nowu, gohiyv … tsanv,ti nvwoti utloyasdo” hesdi, iga osi atsalagi, tsigi, gawonihisdi,
segments.translation: Really. That’s what somebody said one time, an old man. “When a White person is in debt a lot, they will be worrying about it. And if it’s a Cherokee in debt, they will just be laughing around.” [laughter] Yeah, it’s that way. This guy was saying, “When a Cherokee is feeling bad, and if he was hearing Cherokees talking, after a while he will be laughing around and feeling good.” You know, like he said, laughter is medicine. Somebody that talks Cherokee real well, if they’re here.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Ed!

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Ed!

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Go ahead.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Ed, tell us a lie about something you’ve done. [laughter]

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: I don’t know anything.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏥᏚᏃᏎᏗ,’Ꮫ ᎭᏰᎵ,ᏍᏗ, ᏗᎾᎵᏗ,ᏗᏍᎪᎯ ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎲ ᎦᏚᎲ ᏧᎾ,ᏛᎯᏍᏗ ᏓᏂᏅ ᏣᎢᏒ’Ꭱ ᎾᏃᎵ,Ꭼ, ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ, “ᎾᏅᎲ ᏥᏓᏯᎢ” ᏧᎾ,ᏛᏅ “ᎩᎳ’ᏭᎢᏛ, ᏲᏥᏍᎪᏁᎳ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ,” ᏧᎾ,ᏛᏅ ᎾᎥ ᎤᎷᏨ “Hey!” ᏣᏓ, “Ꭷ! ᏂᎯᏃ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎢᏥᏍᎪᏌ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ’Ꮽ,” ᏧᏃᏎᎸ … “ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, Ꮭ ᏙᏳ, ᎢᎦ ᏯᏩᏝᏅᏓᏕ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎤᏲ ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏏ, ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᎮᎾ, ᏁᎲᎾ, ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗ” -- ᏭᎶᏒ ᏭᏕᎵᏨ -- ᎤᏲ ᎤᏂᏰᎸᏅ ᏧᎾ,ᏛᎯᏍᏗ, Boy, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏚᎾ,ᎴᏅ ᎠᏓᎾᏅ ᏭᏴᏢ ‘ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᏭᏂᎩᏒ ᎤᎾᎵ,ᏍᏛᏡᏅ ᎠᏂᎦ,ᏘᏴ ᎢᎤᎷᎯᏍᏗ … ᏣᎢᏒ ᎤᏂᏁᎴ … “ᎯᎢ ‘Ꮩ!?” ᎤᏛᏅ … “ᎢᏨᏍᏕᎸᎡᏗ,’Ꮫ Ꮎ ᎤᏲᏟ, Ꮒ,ᏣᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎸ Ꮳ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᏧᏲᎱᏒ” – “Hm! ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, Ꮭ ᏳᏲᎱᏌ, ᏗᎦ,ᏚᎴᏂ’Ꮽ, ᎤᏣᎠ,!” – “’ᎠᏲᎱ--ᎠᏲᎱᎩ’ ᏥᏂ,ᏍᎩᏪᏌ,!” –“ᏥᏥᏍᎪᏌ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ!” ᏥᏍᎩᏲᏌ,
segments.transliteration: tsidunosedi,’dv hayeli,sdi, dinalidi,disgohi tsana,dihv gaduhv tsuna,dvhisdi daninv tsaisv’e nanoli,gv, udvhisdi, “nanvhv tsidayai” tsuna,dvnv “gila’wuidv, yotsisgonela, gohu,sdi,” tsuna,dvnv nav ulutsv “Hey!” tsada, “ka! nihino gohu,sdi, itsisgosa, gohu,sdi’wu,” tsunoselv … “tsanv,ta, tla doyu, iga yawatlanvdade” udvnv “uyo nawali,sdasi, agi,sdayvhvsgi, hena, nehvna, nigali,sdi” -- wulosv wudelitsv -- uyo uniyelvnv tsuna,dvhisdi, Boy, nigada, duna,lenv adananv wuyvtlv ‘sgasdi wunigisv unali,sdvtlunv aniga,tiyv iuluhisdi … tsaisv uninele … “hii ‘do!?” udvnv … “itsvsdelvedi,’dv na uyotli, ni,tsali,sdanelv tsa,sdayvhvsgi, tsuyohusv” – “Hm! agi,sdayvhvsgi, tla yuyohusa, diga,duleni’wu, utsaa,!” – “’ayohu--ayohugi’ tsini,sgiwesa,!” –“tsitsisgosa, gohu,sdi!” tsisgiyosa,
segments.translation: There used to be old men sitting around in town trading knives, they said. There was one coming that they knew, “Look who’s coming,” they said. “He’s just going to start lying,” they said. He came over and said, “Hey!” “Go ahead and start telling us lies!” they told him. He said, “I don’t feel like doing that, I’m too sad because my wife just died.” He went on by and went away. Those old men felt bad. They stood up and went in the store real quick and got groceries for him. Then they sat down and waited for him to come back. They gave it to him, “What is this for?” he said. “We are helping you because your wife passed away,” they said. “Hmm! My wife didn’t die, she’s in the car.” “You told us she died!” they said. “Y’all said for me to lie to y’all!” he told them [laughter]
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᎦᏥᏃᏎᎲ ᎢᎸᏍᎩ, ᏄᏒ … ᏒᏃᏱ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᏗᏝᏃᎮᏗ ᎤᏃᏴᏏᏞ ᎥᎩᏙ “ᎠᏍᎦᏯ ‘Ꮲ ᎡᎯ,” ᏓᏳᏛᏅ “ᎤᏛᏐᏅ” … “ᎡᎵᏭ’Ꭸ ᏗᏍᏕᎾ?” – “Yeah!” ᏥᏲᏎᎸ “ᏱᏬᏍᏗᎷᎦ,’Ꮫ ᎤᎾ” ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, ᎣᎩᎾᏂᎩᏒ ᏬᎩᎷᏨ’Ꮓ … ᏬᎩᎷᏨ ᏃᏭ ᏬᎩᏂᏴᏢ ᏙᏳ ᏍᏊ ᎢᎾᎨ ᏗᎨᏎ ᎨᎲ ᏬᎩᏂᎷᏨ ᏚᏃᏢ ᏍᎩᏃ ᏭᏝᏃᎮᏢ ᎤᏙ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏭ’Ᏼ ᎤᏬᏢ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᏁᎲᎾ ᏥᎩ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏙᏳ, ᎡᏆ ᏙᏥᏬᏂᎲ … ᏣᏝᏃᎮᏍᎪ ᎪᎯ’Ꭱ ᎦᏏ, ᏧᏙᎢᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᏧᎦᎸᏗ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏛᏐᏅ ᎾᏅ ᎤᎾᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏗᏢ, ᎤᏬᏢ … ᎯᎢ’Ꮫ ᏌᎻ, ᏚᏙᎥ ᏌᎻ, ᎬᏅᎯᏓ, “ᎯᎢ’Ꮫ ᏌᎻ, ᎬᏅᎯᏓ,” ᎤᏃᎮᏢ ᏌᎻ, ᎬᏅᎯᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ “ᎠᏴ,’Ꮫ … ᏔᎵ, ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎬᏲᎱᏌ, ᏥᏯᏤᏓᏁᎸ” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏌᎻ, … Ꮎ ᎤᏛᏐᏅ ᎦᏏ, “Huh uh, ᏦᎢ’Ꮫ ᎨᎵ ᏥᎨᎲ” ᏣᎪᏎᎸ ᏧᏓᎧᏅ “ᎦᏙ’Ꭹ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ?” – “ᎭᏅ,ᏓᏗᎰᏍᎪ, Ꮎ ᏘᏂ, ᏥᎨᏣᎸ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ,?” ᏣᎪᏎᎸ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) … ᏃᏭ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏙᎦᏓᏩᏛᏗ ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏙᎦᏓᏩᏛᎲ … ᏗᎣᎩᎾᏂᎩᏌ, ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, “ᏙᎯᏳᎢ ᎤᏂᎷᎶᏣ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏙᎲ?” Man, ᏙᏳ ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮧ, ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv squu gatsinosehv ilvsgi, nusv … svnoyi adanelv ditlanohedi unoyvsitle vgido “asgaya ‘tlv ehi,” dayudvnv “udvsonv” … “eliwu’ge disdena?” – “Yeah!” tsiyoselv “yiwosdiluga,’dv una” agi,sdayvhvsgi, oginanigisv wogilutsv’no … wogilutsv nowu woginiyvtlv doyu squu inage digese gehv woginilutsv dunotlv sgino wutlanohetlv udo gehv sgina awu’yv uwotlv sgina agayvlige udvhistanv nehvna tsigi, nigada, doyu, equa dotsiwonihv … tsatlanohesgo gohi’e gasi, tsudoida, gehv tsugalvdi’nv, squu gehv udvsonv nanv unadvhistanv agvyi ditlv, uwotlv … hii’dv sami, dudov sami, gvnvhida, “hii’dv sami, gvnvhida,” unohetlv sami, gvnvhida, tsigehv “ayv,’dv … tali, yuwaga,da, gvyohusa, tsiyatsedanelv” udvnv sami, … na udvsonv gasi, “Huh uh, tsoi’dv geli tsigehv” tsagoselv tsudakanv “gado’gi usdi gehv?” – “hanv,dadihosgo, na tini, tsigetsalv sawu yuwaga,da,?” tsagoselv (uniyetsi,sgv) … nowu osda, dogadawadvdi nigada, dogadawadvhv … dioginanigisa, agi,sdayvhvsgi, “dohiyui unilulotsa sgina, dohv?” Man, doyu uwoli,di, tsigehv
segments.translation: I was telling them this the other day. Around midnight the phone rang, My sister said, “There’s an old man here. Could y’all come over here?” “Yeah, we’ll be there,” I told her. Me and my wife took off. When we got there, we went inside, and she lives way out in the woods. When we got there they were sitting there, and he said that was his sister. That old lady sitting nearby, the one that raised him. But she’d passed on. We were talking real sad, real heavy while we sat there. Gas(i) was his name. He was a jokester, too, he was an old man. And the one they raised was sitting in front, his name is Sam(i) Gvnvhid(a), Samuel Long. “This is Samuel Long,” he told a story about the late Sam(i) Gvnvhid(a). “They say that ‘you die twice’,” that old man, Gas(i). “Uh uh! I think it’s three times!” he said. He looked at him, “What was it? …Do you remember when you had lice?” [laughter] … We forgot about feeling bad. When we left, my wife said, “They sure are crazy.” Man, it was funny.

segments.text: ᎥᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ, ᎤᏄᏩ, ᏗᏟᎶᏍᏔᏅ Ꮳ,ᏍᏘᎬ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) … ᎤᏃᏍᏛ ᏗᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ,

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎥᎾ’ᏭᎨ ᎮᎰ? Ꮟ? Ed, ᏨᏥ ᏣᏙᏓ, ᎤᎾ,ᏕᏅ?
segments.transliteration: vna’wuge heho? si? Ed, tsvtsi tsadoda, una,denv?
segments.translation: You’re at where your parents used to live?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Have your parents already passed on, or are they still living?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: They’re gone,

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: yeah

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.text: … ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎠᏬᏝ, ᎠᎩᏙᏓ, ᏍᏊ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏧᏬᏠ… (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) … (…)
segments.transliteration: … ahani, awotla, agidoda, squu utloyi tsuwotlo… (uniyetsi,sgv) … (…)
segments.translation: I’m sitting here like my dad [laughter].

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How many siblings do you have?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Now it’s just me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It’s just you.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: How many of y’all altogether?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.text: ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ it’s just me and her. Jean. ᏔᎵ’Ꮽ,
segments.transliteration: doyu’dv it’s just me and her. Jean. tali’wu,
segments.translation: It’s just me and her, Jean. There were two of us.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You all spoke Cherokee?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Ain’t it. What was it like? Where did you go to school?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: I was listening to the elders talking.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Where’d you go to school?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: School. Where did you go?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Greasy.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Greasy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did you go to school at Marble? [Marble City Public School]

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Uh uh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Over at Greasy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Oh, yeah. ᎪᎣ … ᎯᎦ,ᏔᎮ’Ꭸ ᎦᏲᏟ, ᏳᏁᎦ, ᏣᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᏣᎴᏅᎲ?
segments.transliteration: Oh, yeah. goo … higa,tahe’ge gayotli, yunega, tsawonihisdi tsalenvhv?
segments.translation: Oh, yeah. Greasy. Did you know how to speak a little English when you started school?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So you didn’t have any problems speaking English?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: I don’t think so.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah. [laughs] What about you? Where did you go to school?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Bell.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Bell-Ꭲ ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ,’Ꭸ ᏳᏁᎦ, ᎯᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎨᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: Bell-i gayu,la,’ge yunega, hiwonisgv gehv tsadihv
segments.translation: Bell. And you said you already spoke English.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎥᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎦᏗ ᏑᏓᎵ,’Ꭱ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎩᎳ, ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᎩᏬᏂᏒ Stilwell-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, high school. ᏦᎢ’ᎸᏢ ᏱᏅᏓ, ᏓᏪ--ᏓᎩ--ᏓᏩᏕᎶ;ᏆᎥ’Ꮓ ᎡᏥ ᏥᏲᏎ--ᎡᏥ ᏥᏲᏎᎲ “Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ ᎠᏩᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᏗ Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏳᏰᎵ,Ꮧ,” ᏥᏲᏎᎸ “ᏙᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎵ’Ꮽ … ᏱᎬᏍᏕᎳ, ᎭᏈᏴᎲᏅ” ᏥᏲᏎᎸ ᏙᏳ, ᎠᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏥᏔᎩ, ᏕᏥᏂᏱᏍᎬ ᏓᎳᏚ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏥᏔᎩ, ᏥᏕᏥᏂᏴᎲ … ᎾᎩᏁᏏᏒ ᎠᏕᎳ, ᏗᏎᏍᏗ, ᎠᏰᏟ’Ᏼ ᏕᏥᏁᎲ ᎡᏥ
segments.transliteration: vsgi hena, tsigadi sudali,’e yawadetiyvda, gila, tsalagi, agiwonisv Stilwell-i’nv, high school. tsoi’lvtlv yinvda, dawe--dagi--dawadelo;quav’no etsi tsiyose--etsi tsiyosehv “tla yawaduli awadelo;quasdi tla gohu,sdi, yuyeli,di,” tsiyoselv “dodagilvwi,sdaneli’wu … yigvsdela, haquiyvhvnv” tsiyoselv doyu, awalenvhv dagilvwi,sdanehv tsitagi, detsiniyisgv daladu tsudetiyvda, tsitagi, tsidetsiniyvhv … naginesisv adela, disesdi, ayetli’yv detsinehv etsi
segments.translation: Yeah, like I said, I didn’t speak Cherokee until I was six years old. I went to Stilwell High School for about three months. And then I told my mom, “I don’t want to go to school. It’s no use. I’m just going to work and help you pay bills.” So I started working, catching chickens. I caught chickens for 12 years. When I got a paycheck, I would give half of it to my mom.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ … yeah, ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᏣᏩᏛᏏᏗᏒ … ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏍᎩᎦᏚ--ᏍᎩᎦᏚ’ᏛᎮ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ lumberyard-Ꭲ ᎥᎩᎾᏢᏅ … ᎬᏅᎯᏓ’ᏭᏛ ᏥᎩ, ᏥᏳ trailer—trailer ᎤᏂᏲᏢᏅ ᎾᏅ ᎦᎸᎳᏗ, ᎾᎥ ᏥᎨᏒ *ᎯᎢ* ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏗᎧᎾ,Ꮧ ᎾᏅ ᎦᏌᎾᎵ, ᎤᏂᏢ … plastic-ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ … ᏅᎩᎭ ᏃᏥᎥ ᎠᏂᏍᎦᏯ, ᎠᏴ, ᏥᏧᏣ’Ꮽ -- Boy! ᎤᏙᏓᏩᏓ, Ꮩ-ᏙᎦᎴᏅ … ᎤᎾ ᎣᏥᏬᎾ,ᏗᏍᎬ ᏃᏭᎴ “stack” ᏃᏨᏁᎲ ᎠᏂᏳᏁᎦ,’Ꭾ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏂᏐᎢ, ᏌᏭ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, … ᏚᏂᎬᏩᎵ,ᏔᏁ’Ꮓ ᏴᏛᎾ, “ᎯᎢ’Ꮓ ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎢᎩᏍᏓᏩᏗᏙᎯ, ᎪᎯᏴ’Ꮽ,Ꮫ ᏛᏂᎩᏏ,” ᎠᎾᏓ--ᏓᏙᏎᎲ “ᎭᎳᎦ ᏕᏂᎬᏩᎵ,Ꮣ?” … ᏌᏭ ᎤᏑᏴ “ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᎨᏒ ᎠᏬᎯᏳ ‘ᏙᏓᏩᏓ, ᏛᏰᏙᎳ,” Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏬᏢ ᏍᏊ lumberyard ᎤᏠᏱ ᏤᎵᏍᎨ Ꮭ ᎤᏙᏓᏩᏓ, ᏱᏓᎨᏙᎵ, ᎡᎵᎲ … ᏙᏳ’Ꭱ ᎤᏙᏓᏩᏓ, ᎠᏪᏙᎸ Boy! ᎤᏂᏍᏆᎾ,ᎪᏒ’Ꮫ … ᏍᎩᎦᏚ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᎠᏪᏙᎸ … Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏙᏳ, ᎠᏩᏓᎨᏓ, ᏱᎨᎮ ᎠᎩ--ᎠᏩᎴᏐᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ … ᎤᏓᎾᏅ’Ꮓ ᎠᏗᎲ “Boy,” ᎠᏬᏎᎸ “I didn’t think you was gonna last that long, Chief,” ᎠᏬᏎᎸ “I had to,” ᏥᏲᏎᎸ “’cause Mom chased me over here!” ᎠᏩᏛᏅ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) … “I’m going to pay you as much as I did these grown up guys,” ᎠᏬᏎᎸ … ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᏓᎩᏁᎸ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏍᏊ ᎤᎪᏛ ᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ … ᏅᎩ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᎠᏕᎳ ᎨᎵ ᏛᎩᏁᎸ Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᎤᎪᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, doyu’dv … yeah, doyu’dv hena, squu tsawadvsidisv … saquu yuwaga,da, sgigadu--sgigadu’dvhe yawadetiyvda, gehv lumberyard-i vginatlvnv … gvnvhida’wudv tsigi, tsiyu trailer—trailer uniyotlvnv nanv galvladi, nav tsigesv *hii* yusdi, yusdi, gehv dikana,di nanv gasanali, unitlv … plastic-yusdi, gehv … nvgiha notsiv anisgaya, ayv, tsitsutsa’wu -- Boy! udodawada, do-dogalenv … una otsiwona,disgv nowule “stack” notsvnehv aniyunega,’he gehv anisoi, sawu atsalagi, … dunigvwali,tane’no yvdvna, “hii’no atsutsa, igisdawadidohi, gohiyv’wu,dv dvnigisi,” anada--dadosehv “halaga denigvwali,da?” … sawu usuyv “ayv’dv gesv awohiyu ‘dodawada, dvyedola,” na squu uwotlv squu lumberyard utloyi tselisge tla udodawada, yidagedoli, elihv … doyu’e udodawada, awedolv Boy! unisquana,gosv’dv … sgigadu yawadetiyvda, gehv sgi yigohida, awedolv … tla squu doyu, awadageda, yigehe agi--awalesoda, hena, gehv nahiyu … udananv’no adihv “Boy,” awoselv “I didn’t think you was gonna last that long, Chief,” awoselv “I had to,” tsiyoselv “’cause Mom chased me over here!” awadvnv (uniyetsi,sgv) … “I’m going to pay you as much as I did these grown up guys,” awoselv … sgi iga daginelv eliwu squu ugodv gehv nahiyu … nvgi,sgohi, adela geli dvginelv na’dv ugodi, tsigehv nahiyu
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s true. When I was growing up, one time, I was about 16 years old. The lumber yard hired me on. There was a long trailer loaded with lumber. On top, back then, it used to look like this [gestures]. And on the roof, it was like plastic. There were four of us men. I was only a boy. We were there all day. We were, then we were, stacking them up. The others were White and there was one Cherokee. They made a bet. “That boy that is following us around, working with us. He’s going to leave soon,” they said. “How much do you want to bet?” There was one there, among them, that said, “No, I think he’s going to be here all day.” Even the one that owned the lumber yard was thinking the same. He thought I wasn’t going to be there all day. But I worked all day. And they were really surprised. I was only around 15 years old and I was there that long. I wasn’t that big back then, I was skinny. [laughs] The owner said, “Boy! I didn’t think you was gonna last that long, Chief,” he said. “I had to, cause Mom chased me over here!” I told him. [laughter] “I’m going to pay you as much as I did these grown up guys,” he told me. That’s how much he gave me, and it was $40, and that was probably a lot for back then.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏍᎪᎯ, ᎠᏕᎳ’Ꮽ, ᎤᎪᏓ, ᎾᎯᏳ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏥᎩ, ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᏍᎪᎯᏥ,Ꮚ ᎠᏕᎳ ᎤᏠᏱ’ᏭᏛ ᏍᎪᎯ, ᎠᏕᎳ ᎯᏲᏍᏔᏅ’Ꮫ it’s gone. ᎩᎳ’Ꮽ ᎤᏟᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: sgohi, adela’wu, ugoda, nahiyu nowu’nv, tsigi, etsulaha sgohitsi,quu adela utloyi’wudv sgohi, adela hiyostanv’dv it’s gone. gila’wu utlisdi,
segments.translation: Ten dollars was a lot back then. Nowadays, a $100 is just like $10 today. You can spend it up real quick.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏅ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᏮᎩᎷᏣ, ᎠᏰᏟ’Ꮓ ᏦᏍᎪᎯ, ᎠᏕᎳ, ᏕᏥᏁᎸ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ … “ᏍᎩᏍᎪ, ᎢᎦ ᎰᏢᎾ?” – “Yeah!” – “ᏍᏗ’Ꭸ Ꮟ ᏕᏣᏝ,?” – “ᎥᎥ…” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎠᏎᏅ,--ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎠᏩ--ᎠᏩᏍᏉᎵ,ᏓᏁᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᏩ--ᏓᏩᏝᏩᏛ ᏗᎩᏢ,Ꮧ ᏃᏭᎴ ᎾᎯᏳ’ᏛᏃ ᏒᎯᏳ ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ ᏧᏂᏓᏲᎯ,ᏍᏗ ᏗᏢ, ᎠᏪᏅᏒ ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ pop-Ꭲ’Ꮕ ᏫᎦᏗᏔᏍᎬ peanuts ᏫᏙᏥᎳᏍᎬ Ꮎ coke-Ꭲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏍᏊ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎥᏍᎩ ᏂᏣᏛᏁᎴ
segments.transliteration: nonv adanelv wvgilutsa, ayetli’no tsosgohi, adela, detsinelv etsi tsigehv … “sgisgo, iga hotlvna?” – “Yeah!” – “sdi’ge si detsatla,?” – “vv…” tsiyohelv (uyetsi,sgv) asenv,--asenv, awa--awasquoli,danelv sgina diwa--dawatlawadv digitlv,di nowule nahiyu’dvno svhiyu yinuli,stana, nowu’dv tsunidayohi,sdi ditlv, awenvsv nowu’dv pop-i’nv wigaditasgv peanuts widotsilasgv na coke-i tla yawanv,ta, squu ilvhiyu vsgi nitsadvnele
segments.translation: And then when I got back to the house, I gave $30 to my late mother. “Is that how much you made?” she said. “Yeah!” I said. “Do you still have some more?” she asked. “Yeah…” I told her. [laughs] She let me keep that money in my pocket. And then when the evening came, I went to the pool hall. And then, I was drinking pop and putting peanuts in it. It was a coke. I don’t know if you all have ever done that.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎥᎥ root beer—root beer’ᏛᏲ ᎨᎲ … root beer and peanuts.
segments.transliteration: vv root beer—root beer’dvyo gehv … root beer and peanuts.
segments.translation: It was root beer. Root beer and peanuts.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏕᏥᏢᏍᎪ-Ꭳ ᎦᏗᏍᏔᏍᎬ ᏕᏥᏓᏲᎯᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ’Ꮫ ᏗᏩᏛᏓ,’ᏛᏃ ᏥᎨᎵᎲ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) … ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, … ᏥᎵᎡᎵᏤᎲ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ “ᏩᏗᏓ! ᏗᏣᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎷᎦ!” ᎠᏬᏎᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ, Ꮭ ᏯᎩᎭ, ᏣᏩᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᏳᏓᎭ’Ꮫ ᎠᎩ,ᏓᎩ,ᏍᎪ ᎩᎶ ᎠᎩ,ᏘᏅᏍᏗᏍᏗ ᏗᎬᏂᎰ ᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗ “Guy awake?” – “Yeah, he’s awake!” – “Tell him to wake up! We gotta go to work!” ᏃᏭᎴ ᏗᏣᎢᏐᎢ “ᎩᎶ ᎡᏣᏯᏅᎯ ᏗᏣᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎴᏍᏗ!” … “Eh… ‘Ꮧ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ ᏗᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎴᏍᏗ” – “ᎠᏎ’Ꮫ ᏗᏣᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎴᏍᏗ!” … ᏃᏭᎴ ᏓᎿᏬᏍᏗ, Ꮣ-Ꮣ-ᏓᎩᎿᏬᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᏗᏰᎦᏟ, ᏙᎦᎾ,ᏏᏁᏍᎪ ᎠᎢ ᏗᎬᏁᎲ ᎥᏍᎩ’Ꮫ Ꮹ-ᏩᎩ,ᏓᎩ,ᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏥ ᎥᏍᎩ ᏱᏂ,ᏚᏮᏁᎳ, (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏃᏭᎴ ᏥᎾᏏᏁᏍᎬ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏙᎦᎾ,ᏏᏁᏍᎬ … ᏃᏭ ᎠᏎ’Ꮫ ᎠᏩᏗᏓ, ᎾᏮᏁᎸ’Ꮓ ᏳᏓᎭ’Ꮫ ᎡᏍᎦ, ᏥᏰᎵᏎᎲ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᏫᎦᎵᎡᎵᎪ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎩ, … ᎢᎦᏓ, ᎮᎾ, Ꮭ ᏙᏳ, ᏃᏭ, ᏱᏓᏂᏅᏫᏍᏗ ᏧᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ ᏃᏭ,
segments.transliteration: sgi’dv detsitlvsgo-o gadistasgv detsidayohihv osda’dv diwadvda,’dvno tsigelihv (uyetsi,sgv) … doyu, hena, … tsilielitsehv etsi tsigehv “wadida! ditsalvwi,sdaneluga!” awosehv tsigehv digilvwi,sdane,di, tla yagiha, tsawadvsidisv yudaha’dv agi,dagi,sgo gilo agi,tinvsdisdi digvniho galohisdi “Guy awake?” – “Yeah, he’s awake!” – “Tell him to wake up! We gotta go to work!” nowule ditsaisoi “gilo etsayanvhi ditsalvwi,sdanelesdi!” … “Eh… ‘di yawaduli digilvwi,sdanelesdi” – “ase’dv ditsalvwi,sdanelesdi!” … nowule dahnawosdi, da-da-dagihnawosdi na diyegatli, dogana,sinesgo ai digvnehv vsgi’dv wa-wagi,dagi,sgo tsigehv etsi vsgi yini,duwvnela, (uyetsi,sgv) nowule tsinasinesgv nowule dogana,sinesgv … nowu ase’dv awadida, nawvnelv’no yudaha’dv esga, tsiyelisehv etsi tsigehv asenv, wigalieligo gohiyv tsigi, … igada, hena, tla doyu, nowu, yidaninvwisdi tsunilvwi,sdane,di nowu,
segments.translation: I was putting them in the coke and playing pool. I felt like I was rich. [laughs] I appreciated my late mother. “Get up! You have to go to work!” she’d tell me. (I didn’t have a job when I was growing up.) Sometimes I hated that. The one who picked me up was knocking on the door, “Guy awake?!” “Yeah, he’s awake!” “Tell him to wake up. We gotta go to work!” [they said]. Then here comes Mom, “Somebody’s here to pick you up for work!” “I don’t want to go to work,” “But you have to go to work!” [she told me]. She used to pull on my covers and I really hated when she did that. [laughs] I would pull them up and then she’d pull them back again. She made me get up. I used to get mad at her for that, but now I appreciate it. Nowadays they’re not making their kids go to work.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: They don’t know how to work.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏗ, ᎾᎮᎾ, … ᎤᏠᏱ’Ᏼ ᎠᏎ ᏗᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁ,Ꮧ ᎾᏮᏁᎲ ᎠᏴ,
segments.transliteration: Yeah, doyu, hena, sgi nusdi, nahena, … utloyi’yv ase digilvwi,sdane,di nawvnehv ayv,
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s right, that’s how it is. Yeah, they made me a worker.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᏍᎩ ᎩᎳ, ᏗᏩᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᏗ ᏗᎿᏬ ᏛᎩᏅᏁᎸ ᎪᎦ, ᎮᎾ, ᏱᎩ, ᏠᎨᏏ, ᏥᏯ’Ꭳ ᎨᎲ ᏧᎾ,ᏕᎶ;ᏆᏍᏗ ᎠᏴ, ᏴᎩᎷᏣ, ᏥᎶ’ᎢᏍᎪ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏫᏒᏅ ᎡᏠᎩ, ᎵᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎪᎵ’Ꮕ, ᏱᎩ, wheelbarrow ᏥᏏᏙᎴᏟᏙᎲ ᏔᎷᎩᏍᎦᎭ ᎦᏩᏘ, … ᎠᏓ, ᏕᏥᏝᏗᏍᎬ ᏙᏱᎢᏢ ᏕᏥᏍᏡᏍᎬ ᏍᎩ ᏚᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎲ weekend-Ꭲ ᎠᏩᏑᎶ ᏱᎩ, ᏗᏩᎳᏑᎶ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏚᏂᏩᏒ Ꮣ’ᎢᏅᏁᎸ
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv sgi gila, diwadelo;quasdi dihnawo dvginvnelv goga, hena, yigi, tlogesi, tsiya’o gehv tsuna,delo;quasdi ayv, yvgilutsa, tsilo’isgo gehv uwisvnv etlogi, litsi tsigehv … goli’nv, yigi, wheelbarrow tsisidoletlidohv talugisgaha gawati, … ada, detsitladisgv doyiitlv detsistlusgv sgi dunilvwi,sdanehv weekend-i awasulo yigi, diwalasulo’le yigi, duniwasv da’invnelv
segments.translation: Only when I went to school did they [His parents] get me clothes. In the summertime, I was in the field when I come home from school. I was plowing. My aunt had a garden, Litsi was her name. In the wintertime, I was pushing a wheelbarrow around with a metal wheel. I would chop wood and put them on the porch. Since they worked on weekends, they would buy me pants and shoes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏙᏳ’Ꮫ … ᎠᏴ,’Ꭱ ᏍᏊ … ᎡᏙᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏂᏲᏍᎩ ᏥᏭᏴᏢ ᎠᏓᎾᏫ, ᎠᏎᏅ, P.O.W. ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎤᎴᏐ:Ꮧ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᎷᏨ ᎠᏗᏔᏍᎬ’Ꮓ ᏧᎴᏅᎲ ᏃᏭ ‘ᎸᏢ ᏚᎾ,ᎦᎴᏅᎲ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ, café-ᎢᏭ, ᏥᏚᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎮ ᏗᎬᏗᏰᏍᎬ’Ꮽ … ᎡᎵᏭ, Ꮟ--ᏙᏥᏂ,ᏗᏫ,ᏍᎬ Ꮟ ᎦᏲᏟ, ᎠᎦᏈᏴᎡᎲ … ᏃᏭ ᏗᏑᎶ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏙᎩᏁᏅᎲ ᏣᏗ ᏃᏭ ᏗᏐᎢ, … “ᏓᎦᏴᎳᎩ, ᏗᏑᎶ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏓᏔᎴᏌ,” Mabrles ᏂᏓᏩᏁᎶᏂᏙᎸ
