segments.transliteration: Yeah, doyu’dv … ayv,’e squu … edoda, hena, tsigehv aniyosgi tsiwuyvtlv adanawi, asenv, P.O.W. tsinuli,stanv uleso:di, tsigehv tsulutsv aditasgv’no tsulenvhv nowu ‘lvtlv duna,galenvhv etsi tsigehv … etsi tsigehv nowu, café-iwu, tsidulvwi,sdanehe digvdiyesgv’wu … eliwu, si--dotsini,diwi,sgv si gayotli, agaquiyvehv … nowu disulo nowule doginenvhv tsadi nowu disoi, … “dagayvlagi, disulo nowule sgi nusdv datalesa,” Mabrles nidawanelonidolv
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s true. My dad was in the military service. He was in a war and became a POW (prisoner of war). He was really skinny when he got back. He started drinking and they split up, him and my mom. My mom was working in a café and was washing dishes. We were still making it. She wasn’t paid much. Those pants you were saying they gave us… “When the pants get old they’re going to have holes.” Cause I was playing marbles and crawling around.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎦᏝᏂᏙᎯ, -- “ᎦᏝᏂᏙᎯ,” ᎠᏃᏎᎰ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎩᏓᏲᏢ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏴ,
segments.transliteration: gatlanidohi, -- “gatlanidohi,” anoseho sgi hena, agidayotlv squu ayv,
segments.translation: Gatlanidoh(i). He was putting in the hole. That’s what they call it. I played marbles too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ ᏓᏔᎴᏒ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ, ᏚᏂᏩᏍᎬ, ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: nowu tsigi datalesv nahiyu tsigehv nowu tsigi, duniwasgv, sgi yusdi,
segments.translation: Those same holes we had, nowadays that’s the kind of pants they buy.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏤᏥᏲᏎᎲ ᎥᎥ…ᏤᏥᏲᏎᎲ ᏗᎬᎩᎵᏏ, ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ, ᎤᏂᎷᏨ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᏍᏡᏴ ᎬᏗ, “Hey!” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᏝᏍᎪ, -- ᎮᏍᏗ, ᏗᏍᏗᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎯ, ᏗᏍᏓᏓᎵ,ᏚᎩ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, Ꮭ ᏱᏚᏂᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎯ,” ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎲ “ᏗᏍᏗᏃᎯᏏ ᏚᏂᏩᏒᎢ--ᏕᏣᏩᏒ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ,” ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎸ (unintelligble)... ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎸ “ᎠᏴ, ᏗᏩᏛᏒ” ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎸ “ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏔᎾ, ᎣᏥᎳᏕᏍᎬ ᎤᏟ ᏬᎦᏓᎡᎬ ᏱᎩ ᎠᏂᏣᏢᏍᎬ ᎠᎴᏱᎩ,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ … “Ꭽ-ᎭᎳ ᏍᏊ ᏧᎬᏩᎵ;Ꮧ?” – “About seventy bucks” – “Well, what size do you wear?” ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎸ “Walmart-Ꭲ ᏓᎨᏏ,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ “Pick-up-Ꭲ ᎣᏂ, ᏗᏢ ᏙᏓᎨᎵᏏ, then I’ll drive down--up and down this road. ᏕᏥᏔᎴᏍᎬ until you give me $70 a piece for them!” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ
segments.transliteration: tsetsiyosehv vv…tsetsiyosehv digvgilisi, anigeyutsa, unilutsv sgi tsigehv distluyv gvdi, “Hey!” gatsiyohelv “tlasgo, -- hesdi, disdilvwi,sdanehi, disdadali,dugi,’le yigi, tla yidunilvwi,sdanehi,” gatsiyosehv “disdinohisi duniwasvi--detsawasv’le yigi,” gatsiyoselv (unintelligble)... gatsiyoselv “ayv, diwadvsv” gatsiyoselv “sgi yinulistana, otsiladesgv utli wogadaegv yigi anitsatlvsgv aleyigi,” gatsiyohehv … “ha-hala squu tsugvwali;di?” – “About seventy bucks” – “Well, what size do you wear?” gatsiyoselv “Walmart-i dagesi,” gatsiyohelv “Pick-up-i oni, ditlv dodagelisi, then I’ll drive down--up and down this road. detsitalesgv until you give me $70 a piece for them!” gatsiyohelv
segments.translation: That’s what I was telling my granddaughters when they came. They had on those kind of pants. I asked them, “Hey, y’all don’t work. Your boyfriends don’t work. Tell them to buy you clothes, or buy them yourselves. When I was growing up and that happened, we’d cut the pantlegs off. Or, we’d patch them up… How much did they cost?” “About $70,” [they said]. “Well, what size do you wear?” I asked them. “I’m going to go to Walmart and tie them to the back of the pickup and drag them and make holes on them. Then you can give me $70 a piece for them,” I told them.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏥᏗᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏗᎩᏥ ᏗᎩᎦᏴᎵᎨ Ꮧ--ᏚᎾ,ᏙᎥ ᏃᏭᎴ … ᏣᎵᏏ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᏚᏓ, Ꮩ’Ꭹ ᏚᎾ,ᏙᎡ ᏣᏗ,?
segments.transliteration: tsidinohesgv digitsi digigayvlige di--duna,dov nowule … tsalisi, tsigehv tsaduda, do’gi duna,doe tsadi,?
segments.translation: We were talking about our mothers and grandmothers and their names. Your grandma and grandpa, what did you say their names were?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏤᎩ,’Ꮫ ᏚᏙᎥ ᎡᏚᏥ, ᏴᎱᎵ’Ꮕ, ᏐᎢ, … ᎡᏥ’Ꮕ, Louise ᏚᏙᎥ … ᎠᎾ,ᏓᎸᎢᏴ ᎡᏓᎨ ᎠᏃᏎᎰ Nancy, ᏎᎵ’Ꮕ, - Sarah, Bibi – Lucy, ᏩᎵ’Ꮕ, - Polly, ᏏᎵ’Ꮕ, Ce-Ce-Ce-Celia ᏚᏙᎥ … ᎾᏅ Garlen Eagle ᎤᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ … was my mom’s sister ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ
segments.transliteration: tsegi,’dv dudov edutsi, yvhuli’nv, soi, … etsi’nv, Louise dudov … ana,dalviyv edage anoseho Nancy, seli’nv, - Sarah, Bibi – Lucy, wali’nv, - Polly, sili’nv, Ce-Ce-Ce-Celia dudov … nanv Garlen Eagle utsi tsigehv … was my mom’s sister squu sginana
segments.translation: My *grandpa’s name was Tseg(i) and Yvhuli [his grandmother] was the other. And my mother’s name was Louise. Her sisters, they called Nancy, Edage; Seli, Sarah; and Bibi, Lucy; Wali, Polly; and Sili was Celia. That Garlen Eagle—his mom was also my mom’s sister.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Your parents aren’t around now?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Huh uh. ᎯᏍᎩ ᏦᎢᏁᎢ, ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎡᏥ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎠᏮᏌ, ᏃᏭ, ᎾᎩ,ᏍᏗᏕᎪ ᎨᎲ … ᎡᏚᏚ ᏥᎨᎲ Ned ᎩᏟ, -- Ned--ᎩᏟ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏚᏙᎥ - Ned Puppy ᏚᏙᎥ … ᎡᎵᏏ’Ꮕ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏥᎪᎥ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎡᏚᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎩᏄᏓ’Ꮽ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎨᎲ ᏦᎢ ᎩᏄᏗ’Ꮕ, Irish ᎨᎲ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏣᎦᏟᎶᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᎩᎾ, ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏆᎳ--ᎤᏥ,ᏈᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ’Ꮫ ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏇᏚᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏐᏁᎳ,ᏍᎪᎯ, ᏐᏁᎳ, ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎤᏲᎱᏌ, Ꮟ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ every morning, 9 o’clock, like clockwork. ᎠᏙᎳᏅᏗ ᏛᏯᎢ, ᎨᎲ ᎦᏅᏃᏩ, ᎤᏅᏍᎦᎳ, ᏙᏱᎢᏢ ᏯᎵ,ᏍᏛᏡᎦ, ᎨᎲ ᎦᏅᏃᏩ, ᏳᏬᎩ,ᏐᎾ, ᎧᏫ, ᏳᏂᏟᏍᏔᏁᎳ, ᎨᎲ ᏦᎵ,ᏕᏯ, ᏃᏭ ᏱᎦᎴᏅ,Ꮧ, ᎨᎲ ᏯᏂᏅᏍᏓ, “Ꭷ! ᎩᎶ ᏮᎩᎧᎲᎩ!” ᏯᏓ, ᎠᏂ,ᏘᎾᏫᏗᏍᎬ,
segments.transliteration: Huh uh. hisgi tsoinei, yawadetiyvda, gehv etsi tsuyohusv nahiyu awvsa, nowu, nagi,sdidego gehv … edudu tsigehv Ned gitli, -- Ned--gitli usdi dudov - Ned Puppy dudov … elisi’nv tsigehv tla yawanv,ta, tla ilvhiyu tsigov yigehe eduda, hena, tsigehv ginuda’wu, atsalagi, gehv tsoi ginudi’nv, Irish gehv yonega, yusdi, gehv tsagatlilostanv agina, uli,squala--utsi,quidi sgina’dv uli,squedusgv, tsigehv sonela,sgohi, sonela, yudetiyvda, gehv uyohusa, si ganvdadisgo every morning, 9 o’clock, like clockwork. adolanvdi dvyai, gehv ganvnowa, unvsgala, doyiitlv yali,sdvtluga, gehv ganvnowa, yuwogi,sona, kawi, yunitlistanela, gehv tsoli,deya, nowu yigalenv,di, gehv yaninvsda, “ka! gilo wvgikahvgi!” yada, ani,tinawidisgv,
segments.translation: Uh uh. When I was twenty five, my mom passed away. That was when I was on my own. My grandpa’s name was Ned Gitl(i) or Gitl(i) Usdi, Ned Puppy. My grandmother, I don’t know, because I never saw her. My grandpa was a quarter Cherokee and three quarters Irish. He looked like a white man. I got a picture of him, he liked to wear his hat crooked, cause he’s wearing one. He was 99 when he passed away, I still remember it. Every morning at nine o’clock, like clockwork. He would be coming with a cane. He would have a pipe in his mouth and sit down on the porch. When he finished smoking, then they gave him a cup of coffee. He wouldn’t stay after that. He wanted somebody to take him home. And they took him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And how about you, what did you say your parents’ names were?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: William and Nancy Bunch.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: William Bunch.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: And in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: I forgot. Just Wil(i) was my dad’s name.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And what was your mom’s name? [In Cherokee]

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: I forgot, too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Nen(i)s(i) was her name, it was Nen(i)s(i).

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah… When y’all were growing up did you all have a garden? Or your parents?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: My dad had a garden.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did he plant a lot of stuff?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Not really.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏙᏳ? … yeah, ᏍᎩᏛ ᎢᏣᎵ,ᏍᏕᎸ;ᏙᏗ ᎨᎮ ᏙᎲ? ᎠᏎ’Ꮫ
segments.transliteration: tla doyu? … yeah, sgidv itsali,sdelv;dodi gehe dohv? ase’dv
segments.translation: Oh, no? I guess that’s what helped you all, right? I would guess.

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ, ᎢᏥᏩᏛᏗ … ᏄᎾ,’Ꭸ ᏕᏥᏫᏒ? ᏚᏯ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ,?
segments.transliteration: ali,sdayv,di, itsiwadvdi … nuna,’ge detsiwisv? duya’le yigi,?
segments.translation: You all got your food from the garden. Did you all plant potatoes or beans?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Yeah. That’s what he planted, and cucumbers.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Boy, cucumbers they are the best to eat.

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: And tomatoes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What about, do you hunt?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: I used to.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.text: ᏥᎾᎵ’Ꮽ, ᏃᏭ, ᏌᎷᏱ ᎡᏓᏍᏗ … Ꮵ,ᏈᏯ ᎠᏨᏏᏰᏓᏍᏗ
segments.transliteration: tsinali’wu, nowu, saluyi edasdi … tsi,quiya atsvsiyedasdi
segments.translation: I’m too lazy to get out in the woods now. It’s too much walking around.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: … Ꮎ ᏥᏣᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᏣᏙᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᏃᎭᎵᏙᎯ,’Ꭸ ᎨᎮ?
segments.transliteration: … na tsitsadvsidisv tsadoda, tsigehv ganohalidohi,’ge gehe?
segments.translation: When you were growing up, did your dad hunt?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Uh uh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: My dad wasn’t a hunter.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: … ᏴᏓ ᏙᎲ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎡᎯ, ᎠᏎ ᎢᏥᏲᎮ ᏗᏥᏰᎸ ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏕᎸ;ᏙᏗ ᎠᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ, … ᏂᎯ’ᏛᏛ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏠᏱ Ꮭ’Ꭸ? ᏴᏓ ᎫᏩᏯ ᏱᎩ, ᏜᏱ,Ꮥ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏃᏭᎴ …
segments.transliteration: … yvda dohv inage ehi, ase itsiyohe ditsiyelv uli,sdelv;dodi ali,sdayv,di, … nihi’dvdv squu utloyi tla’ge? yvda guwaya yigi, dlayi,de’le yigi, nowule …
segments.translation: I guess you all were hunting wild things to feed your body with. To eat. And it was probably the same with you, right? [To Mack] Like, blueberries and poke?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: I have never liked poke salad.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No? [laughs]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: You don’t? It’s really good.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏒᎩ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ ᎬᏂᏍᏔᏅ ᏱᏥᎩ,’Ꭱ ᎾᎮᎾ, ᏭᏟ ᏱᏂᏥᏰᎸᎾ ᎠᎪᏍᏓ’Ꮽ, ᏥᏍᏆᏴᏍᏗ ᎪᎢ ᏫᏥᏍᏚᏟᏍᏗ ᎠᎻ’Ꮕ, ᎦᏚ’ᎢᏅ, ᎬᏗ, ᏩᎩᎩᏍᏗ ᎤᏟ ᏥᏰᎸᎾ, ᏒᎩ,
segments.transliteration: svgi’nv, squu gvnistanv yitsigi,’e nahena, wutli yinitsiyelvna agosda’wu, tsisquayvsdi goi witsisdutlisdi ami’nv, gadu’inv, gvdi, wagigisdi utli tsiyelvna, svgi,
segments.translation: Wild onion, I can eat it cooked, but I’d rather eat it raw. I chew on it. And put grease and salt on it, with bread. That’s how I like wild onion.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ᏺ ᏒᎦ,Ꮤ’Ꮽ, ᏳᏪᎵᏍᏗ, ᏱᏥᎩ, ᏒᎩ, (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎠᏎᏃ heartburn ᏱᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏌ,
segments.transliteration: ayv’yo svga,ta’wu, yuwelisdi, yitsigi, svgi, (uyetsi,sgv) aseno heartburn yinawali,sdasa,
segments.translation: I can eat onion like an apple. [laughs] But then I get heartburn.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᎠᏥᎳ, ᎠᎹᏱ ᎤᏚᎯ, ᏱᎦᏑᏴᎾ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ
segments.transliteration: nanv atsila, amayi uduhi, yigasuyvna, sginana
segments.translation: And then watercress, I can really eat that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏥᎳ ᎠᎹᏱ ᎡᎯ,
segments.transliteration: ayv’dv squu agilvquo,di, tsigehv sgina atsila amayi ehi,
segments.translation: I used to really like that watercress.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎯᎢ ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ, ᏗᏩᏂᎩᏒ ᏑᎾᎴ ᎦᏗᏓ, ᏚᏯ Ꮥ--crockpot-Ꭲ ᏕᏥᎸᎦ, ᏚᏯ … ᏏᏆ ᏧᎳᏏ,Ꮧ ᏙᏥᎸᎦ,
segments.transliteration: hii nowu tsigi, diwanigisv sunale gadida, duya de--crockpot-i detsilvga, duya … siqua tsulasi,di dotsilvga,
segments.translation: When I got up this morning, I put some beans in the crockpot with a hogham.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Gah lee!

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏁᎳᎩ, ᏔᎵᎭ ᎢᎦ, ᏙᏓᎬᏂᏍᏔᏂ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏎᎷ ᎦᏚ ᏙᏓᎪᏢᏂ, ᎪᎢ ᎦᏚ ᏙᏓᎬᏂᏍᏔᏂ ᏏᏆ ᎭᏫᏯ ᎣᏂ, ᏗᏢ ᎤᏍᏗᏟ,
segments.transliteration: nelagi, taliha iga, dodagvnistani nowule selu gadu dodagotlvni, goi gadu dodagvnistani siqua hawiya oni, ditlv usditli,
segments.translation: I’m going to cook it for two days. And then I’m going to make cornbread, cook bread in the oven. Then I’m going to throw in some hogmeat.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [laughs] I guess this one [Edward] is going to come visit you.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: I’m going to run him off!

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: I’ll already be sitting there this evening.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: More for you! [Mack]
[Everybody talking]

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎠᏎ’Ꮫ ᏗᏦᏞᏍᏗ ᏑᎾᎴ ᎤᏒ ᎩᎳ, ᏥᎦᏓ,
segments.transliteration: ase’dv ditsotlesdi sunale usv gila, tsigada,
segments.translation: You’re going to be sitting there. Because I said: it’s tomorrow night!
[laughter]

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: I can wait.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: You can wait.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: He’ll be sitting there all night.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Where do you find watercress you were talking about?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: It is laying across, like on a rock or log.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It’s hard to find, but I can’t ever find it.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Because --

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: --It grows all over Sallisaw Creek.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎠᏴ, … Garlen Eagel, Ꮎ ᏧᏙ, ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ, Shorty, Toya ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᏩᏂᎷᎪ ᏒᎩ, ᏫᏥᏯᎩᎡᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏥᎳ, ᎠᎹᏱ ᎤᏚᎯ, ᎾᏅ ᎪᏤᎾ, … ᎪᏧᎾ, y’know, ᏣᏅᏔ, ᏬᎩ--ᎤᏂᏯᎸᏍᎪ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ, ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayv, … Garlen Eagel, na tsudo, anigeyutsa, Shorty, Toya tsigehv … adanelv wanilugo svgi, witsiyagieho sgina atsila, amayi uduhi, nanv gotsena, … gotsuna, y’know, tsanvta, wogi--uniyalvsgo igohida, gehv
segments.translation: Me…that Garlen Eagle. His sisters, it was Shorty and Toya, they came to the house. I would go get onion for them. And watercress and kochan or kochun. That’s what they were looking for all the time.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᎢᎦ ᎠᎩᎸᏉᏗ, ᏍᎩᎾ watercress. ᎾᏅ ᎣᏍᏗᏁᎳ, “’ᏙᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᎩᏍᎪ ᏝᏍᎪ, ᏩᎧ, ᎤᏂᎩᏍᏗ, ᏱᎩ,?” ᏯᏬᏏ,’Ꮫ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: iga agilvquodi, sgina watercress. nanv osdinela, “’donv sgina tsigisgo tlasgo, waka, unigisdi, yigi,?” yawosi,’dv (uyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: I really like watercress. My husband, “Why are you eating that? Isn’t that what the cows eat?” he’d say. [laughs]

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮧ, ᏱᏓᏂᏃᎵ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎵᎨ “ᏒᎩ,Ꮓ ᏳᏛᏌ, … “Boy,” ᏣᏗᏍᎬ “ᎢᏣᎦ,ᏎᏍᏙᏗ,’Ꮫ ᏩᎧ, ᏳᏪᎵᏍᏗ, ᏕᏣᏏᏞᏍᏗ,” ᏯᏓ, “ᎡᎵ ᎢᎩ ᏱᏥᎬ”
segments.transliteration: uwoli,di, yidaninoli tsigehv anigayvlige “svgi,no yudvsa, … “Boy,” tsadisgv “itsaga,sesdodi,’dv waka, yuwelisdi, detsasitlesdi,” yada, “eli igi yitsigv”
segments.translation: It’s funny, when the onion grew, the elders would say, “Boy, you all need to watch out, if you eat enough, you all are going to have leaves sticking to your butt just like cows do.”
[laughter]

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᏣᏓ, … … Ꭺ-ᎪᏤᎾ, -- ᎪᏧᎾ, Ꭺ--ᎪᏧᎾ,? ᎢᎦᏓ “ᎪᏤᎾ,” ᏯᎾᏓ,
segments.transliteration: nanv tsada, … … go-gotsena, -- gotsuna, go--gotsuna,? igada “gotsena,” yanada,
segments.translation: What you were saying kochan, kochun. Some would say “kochan”

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Yeah, ᎪᏤᏂ ᏯᎾᏓ, ᎪᏤᏂ, ᎪᏧᎾ, ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏃᏎᎰ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, gotseni yanada, gotseni, gotsuna, hena, anoseho
segments.translation: Yeah, kocheni. They call it kochun.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: I’ve heard that—kochun.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I’ve never eaten that.
Oh, it’s good, kinda crunchy and soft.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎤᏖᏗ,’Ꮫ … ᎠᎾ,ᏗᏍᎪ Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᏯᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮩ ᎠᏴ, ᎾᏅ, … ᏚᏯ ᏍᏊ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎡᎯ, ᏍᏊ ‘ᏓᏁᎸ ᎤᏰᎬ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ--
segments.transliteration: utedi,’dv … ana,disgo tla hena, yagilvquo,do ayv, nanv, … duya squu inage ehi, squu ‘danelv uyegv, sginana--
segments.translation: They say it’s good, but I don’t like it. Wild beans, those are good, they grow at the house --

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: --ᏗᏩᏛᏒ’Ꮫ ᎤᏰᎬ, Huh uh, “ᎤᏴᎭᏘ,”ᏍᎪ, ᎭᏗᎯ? … Huh uh, “Wild Bean” ᎠᏃᎮᎲ *ᎯᎢ’ᎮᎾ,* ᏱᎩᏗ, … vine ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏯᏛᏂ, ᏂᏚᏍᏙ ᏍᎩᎾ, … ᏃᏭ ᎤᏍᎪᎵ’Ꮽ ᏱᏩᏍᏕᏝ, where it “snap” ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲ cause if you don’t, ᎠᎦᏴᎳᎵ’Ꮓ ᎨᎰ *ᎯᎢ* ᏗᎬᏅᎯᏗ, ᏓᏂ--Ꮒ,ᏓᏅᏁᎰ ᎠᏅᏂᏍᏗᏍᎪ ᏍᏊ
segments.transliteration: --diwadvsv’dv uyegv, Huh uh, “uyvhati,”sgo, hadihi? … Huh uh, “Wild Bean” anohehv *hii’hena,* yigidi, … vine yusdi, yadvni, nidusdo sgina, … nowu usgoli’wu yiwasdetla, where it “snap” yini,galisdihv cause if you don’t, agayvlali’no geho *hii* digvnvhidi, dani--ni,danvneho anvnisdisgo squu
segments.translation: --or they grew at the house where I grew up. Uh huh, did you say Uhyvhat(i)? They just called it ‘wild bean.’ Uh huh. It’s about this [gestures] big, it climbs like a vine. You take the bean off of the ‘head’ of the vine. It snaps, right away. If not, then it’s too old to cook. They cut them this [gestures] long, they cook them.

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: --Bean vine --

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Is that really a bean?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: … ᎠᎮ-ᎠᎮᏗ it’s like a green bean, ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎵᏍ,Ꮣ, But, “wild bean,” ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏃᏎᎰ
segments.transliteration: … ahe-ahedi it’s like a green bean, yini,galis,da, But, “wild bean,” hena, anoseho
segments.translation: I guess. It’s kind of like a green bean. But they call it ‘wild bean.’

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Is that what they were talking about? That uhyvhat(i). Is that not -- ?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: No, that’s still something else.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Oh, it’s still something else? Okay.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Uhyvhat(i) is still something else.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏭ ᎮᎾ,’Ꮓ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏣᏩᏓᎨᎸ ᏐᏧᏁᎦ, ᏥᏍᏓᏗ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏍᏊ ᎣᏂ ᎠᏩᏕᎨᎸ’Ꮫ ᏍᏓᏱ ᎠᏩᏛᏗ ᏃᏭ ᎥᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: nowu hena,’no sawu yuwaga,da, tsawadagelv sotsunega, tsisdadi nahiyu squu oni awadegelv’dv sdayi awadvdi nowu vsgiyusdi,
segments.translation: That socheneg(a) you all were talking about. I ate it one time. That was the last time I ate it, it is hard to find now.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Shoot, ᎾᏅ Sam Reed ᏧᏓᎾᎾᎿ … Sallisaw Creek’Ꮫ ᎾᎥ ᎤᎾ Ꮟ Ꮵ,ᏈᏍᏔᏅ ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏙᏔᏅ
segments.transliteration: Shoot, nanv Sam Reed tsudananahna … Sallisaw Creek’dv nav una si tsi,quistanv yuli,sdotanv
segments.translation: Shoot, Sam Reed Store next to Sallisaw Creek, there’s always some growing there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really? Man!

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏒᎩ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎡᎯ, ᏱᏣᏰᎯᏌ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᏂ,ᏨᏁᎳ, ᏱᏦᏢᎾ, when, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏱᏂ,ᏨᏁᎳ, ᏂᎦᏓ, Ꭳ’Ꭲ ᏗᏢ, ᏱᏫᏣᏕᎦ, Boy, ᎢᏤ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ, ᏯᏛᎯ, -- ᏯᏛᎯ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ … Ꮭ ᎠᏎ ᏭᏟᎢ ᏫᏣᏯᎸᏍᏗ, ᏱᎩ, ᏗᏤᏅᏒ’Ꮽ, ᎤᏒᏛ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏂ,ᏨᏁᎳ, ᏅᎰᏍᏔᎾ ᏱᏫ,ᏣᏕᎠ ᏩᎦ,Ꮫ’Ꮽ ᏯᏛᎯ, … ᏱᎧᏁᏉᎦ,
segments.transliteration: svgi inage ehi, yitsayehisa, osda, yini,tsvnela, yitsotlvna, when, osda, yini,tsvnela, nigada, o’i ditlv, yiwitsadega, Boy, itse iyusdi, yadvhi, -- yadvhi, sginana … tla ase wutlii witsayalvsdi, yigi, ditsenvsv’wu, usvdv sgi yini,tsvnela, nvhostana yiwi,tsadea waga,dv’wu yadvhi, … yikanequoga,
segments.translation: If you pick some wild onion, clean it, and you fix it up good. Then if you till an area of the ground. Then throw that onion stems there. You will have a whole bunch of wild onion growing there. Then you won’t have to go out looking for it—if you put in your back yard. It’ll be growing. If you’re throwing out the parts you didn’t use, it’ll multiply.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Somebody will go get it all. [laughter] There will be nothing left.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: They’ll be walking around like a cow.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏫᏥᎦᎵ,’Ꭱ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎪᎯᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᏥᏰᏣᏍᏗᎲ “ᎠᏂᏲᏍᎩ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎣᎩᏯᏅᎲ” ᏣᏗᎲ … “ᎾᎯᏳ’Ꭱ ᏥᎨᎲ” ᏣᏗᎲ “We didn’t have no choice,” – “when you turned of age, ᏓᏂᏯᏂᏍᎬ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᏓᎿᏫ, ᎾᎯᏳ ᎠᏍᏆᎵᏍᎬ” ᏣᏗᎲ ᎠᎵ,ᏍᎪᏍᎬ’Ꭱ ᎠᎮᏅ, ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮧ ᎮᎾ, “ᎣᎦᏓᏅᏅ,Ꮣ’Ꮫ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎣᎩᏥ,ᏈᏍᏔᏅ” ᏣᏗᎲ … “Tent’Ꮫ ᎤᏪᏬᏨ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎠᏓᏁᎸ” ᏣᏗᎲ “curtains’Ꮽ Ꮒ,ᏚᏍᏛ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᏕᎧᏅᏑᎸ ᏗᏰᎸ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎣᎦᏓᏅᏅ,Ꮣ ᏩᎧ, ᏳᏪᎵᏍᏗ,” ᏣᏗᎲ ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᏓᏂᏙᎾᎥ “ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ ᏱᏬ’ᎢᎶᏌ, *shh-shh* ᏣᏓ, ᏙᎩᏣᏲᎯᎲ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᎨᎲ curtain Ꮒ,ᏚᏍᏛ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏗᏢ, ᏱᏬᎩᎷᏣ,” ᏣᏗᎲ “Nurse Ꮼ’ᎢᏯᏂᏍᎬ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᏃᏭ Ꮩ’ᎢᎪᎵᏰᏍᎬ” ᏣᏗᎲ “Ꭷ! ᎤᏛᏅ” ᏣᏗᎲ ᎠᎨᏯ, “Mr. Eagle, ᎠᏬᎮᎸ” ᏣᏗᎲ “’I’m going to need you to … bend over and--and cough for me,’ ᎤᏛᏅ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎭᏩ ᎠᏩᏌᎷᏅ’Ꮫ” ᏣᏗᎲ “’Ooh!’ ᎤᏛᏅ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎤᏓᎾᏫ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᎨᏯ,” ᏣᏗᎲ “’That boy’s got worms!’ ᎤᏛᏅ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎾᎯᏳ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, nurse” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎤᏴᏟᏢᎢ,” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎤᎦ,ᏛᏅ’Ꮫ ‘Ꭽ!’ ᎤᏛᏅ ᏭᎦ,ᏔᎲᏒ ‘He ain’t got worms! It’s just wild onion that was hanging out!’ ᎠᎪᎮᎸ” ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: witsigali,’e tsadihv gohidi, tsigehv otsiyetsasdihv “aniyosgi” tsadihv “ogiyanvhv” tsadihv … “nahiyu’e tsigehv” tsadihv “We didn’t have no choice,” – “when you turned of age, daniyanisgv” tsadihv “dahnawi, nahiyu asqualisgv” tsadihv ali,sgosgv’e ahenv, uwoli,di hena, “ogadanvnv,da’dv” tsadihv “ogitsi,quistanv” tsadihv … “Tent’dv uwewotsv” tsadihv “adanelv” tsadihv “curtains’wu ni,dusdv” tsadihv “dekanvsulv diyelv” tsadihv “ogadanvnv,da waka, yuwelisdi,” tsadihv etsulaha danidonav “ganaga,ti yiwo’ilosa, *shh-shh* tsada, dogitsayohihv” tsadihv “nowu’nv gehv curtain ni,dusdv agvyi ditlv, yiwogilutsa,” tsadihv “Nurse wo’iyanisgv” tsadihv “nowu do’igoliyesgv” tsadihv “ka! udvnv” tsadihv ageya, “Mr. Eagle, awohelv” tsadihv “’I’m going to need you to … bend over and--and cough for me,’ udvnv” tsadihv “hawa awasalunv’dv” tsadihv “’Ooh!’ udvnv” tsadihv “udanawi,stanv ageya,” tsadihv “’That boy’s got worms!’ udvnv” tsadihv “nahiyu atsalagi, nurse” tsadihv “uyvtlitlvi,” tsadihv “uga,dvnv’dv ‘ha!’ udvnv wuga,tahvsv ‘He ain’t got worms! It’s just wild onion that was hanging out!’ agohelv” tsadihv
segments.translation: Witsigal(i) was saying, we were laughing at him, “They called us to go into the Army,” he said. “We didn’t have a choice then. When you came of age, they called you into service. The war was going on.” He was lying, but it was funny. “There was a bunch of us lined up. There was a giant tent and they only had curtains for rooms. We were all lined up just like cattle and there was a doctor on each side. When they would walk by [shh-shh] they’d give us all shots. Then when we got in front of the curtain a nurse would call us.” “They were examining us,” he said. Then the nurse said, “Alright, Mr. Eagle. I’m going to need you to bend over and cough for me,” she said. “I just bent over,” he said. “Ooh!” she said. She ran away. “That boy’s got worms!” she said. “Then a Cherokee nurse came in,” he said. She looked at him, “Haw! He ain’t got worms, it’s just wild onion hanging out!” she told her.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎡᏠᎩ,’ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ, ᏧᏂ,ᏘᏅᏒ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏎᎵ,’Ꭱ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏎᎵ,’Ꭱ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᎦᎸᏗ’Ꭾ ᎨᎲ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎮᎾ, Man! ᎤᏂᎸᏉ,Ꮫ ᎧᏅᏌᏛ ᎮᎾ, … ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ ᏭᏂ,ᏘᏂᏙᎸ ᎤᏂᎷᏨ … Ꮎ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, “Aunt Sarah, what’d-… What’d they tell you?” ᎠᎪᎮᎸ “Oh, my doctor?” ᏣᏓ, “He say” ᏧᏛᏅ “He say ‘You got two bucking horses.’” ᎤᏛᏅ ᏣᏗᎲ Ꮎ ᎤᏓᏘᏅᏓ, Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ, “’ᏙᎩ ᎭᏓ, ᏎᎵ,?” ᏣᏓ, “Ꮎ ‘Two bucking horses Ꮒ,ᏣᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁ’ ᎠᏬᎮᎸ” – “Ꮭ ‘Two bucking horses’ ᏰᏦᏎᎸ Tuberculosis ᎡᏦᏎᎸ!”
segments.transliteration: etlogi,’hena, squu ganaga,ti, tsuni,tinvsv (uniyetsi,sgv) seli,’e tsigehv seli,’e tsigehv tsugalvdi’he gehv diniyotli, hena, Man! unilvquo,dv kanvsadv hena, … ganaga,ti wuni,tinidolv unilutsv … na diniyotli, “Aunt Sarah, what’d-… What’d they tell you?” agohelv “Oh, my doctor?” tsada, “He say” tsudvnv “He say ‘You got two bucking horses.’” udvnv tsadihv na udatinvda, na ageyutsa, “’dogi hada, seli,?” tsada, “na ‘Two bucking horses ni,tsali,sdane’ awohelv” – “tla ‘Two bucking horses’ yetsoselv Tuberculosis etsoselv!”
segments.translation: Also, my aunt, they took her to the clinic. [laughter] Her name was Sel(i). She was goofy. The kids all liked her, she would just say anything. They took her to the doctor, and when they came back, the kids said, “Aunt Sarah, what’d they tell you?” “My doctor? Oh, my doctor?” she said. “He say… He say ‘You got two bucking horses’,” she said. Then her daughter asked, “What do you say, Sel(i)?” “He said ‘You’ve got two bucking horses’… He didn’t say ‘Two bucking horses!’ He said ‘You’ve got tuberculosis!’”
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎠᏧᏣ, … Ꮩ-ᏙᏳ’Ꭱ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, ᎬᏩᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅᎢ, Ꮎ ᏧᏢᎬ ᏃᏭ, ᎦᎾᎦ,Ꮨ ᏭᏂ,ᏘᎾᏫᏛᏙᎸ ᏙᏗᏰᏥᏲᎳ Ꮎ “injection” ᏓᏃᏎᎰ ᏚᎾ,ᏓᏣᏲᏟ, … “’ᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏗ, Ꮒ,ᏣᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎢ ‘ᏧᏣ,?” – … “Injection’Ꮫ ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎢ” ᎤᏛᏅ “ᎾᏃ ᏓᏥᏣᏲᎸ” ᎤᎾ,ᏛᏅ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: na’dv sawu yuwaga,da, atsutsa, … do-doyu’e atsalagi, gehv atsutsa, anitsalagi, gvwadvhistanvi, na tsutlvgv nowu, ganaga,ti wuni,tinawidvdolv dodiyetsiyola na “injection” danoseho duna,datsayotli, … “’dohv usdi, ni,tsali,sdanei ‘tsutsa,?” – … “Injection’dv nawali,sdanei” udvnv “nano datsitsayolv” una,dvnv (uyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: One time, that one boy, he was really Cherokee. He was raised by Cherokees. He got sick and went to the doctor. The doctor said he was going to give him a shot. And we call it an injection. [At home] they asked the boy, “What’s wrong with you?” Then he said, “I’ve got an injection.” “He’s talking about getting those shots,” they said. [laughs]
(laughter)

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Aww.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏭ ᎧᎵ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏧᏣ,
segments.transliteration: nowu kali atsalagi, tsigehv sgina atsutsa,
segments.translation: He was really a full-blood Cherokee, that boy.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎢᎸᎯᏳ Ꮎ ᎢᏤᎵᏎᏍᎪ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᏴᏫ, ᏳᏬᏂᏌ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎢᏣᎦ,ᏎᏍᏔᏅ ᏱᎩ, ᏍᎩ ᏂᎨᎲᎾ, ᎢᏣᎦ,ᏎᏍᏔᏅᎢ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏂ--ᎧᎵ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᎠᏁᏙᎲ ᎢᏤᏙᎲ … ᏳᏂᏬᏂᏌ, “He” ᏯᎾᏓ, ᏍᏊ ᎠᎨᏯ ᏯᏂᏃᎮ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ ᏯᏂᏃᎮ “She” ᏗᎾ,ᏗᎰ ᎾᏅ, ᏍᏊ ᎠᎦ,ᏛᎲᏍᏔᏅᎢ, ᎮᎾ, ᏱᎾᏂᏩ, ᏂᎦᏓ,’Ꮫ ᎠᏂᏴᏫᏯ ᏍᎩ ᏄᎾᏍᏗ, … ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᏥᎩ, ᏳᏓᎭ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎾᏩᏓᏅ,ᏖᏗ, ᏤᏥᏲᎮᎰ “If I don’t think what I’m going to say first,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎰ “ᎠᏏᏅᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᏱᏂ,ᏥᏫ,” ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎰ “ᎤᏟᏍᏗ ᏱᏩᎩᏁᏣ,” ᎨᏥᏲᎮᎰ
segments.transliteration: ilvhiyu na itselisesgo, atsalagi, yvwi, yuwonisa, tla yawanv,ta, itsaga,sestanv yigi, sgi nigehvna, itsaga,sestanvi ilvhiyu tsalagi, ani--kali tsalagi, aniwonisgi, anedohv itsedohv … yuniwonisa, “He” yanada, squu ageya yaninohe tsanv,ta, ilvhiyu asgaya yaninohe “She” dina,diho nanv, squu aga,dvhvstanvi, hena, yinaniwa, nigada,’dv aniyvwiya sgi nunasdi, … ayv, hena, squu tsigi, yudaha squu sgina nawadanv,tedi, tsetsiyoheho “If I don’t think what I’m going to say first,” gatsiyoheho “asinvda, hena, yini,tsiwi,” gatsiyoheho “utlisdi yiwaginetsa,” getsiyoheho
segments.translation: Have you all noticed that when a Cherokee speaks—I don’t know if y’all’ve noticed, if not, next time pay attention—when a full-blood Cherokee speaks English, they say “He,” when they’re talking about a woman. And when they talk about a man, they say “She.” They say it backwards. And it’s all the Cherokee that does that. That happens to me, too. If I don’t think about what I’m going to say, "If I don’t’ think about what I’m going to say, first,” I tell people. “I’ll say it backwards. If I talk too fast,” I tell them.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: If you talked about Mitch, you’re going to say “She.” [laughs]

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: “She interviewed me,” I’m gonna say.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᎩᏂᏭᏗ, Ꮳ--ᏣᏁᎲ ᎠᏂ-Wolfe ᏭᏂᏍᏕᏢ ᎡᏘᏴ ᎠᏁᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏃᏭ, ᎠᏁᏙᎯ, ᎯᎢ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨᎢ’Ꮫ ᏑᏌᏂ, ᏥᏚᏙᎥ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, … ᏌᏭ ᎡᎲ ᎠᏧᏣ, ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏔᏅᎢ, “Hotshot” ᎠᏃᏎᎲ ᏂᎪᎯ,Ꮈ ᎠᏗᏔᎯᏙᎯ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏧᏣ’Ꮽ, ᏍᏊ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᏄᏓᎴ ᏩᏂᏯᏂᎲ ᏩᏥᏍᏚᎲᏍᎬ ᏧᎾᏓᏍᏚᏗ … ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᏃᏭ, ᏗᏂ,ᏓᏂᏱᏍᎩ, ᏃᏭ, ᎪᎨᎲᏎ Hotshot-Ꭲ’Ꮫ ᏓᏂᏲᎯᎲᏛ ᏃᏭ, ᎤᏥ ᏫᎤᎷᏣ, ᏃᏭ, ᎣᏂ, ᏗᏢ, ᎠᎾᏝᎢᏢ ᏗᏂ,ᏓᏂᏱᏍᎩ, “Where you take my boy?” – “Oh, we gotta take him to jail,” – “How come?” – “He’s drunk.” ᏃᏭ ᎤᏂ,ᏘᏂᏫ,ᏛᎲᎢ, … ᏃᏭ ᏗᏓᎾᏅ ᎩᏂᏭᏗ, ᏳᏁᎦ, ᎤᏓᎾᏅᏅ ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎪᎵ,Ꭼ ᎤᏂᎪᏗ, ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ, ᎩᏂᏭᏗ, ᎠᏎ ᎤᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ, ᏧᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ’Ꮫ … ᎤᏴᏟᏢ “I’m Ms. Wolfe,” ᎾᏅ “What can I do for you today, Ms. Wolfe?” – “I want phone.” – “Right there it is!” – “I want use phone.” – “Go ahead!” … “ᎤᏡᏢ” ᏣᏗᎲ “Hello, Jail,” ᏭᏛᏅ ᏣᏓ,
segments.transliteration: na squu giniwudi, tsa--tsanehv ani-Wolfe wunisdetlv etiyv anehv aseno nowu, anedohi, hii agayvligei’dv susani, tsidudov atsalagi, … sawu ehv atsutsa, udvhistanvi, “Hotshot” anosehv nigohi,lv aditahidohi, tsigehv atsutsa’wu, squu tsigehv gayu,la, nudale waniyanihv watsisduhvsgv tsunadasdudi … sawu yuwaga,da, nowu, dini,daniyisgi, nowu, gogehvse Hotshot-i’dv daniyohihvdv nowu, utsi wiulutsa, nowu, oni, ditlv, anatlaitlv dini,daniyisgi, “Where you take my boy?” – “Oh, we gotta take him to jail,” – “How come?” – “He’s drunk.” nowu uni,tiniwi,dvhvi, … nowu didananv giniwudi, yunega, udananvnv asenv, atsalagi, goli,gv unigodi, anitsalagi, giniwudi, ase udelo,quasdi, tsuli,stanv’dv … uyvtlitlv “I’m Ms. Wolfe,” nanv “What can I do for you today, Ms. Wolfe?” – “I want phone.” – “Right there it is!” – “I want use phone.” – “Go ahead!” … “utlutlv” tsadihv “Hello, Jail,” wudvnv tsada,
segments.translation: Those Wolfes that live in Kenwood …But [they’re] the ones that came later. There was an old woman, her Cherokee name was Susan(i). She had one boy that she raised, they called him Hotshot. He was always out drinking. Even when he was a young boy, he was already getting locked up in jail. One time, the police chased him and they were shooting at him. When he got to his mom’s all the police pulled up. “Where do you take my boy?” she said. “Oh, we gotta take him to jail,” they said. “How come?” she asked. “’Cause he’s drunk,” they said. They took him. There was a store in Kenwood, owned by a White man. But he understood Cherokee, since there were a lot of Cherokee there he had to have learned it. She went into the store and said, “I’m Ms. Wolfe.” He asked her, “What can I do for you today, Ms. Wolfe?” “I want a phone,” she said. “Right there it is!” he said. – “I want to use the phone.” “Go ahead!” he said. She picked up the phone and said, “Hello, jail?”
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᎤᎦ,ᏛᎲᏍᎬ ᎯᎳᎦ ᏙᏓᏳᎬᏩᎳᏂᏏᏒ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎥᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎠᏛᎩᏍᎬ ᏳᏁᎦ, ᎤᏓᎾᏅ ᎤᏬᎵ,Ꮧ ᏧᏰᎸᏒ ᏳᏃᎮᏝ,
segments.transliteration: nanv uga,dvhvsgv hilaga dodayugvwalanisisv (uniyetsi,sgv) nigohilv vsgi yusdi, advgisgv yunega, udananv uwoli,di tsuyelvsv yunohetla,
segments.translation: She was wanting to know how much it was going to cost her son. [laughter] He always heard these kinds of stories, the White storeowner. He was always laughing about it.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Haw.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᏅ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, ᎦᏏ, ᏧᏙᎢᏓ, ᏦᏥᏃᎮᎲ motor ᏥᎦᎴᏍᎬ ᏙᏆᎴᎵ ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᏍᏊ ᎤᎴᏓ, ᎨᎲ motor ᎠᏭ, ᎤᎲ … “ᎦᏏ, ᎢᏎ ᎠᏍᏗ ᎬᏭ ᎩᎾᏒᏁ ᎠᎪᏎᎸ ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ, -- “Ꮩ’ᎢᏳᎭ?” -- ᎠᏓᏅ,ᏖᏢᏍᎬ’Ꮫ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏃᏭ ᏙᏆᎴᎵ ᏭᏣᏅ ᎦᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᎦ,ᏐᏍᎬᎢ ᏃᏭ ᏭᎦ,ᏐᏒ ᏅᏃᎯ, ᎤᏠᎸ ᏣᏓ, ᎩᎶ ᎤᏠᎸ“’ᏙᏭ ᎦᏏ?” – “ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎦ’Ꮫ ᎠᎩ,--ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏆᏃᏴᏟ,ᏍᏙᏗ” Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, motor ᏱᎦᏞ ᏙᏳ, ᏚᏳᎪ,Ꮫ Ꮒ,ᎬᏪᏍᎬ “ᎮᏍᏗ, ᎮᎾ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏯᏛᏁ ‘ᎠᏭ’ ᏱᎾᏮᏁᎳ, switch,” ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ, ᏚᏳᎪ,Ꮫ ᎧᏃᎮᏍᎬ Ꮭ motor ᏱᎦᏞ “ᎭᏢᏴ ᏫᎦ,Ꮨ,?” – “ᎠᏭ ᏗᏓᎾᏅ ᏥᎦᏘ,” – “ᎭᏩ ᎡᎵᏭ’Ꮫ ᏱᎬᏯᏌᏙᎯᏓ, ᎢᎾᏰ” … ᎠᏥᏌᏙᏱᏙᎸ ᏗᏓᎾᏅ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, … ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏭᏓᎾ,ᏁᏒᎲᏅ ᏃᏭ ᏙᏱ ᏗᏢ ᎦᏍᎩᎸ ᎢᎦᏓ, ᏧᎾ,ᏛᏐᏅ ᎤᎾᏅᏗ ᎾᏅ ᏭᏣᎾ, ᎦᏏ, ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎤᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬ ᎤᏍᏆᏃᏴᏟ,ᏍᏙᏗ ᏕᎪᏎᎮ’Ꮫ “ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏆᏃᏴᏟ,ᏍᏙᏗ ᏙᏆᎴᎳ” – “Well, ᏲᏣᏁᎵ,Ꮧ ᎢᏨᏯᏌᏙᏯ,” – “ᎥᎥ!” … ᎤᏂᏌᏙᏴ ᎦᏏᏅᏓ, ᏅᏃᎯ, ᏃᏭ, ᎤᏂᎷᏣ, ᎤᏂᏌᏙᏴ ᏏᏭ’Ꮫ Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᎮ ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ ᎩᎶ ᎤᏠᎸ “’ᏙᏭ ᎦᏏ,?” – “ᎣᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬ’Ꮫ ᏦᏥᏍᏆᏃᏴᏟ,ᏍᏗᎲ” – “ᎭᏩ ᏱᎬᏯᏌᏙᏯ’Ꮫ!” ᎠᎪᏎᎸ ᏧᏪᏅᏒ ᏫᎦᏯᏌᏙᏱᏢᎢ, ᏣᏓ, motor ᏂᎦᏢᎾ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᎤᏣᎥ
segments.transliteration: nanv sawu yuwaga,da, gasi, tsudoida, tsotsinohehv motor tsigalesgv doqualeli gayu,la, squu uleda, gehv motor awu, uhv … “gasi, ise asdi gvwu ginasvne agoselv usdayvhvsgi, -- “do’iyuha?” -- adanv,tetlvsgv’dv nowunv nowu doqualeli wutsanv gasi tsigehv gaga,sosgvi nowu wuga,sosv nvnohi, utlolv tsada, gilo utlolv“’dowu gasi?” – “aginulvhvsga’dv agi,--agi,squanoyvtli,sdodi” tla hena, motor yigatle doyu, duyugo,dv ni,gvwesgv “hesdi, hena, gohu,sdi, yadvne ‘awu’ yinawvnela, switch,” doyu, hena, duyugo,dv kanohesgv tla motor yigatle “hatlvyv wiga,ti,?” – “awu didananv tsigati,” – “hawa eliwu’dv yigvyasadohida, inaye” … atsisadoyidolv didananv yigohida, … nowu’nv, wudana,nesvhvnv nowu doyi ditlv gasgilv igada, tsuna,dvsonv unanvdi nanv wutsana, gasi, asenv, unulvhvsgv usquanoyvtli,sdodi degosehe’dv “aginulvhvsgv agi,squanoyvtli,sdodi doqualela” – “Well, yotsaneli,di itsvyasadoya,” – “vv!” … unisadoyv gasinvda, nvnohi, nowu, unilutsa, unisadoyv siwu’dv tla gohu,sdi, yini,gali,sdihe nowu’dv gilo utlolv “’dowu gasi,?” – “oginulvhvsgv’dv tsotsisquanoyvtli,sdihv” – “hawa yigvyasadoya’dv!” agoselv tsuwenvsv wigayasadoyitlvi, tsada, motor nigatlvna, nowule utsav
segments.translation: Also, one time we were talking about him—his name was Gas(i). He was taking a motor out of a truck. He had already taken the motor out, and it was sitting by him. His wife said, “Gas(i) we’re running out of flour.” “Really?” [he asked] Then he thought about it. Then he got in the truck and went down the hill all the way to the road. Somebody pulled up and asked him, “What’s wrong, Gas(i)?” He said, “I can’t get the truck started!” Because there wasn’t a motor in it! And he was telling the truth! He said, “It’s not making a sound when I turn the key.” He was telling the truth, there was no motor in it. “Where you headed?” they asked. “Just over to the store,” he said. “Alright, I can probably push your truck there!” they said. And they pushed him all the way to the store. He went and bought what he needed. And outside there was a bench where the old men sit. Gas(i) got in the truck and he was telling the men that he couldn’t get it to start. “I can’t get it to start,” he said. “Well, we’ll try to push you!” they said. They pushed him going backward. When they got to the road they pushed him again, but it still didn’t do anything. Then after a while, somebody pulled up, “What’s wrong, Gas(i)?” “We can’t get it to start!” he said. “Alright, I’ll push you!” he told Gas(i). They pushed him all the way home. There wasn’t a motor inside it.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᎵ ᏗᏓᎾᏅ ᏭᏪᏙᎸ … ᏧᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ ᏥᎧᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏍᏊ … ᏥᏍᏓᏗᎲ ᏏᏭ’Ꭸ ᏍᏗᏫᏒᏍᎪ?
segments.transliteration: eli didananv wuwedolv … tsuyetsi,sgv tsikanohesgv squu … tsisdadihv siwu’ge sdiwisvsgo?
segments.translation: He went to the store anyway. He was really laughing, talking about it. What you all were talking about, do you still garden?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Not me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You don’t plant anymore.

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: I’m too lazy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) Ꮎ’Ꭱ [Mack] ᏧᏪᏅᏒ ᏫᏛᎯᏙᎰ … ᎪᎯ, ᏥᏗᏃᎮᏍᎬ “ᎠᏣᎳᎩ,” ᏳᏛᎾ, ᎩᎶ … ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ, ᏫᏍᏓᏓᏅ,ᏖᏍᎪ? … ᏱᏍᏓᏓᏅ,ᏖᏝ “ᎠᏣᎳᎩ,” ᏳᏛᎾ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᏳᏂᏃᎮᏝ, ‘ᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏗ, ᏫᏍᏓᏓᏅ,ᏖᏍᎪ? Ꮎ’Ꭸ ᎪᎯ ᏥᏗᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎦᏚᎩ, ᏥᏕᎬ ‘Ꮲ ᏱᏚᎾ,ᏓᏂᎶᏌ, ᏱᎩ, ᎩᎶ’Ꮄ ᏁᎲᎾ, ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ,
segments.transliteration: (uyetsi,sgv) na’e [Mack] tsuwenvsv widvhidoho … gohi, tsidinohesgv “atsalagi,” yudvna, gilo … ‘do usdi, wisdadanv,tesgo? … yisdadanv,tetla “atsalagi,” yudvna, atsalagi, yuninohetla, ‘dohv usdi, wisdadanv,tesgo? na’ge gohi tsidinohesgv yusdi, gadugi, tsidegv ‘tlv yiduna,danilosa, yigi, gilo’le nehvna, yinuli,stana,
segments.translation: [laughs] You go visit him [Mack] at his house. Earlier we were talking about it, if somebody says “Cherokee” what does that make you think about? When you think about when they say “I’m a Cherokee.” When they talk about Cherokees, what do you all think about? Or like earlier—when we were talking about everybody got together when people got sick or when somebody died.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏓᎾ,ᏓᏟᏏᏍᎪ ᏙᏳ ᎪᎯᏗ, -- ᎪᎯᎢᎦ, ᎮᎾ, ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, ᎩᎶ ᏳᏲᎱᏌ, ᏞᎦ,Ꮽ, ᏱᏩᎴᎲᎦ … Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᏱᏪᏙᎯ, ᏦᎢᎭ’Ꮫ ᏅᎩᎭ ᏒᎾ,ᏙᏓᏩᏍᏗ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᎠᎾᏅᏍᎬ, ᎨᎲ ᏙᏱ, ᎠᏃᏛᏍᎬ … ᎯᎢ’Ꮓ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᏍᏗ,
segments.transliteration: dana,datlisisgo doyu gohidi, -- gohiiga, hena, gohi tsigi, gilo yuyohusa, tlega,wu, yiwalehvga … tla gilo yiwedohi, tsoiha’dv nvgiha svna,dodawasdi,’le yigi, yigohida, ananvsgv, gehv doyi, anodvsgv … hii’no tla sgi yinusdi,
segments.translation: Yeah, they all gathered there back then. And today, if someone dies they’ll just come and stay a little while. And then there’ll be nobody there. They would stay three or four [nights] or a week and sit around a big fire outside. It’s not like that anymore.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎲ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᎡᏘᏴ ᎢᏗᏣᎳᎩ, ᏙᎲ? ᎢᏗᏣᎳᎩ,
segments.transliteration: dohv tsinusdv etiyv iditsalagi, dohv? iditsalagi,
segments.translation: That’s the way it was, way back, for us Cherokees.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎢᏳᏍᏗᎲᏭ ᏥᎩ, ᎤᏓᏁᏟᏴᏒ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ, … … ᎤᎾ,ᏓᏅᏖᏗ’Ꮫ ᏥᎩ, ᏴᏫ, ᏄᏓᎴ ᏄᏍᏗ, ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ,
segments.transliteration: iyusdihvwu tsigi, udanetliyvsv gohi tsigi, … … una,danvtedi’dv tsigi, yvwi, nudale nusdi, gohi tsigi,
segments.translation: Everything has changed nowadays. People think differently today.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏴᏛᎾ, ᏥᏓᏗᎲ … ᎮᏍᏗ, Ꮎ ᏍᏓᏱ ᏗᏗᏍᏚᎲᏍᎬ ᏗᎦᎶᎯᏍᏗ ᎡᏘᏴ ᏙᎲ Ꮭ?
segments.transliteration: yvdvna, tsidadihv … hesdi, na sdayi didisduhvsgv digalohisdi etiyv dohv tla?
segments.translation: Like we were saying, we didn’t lock our doors back then.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Uh uh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏭᎴ ᏦᏦᏛᏍᎬ ᏑᎾᎴ ᏥᎨᎲ … bucket ᏥᎦᏙ
segments.transliteration: nowule tsotsodvsgv sunale tsigehv … bucket tsigado
segments.translation: And when it was the morning we built a fire. There was a bucket hanging.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎠᎹ, ᎦᏂᏱᏙᏗ, ᏓᏅ-Ꮣ-Ꮣ-ᏓᏅᏗᏰᏍᎬ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏓᏅ,ᎩᎶᏍᎬ ᏧᏅ,ᏙᏗ … ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᎮᎾ, ᎦᎧᎲ ᏯᏩᏚᎵ ᎮᎾ, Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏄᏅᏁᎸ … ᎠᎢ’Ꮕ wringer ᏱᎬᏓ, ᏣᎲ ᏕᎦᎦᏙᏍᏙ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᏒ Ꭱ-Ꭱ-ᎡᏠᎩ ᏓᏅ,-ᏓᏅ--ᏓᏅ,ᎩᎶᏍᎬ
segments.transliteration: ama, ganiyidodi, danv-da-da-danvdiyesgv nowule danv,gilosgv tsunv,dodi … adanelv hena, gakahv yawaduli hena, tla yawanv,ta, nunvnelv … ai’nv wringer yigvda, tsahv degagadosdo etsi tsigesv e-e-etlogi danv,-danv--danv,gilosgv
segments.translation: To catch water with. They used it to wash dishes and do laundry with. There was one at the house. I was wanting it. But I don’t know what they did with it. It had a wringer on it. I used to watch my mom and my aunt washing clothes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏭᎴ’Ꮓ ᏗᏦᏠ,Ꮧ, … ᏥᏕ--ᏥᏚᏂᎰ tubs ᏙᎲ? ᏥᏚᏂ,ᏦᏠ
segments.transliteration: nowule’no ditsotlo,di, … tside--tsiduniho tubs dohv? tsiduni,tsotlo
segments.translation: They also had conjoined tubs. They were conjoined.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎠᏴ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎬᏱ ᏔᎵ,--ᏔᎵ, ᎢᎦ ᎠᎹᎭ and then ᎪᎢ-ᎪᎢ-ᎪᎢ--ᎣᏟ ᎮᎾ, … ᎠᏴ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᏓᏁᎸ Ꮭ we didn’t have no running water. ᎣᏍᏛ ‘Ꮲ ᏔᎵ,Ꮪ - ᏦᎦᏚ ’ᎸᏢ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎩᎳ, well-Ꭲ pump ᏂᎬᏁᎰ ᎨᎲ ᏩᏟ,ᎧᎵᏴᎲ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ tank ᏂᎬᏁ ᏙᏱ ᎤᎾ,ᏨᏍᏗ ᎧᏂᎩᏓ ᎨᎲ T.V. ᎠᎬᏱ electric ᎠᎬᏱ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ Ꮟ-Ꮟ ᎮᎾ, -- ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, Ꮟ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ Ꮧ-…ᏗᏨᏱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎪᎢ ᏗᏟᏍᏗ, ᎪᎢ ᎤᏴᏜ, ᏗᏟᏍᏙᏗ, ᏙᏨ,ᏗᎰ ᎨᎲ … ᎪᎯ’ᏅᏴ ᏥᎩ, Ꮭ Ᏹ’ᎠᎯᎪᏩᏔ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᏣᏛᏂ… ᏏᎵ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎬᏱ T.V. electric-Ꭲ Ꮕ’Ꭱ ᏗᎨᎬᏁᎸ Zenith T.V. ᏥᎨᎲ black and white ᎤᏂᎧᎮ ᏧᏅ,ᎩᎶᏍᏗ,’Ꭱ ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, Boy, ᎧᎵ’Ꮫ ᎣᏥᏯ’Ꭳ ᎨᎲ ᏦᏥᏲᏟ … ᎡᎳᏗ, ᎣᏣᏅᏍᎪ ᎣᏣᏝᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏧᎾ,ᏔᏂ’Ꮓ ᏗᎦᏍᎩᎶᎢ “ᎢᏥᏁᏍᏗ’Ꮕ ᏞᏍᏗ, ᏙᏣᎴᏅᎢ Ꭰ’ᎥᏱ ᏗᏢ, ᏂᏣᏛᏁ,Ꮧ,” ᎠᎾ,ᏗᏍᎬ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) The Lawrence Welk [Show] ᎤᎾ,ᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ, ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayv hena, agvyi tali,--tali, iga amaha and then goi-goi-goi--otli hena, … ayv hena, adanelv tla we didn’t have no running water. osdv ‘tlv tali,du - tsogadu ’lvtlv yawadetiyvda, gehv gila, well-i pump nigvneho gehv watli,kaliyvhv gali,tsode tank nigvne doyi una,tsvsdi kanigida gehv T.V. agvyi electric agvyi nuli,stanv si-si hena, -- ayv, hena, si ganvdadisgo di-…ditsvyi,sdi, goi ditlisdi, goi uyvdla, ditlisdodi, dotsv,diho gehv … gohi’nvyv tsigi, tla yi’ahigowata, gohu,sdi sgina yitsadvni… sili hena, agvyi T.V. electric-i nv’e digegvnelv Zenith T.V. tsigehv black and white unikahe tsunv,gilosdi,’e yinuli,stana, Boy, kali’dv otsiya’o gehv tsotsiyotli … eladi, otsanvsgo otsatlanvdadisgo tsuna,tani’no digasgiloi “itsinesdi’nv tlesdi, dotsalenvi a’vyi ditlv, nitsadvne,di,” ana,disgv (uniyetsi,sgv) The Lawrence Welk [Show] una,dvdasdodi, gehv
segments.translation: We had two. One was for water and the other was for soap. We didn’t have no running water at our house. I was probably about 12 or 13 years old when we got a well that would pump water into the house. It filled up from a tank. But we didn’t have plumbing. When the TV first came out, I still remember it. We were still using kerosene lamps. Nowadays, you probably can’t see anything if you used them. Celi was the first to get electric. They got a Zenith TV, it was a black and white. TV Man, on Friday nights, there’d be a houseful there. Us, children, we used to sit on the floor so the adults could sit in the chairs. They’d tell us, “Don’t be getting up. Or we won’t be able to see the TV” [Laughter] They were listening to the Lawrence Welk Show.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah. Mhmm.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ that was my favorite, [The] Lawerence Welk [Show.]
segments.transliteration: sgina that was my favorite, [The] Lawerence Welk [Show.]
segments.translation: That was my favorite, Lawrence Welk.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏎᎵ,’Ꮫ Ꮭ ᏱᎦᎬᏅᏗ ᎨᎲ , Lawrence Welk. ᎾᏛ ᏱᏗᎦᏂ ᎦᏂᏍᏓ
segments.transliteration: seli,’dv tla yigagvnvdi gehv , Lawrence Welk. nadv yidigani ganisda
segments.translation: Celi wouldn’t miss Lawrence Welk. [unclear].

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: I used to like that Hee Haw. [show]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꮓ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏊ ᏙᏱ, ᏥᏓᏅ,ᎩᎶᏍᎬ ᏧᏁᎦ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎿᏬ ᏙᎲ? I mean, … ᏧᏁᎦ Ꮒ,ᏕᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᎲ
segments.transliteration: no’nv, squu doyi, tsidanv,gilosgv tsunega’dv tsigehv dihnawo dohv? I mean, … tsunega ni,degali,sdihv
segments.translation: When they used to wash outside, the clothes were really white, isn’t that right? I mean really white.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏭᎴ ᏍᏊ ᏱᏚᏅ,ᎩᎶᎠ, ᏓᏏᎳ,Ꮫ’Ꭸ ᏕᏥᏢᏍᎬ ᏗᎿᏬ ᏕᏥᎧᏲᏗᎲ?
segments.transliteration: nowule squu yidunv,giloa, dasila,dv’ge detsitlvsgv dihnawo detsikayodihv?
segments.translation: Also, when they washed, were you all putting the clothes on the fence to dry?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎤᏂᏏᎳ,ᏙᎸ ᎨᎲ ‘ᎸᏢ ᏱᏍᎩᏭ ᏱᏄᏓᎶ ᎨᎲ ᏐᎢ ᎢᏡ,Ꭼ Ꮎ--Ꭰ…Ꭰ..—Chinatown-Ꮽ ᎡᎵᏍᏗ, ᏄᏍᏙ ᎨᎲ (ᎤᏂᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏗᎿᏬ ᏥᏕᎦᏖᎳ,Ꮫ
segments.transliteration: unisila,dolv gehv ‘lvtlv yisgiwu yinudalo gehv soi itlu,gv na--a…a..—Chinatown-wu elisdi, nusdo gehv (uniyetsi,sgv) dihnawo tsidegatela,dv
segments.translation: They used to have a clothes line, they had it hooked to a tree. It was like Chinatown [laughter] with clothes hanging everywhere.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏙᏳ’ᏛᎲ ᏚᏓᎴᎿᎥ ᏃᏭ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎩ,
segments.transliteration: Yeah, doyu’dvhv dudalehnav nowu gohiyv tsigi,
segments.translation: Yeah, it really has changed since then.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꮟ ᎠᏴ, ᎠᎩᎭ, ᏌᏭ ᏍᎩᎾ sewin--…washing machines.
segments.transliteration: si ayv, agiha, sawu sgina sewin--…washing machines.
segments.translation: I still have one of those sewin… washing machines.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.text: Ꮭ’Ᏺ ᏱᎬᏗᎰ ᎠᏎᏅ, (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) … ᎪᎯᏗ, ᎾᎩᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.transliteration: tla’yo yigvdiho asenv, (uyetsi,sgv) … gohidi, nagiho sgina
segments.translation: I don’t use it, though. [laughs] I’ve had it a long time.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Is that true?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎾᎮ … ᏭᏟ ᏗᏢ, ᏥᏥᏁᎸ Ꮟ Ꮎ’ᎢᏂᏱᏍᎬᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎠᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᏍᏊ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᎠᎩᎲ ᎪᎳ, ᏱᎩ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᎬᏗᏍᎬ … Boy, Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, you can’t beat it, ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ, ᏚᏯ ᎦᏚ’ᎢᏅ, ᏗᎬᎲᏍᏔᏅ… Ꮟ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ Ꮟ ‘ᎸᎯᏳ ᏙᏱ ᏱᎦᏓᏍᏓᎲᏍᎪ ᏩᏮᏲ ᎤᏩᏖᏌᏗ, it just tastes a lot different ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮕ ᏱᎩ, … ᏕᏥᏍᏆᎵ,ᏍᏗᎲ ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ, ᎤᏂᎷᏣ, ᏙᏱ ᏗᏢ, ᎦᏓᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ ᎦᏥᏰᎶᎸ … ᎾᏂᎦ,ᏔᎲᎾ, ᎤᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ Ꮎ ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ, … ᎠᏴ, ᏥᏓᎩᎸᏫ,ᏍᏓᏁᎯ, … ᎤᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᏳᏍᏆᎸᎭ, ᏧᏂ-…ᏓᏂᏃᎭᎵᏙᎯ, ᏳᏂᎷᏣ, … ᎭᏢ’ᎢᏭ ᏗᎨᏙᎲ tractor ᎪᎯᏴ ᎩᎶ ᏗᎩᎸ ᏱᎬᎩᏯᎾ, “ᎭᏓᏍᏓᏴᎭ!” ᏯᎾᏓ, ᏃᏭ’Ꭱ ᎨᏥᏯᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: nahe … wutli ditlv, tsitsinelv si na’iniyisgvna, tsigehv … ada, hena, squu adasdayv,di agihv gola, yigi, sgina gvdisgv … Boy, tla hena, you can’t beat it, sgi nusdv adasdayv,di, duya gadu’inv, digvhvstanv… si adanelv si ‘lvhiyu doyi yigadasdahvsgo wawvyo uwatesadi, it just tastes a lot different sgi nusdv adasdayv,nv yigi, … detsisquali,sdihv anigeyutsa, unilutsa, doyi ditlv, gadasdayvhvsgv gatsiyelolv … naniga,tahvna, una,dasdayv,di na tsuna,tana, … ayv, tsidagilvwi,sdanehi, … una,dasdayv,di yusqualvha, tsuni-…daninohalidohi, yunilutsa, … hatlv’iwu digedohv tractor gohiyv gilo digilv yigvgiyana, “hadasdayvha!” yanada, nowu’e getsiyasdayvhvsgo
segments.translation: When I used to live somewhere else, before I got arrested, I had a woodstove. I still have a woodstove and I use it when it’s wintertime. You can’t beat it, cooking beans and cornbread on it. At the house, sometimes I cook outside and I have a pan that I cook them in. It’s just tastes a lot different if it’s cooked outside. My granddaughters couldn’t believe it when they came and I was cooking outside and that’s what I fed them. They don’t know how to cook—their parents. When I was working, when they had to cook, like when the hunters came. They would come get me on a tractor to come and cook for them. So I would cook for them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Things have really changed, haven’t they?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Yeah. … ᎯᏑᎵ,ᎪᎢ Eddie! Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏓ ᎬᏙᏗ ᏱᎩ ᎭᏓᏅᏖᏍᏗᎨᏍᏗ ᎪᎯᏴ
segments.transliteration: Yeah. … hisuli,goi Eddie! tla gusda gvdodi yigi hadanvtesdigesdi gohiyv
segments.translation: Yeah. …Quit it, Eddie! What you’re thinking about ain’t worth nothing later.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᏥᏣᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᏰᏤᏠᎳ, ᎢᎸᎯᏳ’Ꭸ water gravy ᎯᎩᏍᎨ?
segments.transliteration: na’e tsitsadvsidisv yetsetlola, ilvhiyu’ge water gravy higisge?
segments.translation: When you were growing up, when they fed y’all, did you all eat water gravy?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: Yeah, all the time.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Even still today.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Boy, ᏙᏳ ᎤᏖᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ? ᎦᏚ ᏳᎾ,ᏗᏞᎩ’Ꮓ ᎠᏅ,ᏗᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: Boy, doyu utedi, gehv dohv? gadu yuna,ditlegi’no anv,digo tsigehv
segments.translation: Boy, it was really good. Wasn’t it? They eat it with a hot biscuit.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Waterbiscuits’ᎾᎲ ᏥᏓᏃᏢᏍᎪ ᎪᎯᏓ, ᏧᎭᎨᏛ, … ᎠᏴ,’Ꭱ ᎦᏚ ᏱᏚᏅᏂᏍᏔᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ … *ᎯᎢ* ᏥᏂ,ᎦᏛ … Bibi’Ꭱ ᏥᎨᎲ -- Bibi ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎪ--ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏧᎦ,ᏎᏍᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎧᎵ,ᏎᏥ’Ꮕ, Ꮿ--Ꮞ’ᎠᏨ ᎧᎵ,ᏎᏥ, ᏱᏙᎩᎥᏌ, ᏥᎨᎲ … Ꮎ ᎦᏚ ᏫᏚᏘᏴ “ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ Ꮣ-ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᎧᎵ,ᏎᏥᎢ ᏙᏓᏨᏁᎵ,” ᏯᏓ ᎨᎲ … Bibi ᏥᎨᎲ ᎦᏚ ᏧᏘᏴ ᏱᏓ’ᎥᎭᎷᏱ, ᎨᎲ *ᎯᎢ* ᏗᎩᏓ, ᏱᏂᏕᎬᎦ, ᎨᎲ … ᎧᎵᏎᏥ’Ꮕ ᎠᎹ ᎠᏑᏴ ᏱᏓᏑᏴᎦ, ᎨᎲ ᎪᎢ ᏱᏫ,ᏚᏮᏂᏍᏓ, ᎨᎲ to get that glaze. ᎧᎵ,ᏎᏥ, ᏂᎦᎵ,Ꮝ-- Boy, ᎣᏣᏅ,Ꮫ “ᎧᎵ,ᏎᏥ, ᏙᏥᎩ” ᎣᏤᎵᏍᎬ ᎦᏚ’Ꮽ ᎧᎵ,ᏎᏥ, ᏩᏑᏴᏅ Ꮩ-Ꮩ--ᏕᎬᏂᏍᏗᏍᎪ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏂᏖᏗ, ᏍᎩᎾ,’Ᏺ ᎨᏒ
segments.transliteration: Waterbiscuits’nahv tsidanotlvsgo gohida, tsuhagedv, … ayv,’e gadu yidunvnistana, tsigehv … *hii* tsini,gadv … Bibi’e tsigehv -- Bibi hena, tsigehv nigo--diniyotli, nigohilv tsuga,sesdi, tsigehv … kali,setsi’nv, ya--se’atsv kali,setsi, yidogivsa, tsigehv … na gadu widutiyv “ayv’dv da-ayv’dv kali,setsii dodatsvneli,” yada gehv … Bibi tsigehv gadu tsutiyv yida’vhaluyi, gehv *hii* digida, yinidegvga, gehv … kalisetsi’nv ama asuyv yidasuyvga, gehv goi yiwi,duwvnisda, gehv to get that glaze. kali,setsi, nigali,s-- Boy, otsanv,dv “kali,setsi, dotsigi” otselisgv gadu’wu kali,setsi, wasuyvnv do-do--degvnisdisgo gehv unitedi, sgina,’yo gesv
segments.translation: They used to make water biscuits. When they cooked bread, when I was about this [gestures] tall. The late Bib(i). She always had to watch the children. They hardly every gave us candy. The left over bread, Bibi would say, “I’m going to give y’all some candy.” The leftover bread she would cut them up to this [gestures] size. And she would put the bread in sugared water, then she’d fry them to get that glaze. Boy we really thought we were eating candy! And it was just bread. She was putting sugar with it and cooking it. They were really good.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Did she bake them? Or what was it?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎥᎥ she’d fry them. ᎾᏅ ᎧᎵ,ᏎᏥ, when you fry it, ᎤᏗᏞᎩ, ᏱᏂ,ᏨᏁᎳ, ᏍᏓᏱ ᎮᎾ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓ,
segments.transliteration: vv she’d fry them. nanv kali,setsi, when you fry it, uditlegi, yini,tsvnela, sdayi hena, yusdi, yini,gali,sda,
segments.translation: She’d fry them. When you fry sugar, it hardens.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: And it turns like a glaze.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᏚ’ᎢᏅ, it’d kinda have a little crunch to it. ᎤᏖᏗ’Ꮫ ᎥᎾᎾ
segments.transliteration: sgina gadu’inv, it’d kinda have a little crunch to it. utedi’dv vnana
segments.translation: Then that bread would kind of have a little crunch to it. It was really good.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᏩᏕᏘᏱᏍᎬ--ᎣᎩᎾ,ᏕᏘᏱᏍᎬ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᎥᎩᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ … ᎦᏚ ᏥᏫ,ᎦᏢᏍᎬ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ--
segments.transliteration: nawadetiyisgv--ogina,detiyisgv’le yigi, vgido tsigehv nowu … gadu tsiwi,gatlvsgv etsi tsigehv na--
segments.translation: On my birthday, or on our birthdays—my sister. My mom would put bread in a --

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: --a square pan?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏭᎴ’Ꮓ … ᎤᎦᎾᏍᏗ, ‘ᏙᏛ ᎤᏍᏗ, ᏥᎬ,ᏗᏍᎬ? … Syrup-Ꭲ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏍᏗ ᎦᏚ ᏥᏩᏢᏍᎬ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᎡᏘᏴ ᏧᏍᏓᎷᎩᏍᎩ, ᏤᎲ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ … ᏗᏆᏲᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᏳᏍᏗ, Ꮎ ᎦᏚ ᏩᏢᏍᎬ *ᎯᎢ* ᏍᏊ ᏱᎩᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᏛ’Ꮓ Ꭳ-ᎣᎩᎾ,ᏕᏘᏱᏍᎬ’Ꭱ ᏃᏭ’Ꮫ ᏦᏍᏗᎩᏍᎬ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎣᏍᏓ ᏦᎩᏂᏰᎸᏒ ᎤᎦᎾᏍᏗ, ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏍᏊ’Ꮫ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏳᏃᏢᎾ, ᎠᏎ’Ꮫ ᎣᎩᏂᎩᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ ᏃᎩᏂᎬᎾ, ᏱᎩ, “ᏍᏛᏌ’Ꮽ ᏍᏕᎵᏍᏗ,” ᎣᎩᏃᏒ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᏊ “ᎠᎪᎾ, ᏍᏛᏁᏍᏗ, ᏂᎯ, ᏍᏕᎵᏍᏗ, ᎨᎮᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏥᎦ-ᏥᎦᎵ-ᏥᎬᏂᏍᏔᏅᏍᎬ, … ᎾᎩᏤᎲᎾ, ᏱᎦ ᎢᎦ ᎬᏗᎰ” ᏣᏗᏍᎬ, ᏥᎨᎲ … “ᏂᏣᎬᎾ, ᏱᎨᎮᏍᏗ, ᏱᏣᏲ--ᏱᏣᏲᏏᏍᎨᏍᏗ, ᎪᎯᏴ’Ꮓ ᏂᎯ ᏨᏂᏯ,ᏌᏗ ᎨᏎᏍᏗ,” ᎠᏗᎲ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᏙᏳ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏓᎾ,ᏓᏪᏎᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ? ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎩ, ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏓᎾ,ᏛᏍᎬ ᎠᏎ’Ꮫ--
segments.transliteration: nowule’no … uganasdi, ‘dodv usdi, tsigv,disgv? … Syrup-i’le yigi, sdi gadu tsiwatlvsgv nowu’nv etiyv tsusdalugisgi, tsehv gohu,sdi … diquayodi yusdi, sgi’dv yusdi, na gadu watlvsgv *hii* squu yigidi, gehv sgidv’no o-ogina,detiyisgv’e nowu’dv tsosdigisgv (uyetsi,sgv) osda tsoginiyelvsv uganasdi, tsigehv … nahiyu tsigesv squu’dv usdi yunotlvna, ase’dv oginigisdi, gehv nowu noginigvna, yigi, “sdvsa’wu sdelisdi,” oginosv tsigehv squu “agona, sdvnesdi, nihi, sdelisdi, gehesdi, sgina, yusdi, tsiga-tsigali-tsigvnistanvsgv, … nagitsehvna, yiga iga gvdiho” tsadisgv, tsigehv … “nitsagvna, yigehesdi, yitsayo--yitsayosisgesdi, gohiyv’no nihi tsvniya,sadi gesesdi,” adihv (uyetsi,sgv) doyu sgidv dana,daweseho tsigehv dohv? asenv, gohiyv tsigi, diniyotli dana,dvsgv ase’dv--
segments.translation: Yeah. And then the sweet. What was it she used? It might’ve been syrup. She’d put just a little bit on top. It was shiny like black pepper. She would lay it on top. It was just a little one. So that’s what we were eating on our birthdays. [laughs] We liked them because they were sweet. Back then, whatever they fixed we had to eat it. If we didn’t eat it, “It’s up to you all,” she told us. “If y’all want to go without food. That’s why I cook so much. I cook with what I have,” she used to say. “If you don’t eat it, then you’ll be hungry after a while. And it’ll be your fault,” she said. [laughs] That’s what they used to say back then, but today, these kids that are growing up all they know --

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: --McDonalds!

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: McDonalds, Pizza Hut-Ꭲ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, … ᎠᏎᏃ, ᎣᏏ … ᏦᎩᎾ,ᏓᎵᏏ ᏙᎪᎩᎾ,ᏝᏫ,ᏍᏓ, ᎠᏴ, ᏗᎨᏲᎲᏍᎩ, ᏌᏭ ᏐᏁᎳ, ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏐᎢ’Ꮕ, ᏔᎵ,Ꮪ ᏃᏭ, ᏔᎵ,Ꮪ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᎢᎸᎯᏳ’Ꮓ dumplings ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎪ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ,’Ꮓ biscuits ᎡᎵᏭ ᏱᏕᎪᏢᎾ, ‘ᏍᎦᏍᏗ’Ꮫ ᎣᏍᏓᏓᏍᏓᏴᏅ ᎢᎾ (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: McDonalds, Pizza Hut-i’le yigi, … aseno, osi … tsogina,dalisi dogogina,tlawi,sda, ayv, digeyohvsgi, sawu sonela, yudetiyvda, soi’nv, tali,du nowu, tali,du yudetiyvda, ilvhiyu’no dumplings degotlvsgo nowu’nv, usdikani,’no biscuits eliwu yidegotlvna, ‘sgasdi’dv osdadasdayvnv ina (uyetsi,sgv)
segments.translation: --is McDonald’s and Pizza Hut. But we made a deal, when we got kids that she [his wife] will teach them to cook. One is nine years old and the other is twelve. The 12 year old makes dumplings. And the younger one makes biscuits. We really enjoy eating their cooking. [laughs]

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏍᏚᏗ ᏥᏥᏯᎥ … ᎠᏎ’Ꮫ … “Chief is gonna cook!” ᏯᎾᏓ, ᏥᎨᎲ 5-gallon bucket ᏥᏩᏍᏕᏗ, ᎠᎩᎰ ᎨᎲ ᏙᏳ’Ꮓ microwave-Ꭲ ᏫᎦᏮᏠᎯᏍᏗ ᎾᏮᏅ Cornish Hen-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, ᏙᏣᏓᏃᏍᎩᏍᎪ ᎨᎲ Chow Hall ᎠᏂᏲᏢ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏩᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ, ᏍᎩᎾᎾ Cornish Hen-Ꭲ roman noodle-Ꭲ Ꮎ seasoning ᏥᎦᏢᏍᏗᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎬᏗᎰ for my broth ᎪᎸᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᏥᏔᎦ, ᏥᎬᎭᎷᏍᎬ ᎦᎵᏟ,ᏗᏍᎬ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏆᏗᏕᎾ,’Ꮓ ᎤᏩᏂ,Ꮠ ᎣᏍᏓ,’Ꮓ ᎤᏩᏂ,Ꮠ ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏳᏪᎵᏍᏗ, tortillas ᎠᎻ’Ꮕ, ᎤᏗᏞᎩ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏟᏍᎬ Ꮎ tortillas ᏂᏕᏥᎸᏍᎬ ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ, ᏍᏓᏱ ᏂᏕᎬᏁᎲ ᎦᏐᏆᎸ ᏂᎬᏁᎲ coke-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, pop ᎠᏟᏍᏛ can. The way you use, Ꮎ roll ᏂᎬᏁᎰ ᏌᎨ ᏱᎾᏮᏁᎳ, ᏕᏥᎬᎭᎷᏍᎬ ᏕᏥᎸᏍᎬ ᎾᎲ for dumplings … I like my dumplings ᏍᏗ--Ꮭ ᏯᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, ᎤᏩᎾᏬᏐᏅ I like a little texture, ᏍᏗ ᏍᏓᏱ ᏳᏍᏗ, firm-ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩᎸᏉ,Ꮧ, ᏍᎩᎾ ᎨᎲ ᏂᏕᏥᏴᏁᎲ Boy, ᏙᏳ’ᏛᏲ ᎠᎾᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ … ᎠᏎ’ᏛᏲ ᎠᏩᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ, ᎾᏅᏁᎲ Christmas-Ꭲ’Ꮕ, ᏳᎷᏣ, ᏂᎦᏓ, ᏚᏂᏩᏍᎬ ᏗᎨᏥᏍᏚᏅ ᎤᏂᏩᏍᏒᏍᎪ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏦᏍᎪᎯ, ᎢᎦ pizzas ᏕᎪᎸᏍᎬ ᎠᏮᏌ, *ᎯᎢ* ᏗᎩᏓ, ᏂᏕᎬᏁᎲ cardboard-Ꭲ’Ꮽ ᎢᎦᏗ ᏕᏥᏢᎯᏍᎦ.
segments.transliteration: tsuna,dasdudi tsitsiyav … ase’dv … “Chief is gonna cook!” yanada, tsigehv 5-gallon bucket tsiwasdedi, agiho gehv doyu’no microwave-i wigawvtlohisdi nawvnv Cornish Hen-i’nv, dotsadanosgisgo gehv Chow Hall aniyotlv gehv awadasdayvdi, sginana Cornish Hen-i roman noodle-i na seasoning tsigatlvsdihv sgina gvdiho for my broth golvsgv na tsitaga, tsigvhalusgv galitli,disgv nowu’nv, uli,squadidena,’no uwani,so osda,’no uwani,so osda, yuwelisdi, tortillas ami’nv, uditlegi, tsigehv tsitlisgv na tortillas nidetsilvsgv nowu’nv, sdayi nidegvnehv gasoqualv nigvnehv coke-i’nv, pop atlisdv can. The way you use, na roll nigvneho sage yinawvnela, detsigvhalusgv detsilvsgv nahv for dumplings … I like my dumplings sdi--tla yagilvquo,di, uwanawosonv I like a little texture, sdi sdayi yusdi, firm-yusdi, sgina agilvquo,di, sgina gehv nidetsiyvnehv Boy, doyu’dvyo anali,sdayvhvsgo tsigehv … ase’dvyo awadasdayv,di, nanvnehv Christmas-i’nv, yulutsa, nigada, duniwasgv digetsisdunv uniwassvsgo ilvhiyu tsosgohi, iga pizzas degolvsgv awvsa, *hii* digida, nidegvnehv cardboard-i’wu igadi detsitlvhisga.
segments.translation: When I was in prison, they would say, “Chief’s gonna cook.” I had a five-gallon bucket with a lid. There was a microwave I could use. Then we stole “Cornish Hen” from the Chow Hall. They would bring it for me to cook. It was that Cornish Hen and ramen noodle with the seasoning [packet] in it. That’s what I used for my broth. Then I cut up chicken and boiled it. Then when I thought it was about ready, when it was really done; then I would put tortillas in hot water, when they got firm I would make them round. Then I would get a can of coke and I would roll the [tortilla] dough with that. When I got it thin enough then I would cut them up and put them in [the broth]. That’s what I did for dumplings. I don’t like my dumplings gooey. I like them to have a little texture and I want them to be firm. That’s the way I fixed them. And boy did they eat it. They always made me cook. When it was Christmas all the prisoners bought food. Sometimes I made 30 pizzas by myself. I made them this [gestures] big. I just put them on cardboard.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: The prisoners all were proud of you. [laughs]

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: “Anything, I can cook anything,” I told them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Were they counting that toward your time being in jail?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Uh uh.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Uh uh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They weren’t?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They didn’t feel sorry for you.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: If it weren’t for you, they wouldn’t have been eating.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What about the people that raised you? Were they working?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: The one’s that raised me?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏝᏍᎪ, … ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎤᏂᏃᎮᏢ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎪ,Ꮧ, ᏴᏛᎾ,? ᎢᎦᏓ,’Ꭱ ᏭᏅᎦ,Ꮫ ᎨᎲ ᏴᏫ, ᏧᏂ,ᏍᏗ ᏓᏂᏃᎮ Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏣᏛᎦᏅ ᏱᎩ,?
segments.transliteration: vv tlasgo, … gohu,sdi, uninohetlv yigehe usquanigo,di, yvdvna,? igada,’e wunvga,dv gehv yvwi, tsuni,sdi daninohe tla gohu,sdi, tsadvganv yigi,?
segments.translation: Yeah. Did they talk about something that was interesting? Most people talk about little people. You didn’t hear anything?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Just this one. [gestures to Dianna]
[laughter]

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Hey!

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Or ghosts?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, or ghosts, monsters that they talked about. Nothing?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.translation: Or bigfoot!

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They didn’t talk about anything?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏃᎮᎮ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏯᏆ,ᏛᏓᏍᏛ ᎠᏴ
segments.transliteration: aninohehe tsigehv tla howa yaqua,dvdasdv ayv
segments.translation: They did talk about things, but I didn’t listen.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: … ᏂᎯ’ᏃᎲ Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, Ꮳ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᏱᎨᎮ? ᎢᎦᏓ,’Ꭱ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᎠᎾ,ᏛᎩᏍᎬ ᎨᏒ … ᏂᎯ’ᏃᎲ?
segments.transliteration: … nihi’nohv tla gohu,sdi, tsa,dvganv yigehe? igada,’e aniwonisgv ana,dvgisgv gesv … nihi’nohv?
segments.translation: And you? [Mack] You didn’t hear anything? People talking about things that they were hearing? How about you?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎥᎥ … ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᏗᎦᎸᎳ,Ꮧ, ᏗᏢ, … ᎬᎿᎨ ᏅᏱ ᎦᏝ,Ꭼ ᎤᎾ ᎮᎾ, ᏴᏛᎬᎦ, ᎢᎸᎯᏳ Ꮟ-Ꮟ-Ꮟ ᎪᎯ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎤᏁᏡᎬ ᎤᎾ ᏱᏣᎷᏣ, ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᏙᏳ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᏩᏂ--smooth-Ꭲ’Ꮫ ᏄᏅᏃ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏙᏳ, ᏱᎩ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ,Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏄᏓᎴ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᏮᎾ, ᎤᎾ ᎮᎾ, “ᏴᏫ, ᏧᏂ,ᏍᏗ ᎮᎾ, ᎠᎾᎢ,” ᏯᎾᏓ,’Ꭱ ᎨᎲ ᎡᏚᏥ,’Ꭱ ᏙᏱᎢᏢ ᎤᏬᏢ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ, “ᏛᎾᎢᏒ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎦᏁᏥ,Ꮭ ᎤᏑᎸ Ꮎ ᎠᏧᏣ,” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎾᏅ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ,” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎤᏌᏃᏒ” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᏓᏂ,ᏙᎯᏂᏒ ᏔᎷ-ᏔᎷᏥ ‘ᏔᎷᎩᏍᎩ ᎠᎯᏒ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ,” ᏣᏗᎲ “ᎠᏂᎶᎯ” ᏧᏛᏅ … ᏣᏂ ᎪᏎᎲ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᎤᎦ,ᏎᏍᏗ, ᎠᏗᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ Ᏻ-Ꭴ-ᎤᏍᏚᏅ ᏱᎨᎮ Ꮭ … ᏍᏊ ᎯᎳ ᎢᎦ ᎦᏃᏍᎩᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏰᏙᎲ, Ꮭ ᏯᏴᎯᎲ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ … ᏳᎨᎯᏓ, ᎨᎲ … ᎪᎱᏍᏗ’Ꮕ, ᏃᏒᎾ, ᏱᎩ, ᎠᏛᎦᏅ Ꮻ--ᏦᎢᎭ’Ꮫ ᎢᎦ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎦᏳᎳ, ᎤᏅ,Ꮩ ᎨᎲ ᎡᏚᏥ, ᏲᎩᏃᎯᏏ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏳᏲ-ᏱᏣᏲᎱᏎᎳ, your favorite. Their favorite…kin or whatever, ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏍᏓᏩᏚᎦ, ᎨᎲ … ᏥᏂᎬ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ, ᎠᏩᏗᏔᎯᏙᎸ ᏏᎵ, … ᎠᎵᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏙᏓᏩᏍᎬ ᏗᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᎵᏥ, ᏥᎨᎲ … ᏙᏓᏩᏍᎬ ᏒᎯᏰ ᎠᎩᎷᏨ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᏩᏁᏙᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏚᎵᎲ--Ꮭ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎬᎩᎪᎲ ᏱᎩ, ᎠᎩᏴᏍᏕᏓ, ᎠᎴ ᎦᏗᏍᏔᏍᎬ ᎠᏴ, ᏏᏓᏁᎸ ᎤᎾ,ᏛᏅ … ᏙᏳ, ᎠᎩᎷᏣ, ᎩᎳ’ᏭᏛ ᏩᏩᏂ,ᏏᏅ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏚᎵᏍᎨ ᎬᎩᎪᏩᏛᏗ --
segments.transliteration: vv … adanelv digalvla,di, ditlv, … gvhnage nvyi gatla,gv una hena, yvdvgvga, ilvhiyu si-si-si gohi diniyotli, unetlugv una yitsalutsa, etsulaha doyu, osda, wani--smooth-i’dv nunvno tla yawanv,ta, doyu, yigi, gohu,sdi,le yigi, nudale sgi yinuwvna, una hena, “yvwi, tsuni,sdi hena, anai,” yanada,’e gehv edutsi,’e doyiitlv uwotlv sawu yuwaga,da, “dvnaisv” tsadihv “ganetsi,tla usulv na atsutsa,” tsadihv “nanv ageyutsa,” tsadihv “usanosv” tsadihv “dani,dohinisv talu-talutsi ‘talugisgi ahisv usdi ageyutsa,” tsadihv “anilohi” tsudvnv … tsani gosehv gali,tsode uga,sesdi, adisgo tsigehv tla ilvhiyu yu-u-usdunv yigehe tla … squu hila iga ganosgisv sgina yedohv, tla yayvhihv gali,tsode … yugehida, gehv … gohusdi’nv, nosvna, yigi, advganv wi--tsoiha’dv iga agvyi gayula, unv,do gehv edutsi, yoginohisi, gehv sginana yuyo-yitsayohusela, your favorite. Their favorite…kin or whatever, sgina yusdawaduga, gehv … tsinigv sawu yuwagada, awaditahidolv sili, … alitsi tsigehv nigohilv dodawasgv dideyohvsgi, gehv alitsi, tsigehv … dodawasgv svhiye agilutsv tsunilawisdi wanedohv tla yawadulihv--tla ilvhiyu gvgigohv yigi, agiyvsdeda, ale gadistasgv ayv, sidanelv una,dvnv … doyu, agilutsa, gila’wudv wawani,sinv tla yawadulisge gvgigowadvdi --
segments.translation: Yeah. Right above the house there’s black dirt. You can still hear children hollering. When you go over there, the ground looks smooth. I don’t know if it’s true or not. When you see something like that, people would say, “It’s the little people.” One time my uncle was sitting on the porch and he saw children coming: “A boy with overalls on,” he said. “And a girl with a dress on and they were holding hands. And the girl was carrying a bucket.” “They went by,” he said. They called him John. He watched the house. He never locked it up, if there was a person around that stole things he wouldn’t let them in. He’d chase them off. If something happened about three days ago, my uncle already knew about it. He would tell us about it. If you passed away, the favorite kinfolk would follow him. One time, I was laying down, I had been drinking. Sil(i) and Alits(i)—Alits(i), she was the Sunday School teacher. When I came home on Sunday evening, they were at church. They, my family, said they had never seen me drunk or drinking. So, when I got back, I laid down. I didn’t want them to see me --

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: --them to see you --

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: --ᎬᎩᏒᏫᏍᏗ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᎤᏟᏍᏗ’Ꮽ ᏩᏩᏂ,ᏏᏅ, ᎤᏟᏍᏗ’Ꮽ ᏩᏩᏂ,ᏏᏅ … ᏥᏂᎬ ᏙᏱᎢᏢ’Ꮕ, ᎠᏐᏴ *ᎯᎢ* ᏱᎦᏘ, latch-ᎢᏅ, ᎠᎢ’Ꭾ ᎠᏍᏚᏗ spring-Ꭲ ᎫᏓᎶ ᎨᎲ … ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᎠᏬᎯᏳᏒ “ᎠᏂᎷᎩ” ᎠᏪᎵᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ’ᏭᏛ ᎠᏩᏚᏢᏅ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᏍᏚᏗ ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏚᎢᏌ, screen door ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏚᎢᏌ, ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᏍᏚᏗ ᏃᏭᎴ ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏚᎢᏌ, ᎤᎵ,ᏍᏚᏅ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᏧᏴᏝ, ᎩᎶ ᎤᏩᏂᎸ *thump* ᎠᏗᎰ ᎬᏂᎰ ᎠᎢᏐ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᏘᎬ’Ꮫ ᎣᏂ, ᏗᏢ ᏥᏳᎪ,Ꮧ’ᏭᏃ ᎦᏙᎬ ᎠᎩ,ᏍᎦᎯᏓ, ᎠᏩᏚᏝᎥ’ᏭᏛ ᏃᏭ, kitchen-Ꭲ ᏭᎷᏣ, Boy, ᏗᏖᎵᏙ’ᏛᏲ ᏚᎵ,ᎪᏛᏅ ᏚᏕᏏᏙᎸ ᎦᏳᎳ, ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᎦᏍᎩᎸ ᏱᏭᏴᎭ, ᏱᏭᏩᏌᏙᏯ, ᎤᏃᏴᎸᏍᎬ ᎠᏴ, ᏍᏊ’Ꮓ ᎠᏭ’ᏛᏅ ᏄᏍᏛ … ᎠᏩᏗᏓ,’Ꮫ ᎠᏩᏛᎾᏫ,ᏍᏙᏗ ᏓᎩᎪᎲ ᏗᏨᏱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎤᏂᎷᏨ ᏧᏂᏴᏝ, ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᎩᎳ’ᏭᏛ ᎠᏩᏗᏛᎲ ᎦᎵ,ᏦᏕ ᏩᏩᏕᎵᏨ “Boy, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ,’Ꮫ ᎠᏯ’Ꭰ” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᏏᎵ, “Kitchen-Ꭲ ᎠᎵ,ᎪᏛᏅ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎨᎲ ᎤᏴᏟᏢ” ᏥᏲᏎᎸ “ᏗᏖᎵᏙ ᏂᎬ ᎠᎮ ᎦᏝ,Ꭹ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ … ᎤᏨᏍᏛᏅ Kitchen-Ꭲ Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ‘ᎸᏢ ᏱᎦᎵ,ᎨᏴ ᎤᏬᎵ,ᏓᏁᎸ … ᎤᏰᎵ,Ꮫ’Ꭾ Ꮎ ᏣᏂᏝᏅᏍᎬ ᎤᏂ-ᎤᏂᏑᎸᏛ, ᎥᏳᏃ, ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎾᏝᎲᎾ, ᏱᎩ, Boy, ᏯᏍᎦᎮᏓ,’Ꮫ ᎨᎲ … ᏃᏭ’Ꮕ ᎤᏓᏍᏓᏴᏅ ᏏᎵ,’Ꮫ ᎩᎳ’ᏴᏛ ᎤᏟᏍᏗ, saltmeat ᏚᏮᏂᏍᏔᏅ ᎦᏚ ᎪᎢ ᏫᏚᏒᏂ,ᏔᏅ table-Ꭲ ᏭᏝᏅ ᎣᏝᏪ’ᏛᏃ Ꮭ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ,--
segments.transliteration: --gvgisvwisdi’le yigi, utlisdi’wu wawani,sinv, utlisdi’wu wawani,sinv … tsinigv doyiitlv’nv, asoyv *hii* yigati, latch-inv, ai’he asdudi spring-i gudalo gehv … aqua,dvganv awohiyusv “anilugi” awelihv osda’wudv awadutlvnv gali,tsode sdudi uli,sduisa, screen door uli,sduisa, aqua,dvganv sdudi nowule uli,sduisa, uli,sdunv gali,tsode tsuyvtla, gilo uwanilv *thump* adiho gvniho aiso agi,stigv’dv oni, ditlv tsiyugo,di’wuno gadogv agi,sgahida, awadutlav’wudv nowu, kitchen-i wulutsa, Boy, ditelido’dvyo duli,godvnv dudesidolv gayula, etsulaha gasgilv yiwuyvha, yiwuwasadoya, unoyvlvsgv ayv, squu’no awu’dvnv nusdv … awadida,’dv awadvnawi,sdodi dagigohv ditsvyi,sdi, unilutsv tsuniyvtla, gali,tsode gila’wudv awadidvhv gali,tsode wawadelitsv “Boy, gohu,sdi,’dv aya’a” tsiyohehv sili, “Kitchen-i ali,godvnv tla yawanv,ta, yusdi, gehv uyvtlitlv” tsiyoselv “ditelido nigv ahe gatla,gi” tsiyohelv … utsvsdvnv Kitchen-i tla gohu,sdi, ‘lvtlv yigali,geyv uwoli,danelv … uyeli,dv’he na tsanitlanvsgv uni-unisulvdv, vyuno, sgina, natlahvna, yigi, Boy, yasgaheda,’dv gehv … nowu’nv udasdayvnv sili,’dv gila’yvdv utlisdi, saltmeat duwvnistanv gadu goi widusvni,tanv table-i wutlanv otlawe’dvno tla gohu,sdi,--
segments.translation: --or smell me, when they got home. I was laying down. Outside on the porch, there was a fence about this [gestures] tall. It had a latch with a spring. I heard that and I thought they were home. So, I covered my head. When the door opened, I heard the screen door, it opened and closed. Something came in the house, and somebody knocked. [Thump] It knocked as it went along. The hair on the back of my neck was standing straight up. I was still covered up. When it got to the kitchen, the plates, boy, they started breaking. Like it was throwing them around, and also like it picked up a chair and threw it. The way it sounded. I was about ready to get up and run then I saw [car] lights. They were home. As soon as they came in the house, I jumped up and ran in there. “Boy, something is in the house!” I told Sil(i): “He tore up the kitchen. I don’t know what it was, but the plates are all broken on the floor.” She turned the light on in the kitchen. There wasn’t anything scattered on the floor. It was funny to her. There was a reason why they left the leftover food on the table. If there wasn’t anything on the table, boy it would throw a fit. Sil(i) started cooking right away. She cooked salt meat and bread and put it on the table. And things got quiet.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: --Nothing was making noise?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Nope. … ᏍᎩ-…ᏍᎩ-ᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᎠᎩᎪᎥ--ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᎠᏩᏌ,
segments.transliteration: Nope. … sgi-…sgi-sgi iga agigov--aqua,dvganv’le yigi, awasa,
segments.translation: Nope. That’s all I’ve seen or heard about, myself.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏙᏳ,’Ꮫ ᎡᎵᏏ, ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᏊ … ᏫᏥᏩ,ᏛᎯᏙᎯ, ᎠᏎᏅ, Ꮓ--ᏃᎨᏠᏅᏨᎾ, ᏍᏗ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏥᏩᏝᎲᏍᎨ ᎦᏍᎩᎶ
segments.transliteration: Yeah, doyu,’dv elisi, tsigehv squu … witsiwa,dvhidohi, asenv, no--nogetlonvtsvna, sdi gohu,sdi, tsiwatlahvsge gasgilo
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s right. I used to visit my grandmother and before we went to sleep she would put food on the table.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: They were leaving food for it to eat.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏍᏊ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏠᏱ, ᎠᏆ,ᏛᎦᏅ ᏗᏩᏛᏏᏒ ᏍᏊ ᏍᏊ-ᏍᏊ ᏍᏊ ᏐᎢ,-ᏐᎢ, ᎨᎲ … ᎩᎶ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᎧᏃᎮᏢ ᎤᏠᏱ’Ꮽ, ᏥᎩ, … ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᎤᏃᏴᎬ ᏙᏱ, … ᎤᏒ’Ᏼ ᏗᏢ, Ꮎ ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ ᏗᏢ, ᏃᏭᎴ ᏄᏓᎴᏒ ᏓᎾᏛᎩ ᏃᏭ ᏳᎾᎴᏂᏒ Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, Ꭴ-Ꭴ-Ꭴ…
segments.transliteration: squu squu utloyi, aqua,dvganv diwadvsisv squu squu-squu squu soi,-soi, gehv … gilo yonega, kanohetlv utloyi’wu, tsigi, … gohu,sdi, unoyvgv doyi, … usv’yv ditlv, na tsuna,dasdayv,di ditlv, nowule nudalesv danadvgi nowu yunalenisv tla gohusdi, u-u-u…
segments.translation: I’ve heard the same thing when I was growing up. And another thing, there was a White person who was telling the same thing. Something was making a noise outside at night, it was toward the kitchen. When they checked there was nothing there.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: They didn’t bother anything, nothing had moved?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Huh uh. Huh uh. … ᏃᏭᎴ ᏣᏥ--ᎩᎶ ᏣᏓ, ᏣᏥᏃᏎᎲ ᏍᏊ ᏍᏊ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏥᎨᏒ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏣᏥᏃᏎᎴ “ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎠᎵ,ᏍᏓᏴ,Ꮧ, ᏱᏣᎯᏯᏍᏔᎾ … ᏙᎯ, ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎵ,ᏍᏓ,” ᏙᏳ, ᏥᏄᎾ,ᏛᏁᎸ ᏍᎩᏃ, ᏙᎯ, ᏥᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏥᎾᎾ,ᏛᏁ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ … Yeah, ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎩ ᎤᏠᏱ, ᎤᏃᎯᏳᎯ, ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ, ᎢᎦᏓ, (ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ) ᎢᎦᏓ,
segments.transliteration: Huh uh. Huh uh. … nowule tsatsi--gilo tsada, tsatsinosehv squu squu yonega, tsigesv utloyi tsatsinosele “gohusdi, ali,sdayv,di, yitsahiyastana … dohi, yini,gali,sda,” doyu, tsinuna,dvnelv sgino, dohi, tsinuli,stanv nigohilv sgina, tsinana,dvne nuli,stanv … Yeah, aniyonegi utloyi, unohiyuhi, sgiyusdi, igada, (uyetsi,sgv) igada,
segments.translation: Uh uh. Uh uh. Somebody had told him about it—they were also a White person. “If you leave out some food, it’ll calm down,” they said. So, they did that and it did get quiet. Then they kept doing it. Yeah, the White people believe in something like that, ghost stories. Some of them. [laughs] Some.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Some. And some of them will tell you, “You’re crazy.”
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎯᎢᎾ ᏓᏍᏛᏯᏛᏛᏂ, ᏃᏭ, … Ꭰ-Ꭰ-ᎠᏓᏛᏛᎲᏍᎩ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎠᏎᏅ, ᎢᎸᏍᎩ, ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏱᏩᏟᎢᎶᏢ ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ, ᏍᏗ’ᏭᎨ Ꮟ ᎠᎢᏎᏍᏗ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᏒ? ᏙᎨ? ᏫᏛᏍᎪᎸᏥ? ᏙᎯ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏫᏂ,ᏓᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂ?
segments.transliteration: hiina dasdvyadvdvni, nowu, … a-a-adadvdvhvsgi, ahani, asenv, ilvsgi, tsudetiyvda, yiwatliilotlv gayu,la, sdi’wuge si aisesdi, atsalagi, gawonihisdi gesv? doge? widvsgolvtsi? dohi,’le yigi, wini,dagali,stani?
segments.translation: I’m going to ask y’all this now. We ask this here all the time. In a few years, is the Cherokee language going to still be here, or is it just going to go away or disappear?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎠᏴ’Ꮕ ᎠᏬᎯᏳ ᎯᎢ’Ꮫ ᏄᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᎥᎾ, ᎨᎮᏍᏗ, ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᏛᏲᎱᏎᎵ,
segments.transliteration: ayv’nv awohiyu hii’dv nuna,delo,quavna, gehesdi, diniyotli, dvyohuseli,
segments.translation: This is what I believe—if the children don’t learn to talk it’s just going to go away.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What about you?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: I think the same.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎤᏠᏱ’ᏭᎡ … Ꮎ’ᏃᎲ ‘Ꮩ ᏍᏕᎵᎰ ᏴᏛᎾ, ᎯᎢ, ᏥᏓᎾ,ᏕᎶ,Ꮖ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎤᏂᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ Ꮵ-ᏥᏕᎨᎨᏲᎲᏍᎩ,
segments.transliteration: utloyi’wue … na’nohv ‘do sdeliho yvdvna, hii, tsidana,delo,qua diniyotli, atsalagi, uniwonihisdi tsi-tsidegegeyohvsgi,
segments.translation: The same. What do you all think about the kids that are going to school and teaching them to speak Cherokee?

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: I think they are doing good, that they are teaching them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᎡᎵ’ᏭᏛ ᏛᎵ,ᏍᏕᎵ,ᏙᏔᏂ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᏒ ᏭᏩᎦ,ᏗᏗᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏙᎨ? ᏙᎯ, Ꮒ,ᏓᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂ, ᏛᏍᎪᎸᏥ,?
segments.transliteration: sgi eli’wudv dvli,sdeli,dotani, atsalagi, gawonihisdi gesv wuwaga,didisv tsadihv doge? dohi, ni,dagali,stani, dvsgolvtsi,?
segments.translation: I think that is going to help the language, as it goes. What you said, do you think it’s just going to disappear?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: Ᏹ’ᎠᏓ--Ᏹ’ᎠᏓ ᏩᏂᏍᏛᏅ’Ꮽ ᏫᏛᎾ,ᏓᏲᏒ ᏓᎾ,ᏕᏲᎲᏍᎬ ᏛᏲᎱᏎᎵ, … Ꮭ-Ꮭ ᏭᏟ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ, ᏱᏛᏟᎢᎵᏙᎵ, ᎦᏳᎳ, ᏃᏭ, ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎩ, this generation ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ, ᏔᎵ,Ꮪ Ꮶ’ᎠᏚ ᏧᎾ,ᏕᏘᏴᏓ, ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, even some in [their] 20’s ᏧᎾ,ᏕᏘᏴᏓ, Ꮭ-Ꮭ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᏯᏂᏬᏂᎯ, … Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, … Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ, ᏯᎾ,ᏕᎰᏍᎩ, “ᏄᏓᎴ ᏱᏃᏥᏫ,” ᏯᏁ-ᏯᏁᎵ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᎤᎬᏫᏳ ᎤᎾ-ᎤᎾ,ᏡᏗ ᎾᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᎬᎾ, ᏥᎩ, … ᎠᎾ,ᏕᎰᏍᎬ “ᏓᏲ’ᎢᏰᏣᏍᏔᏂ,’Ꮫ” ᎠᏁᎵᏍᎬ “ᏄᏓᎴ ᏱᏃᎩᏪᏌ, ᏓᏲ-“ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ, ᎤᎬᏫᏳ ᎤᎾ,ᏡᏗ ᎾᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᎬᎾ, ᏥᎩ, … Ꮭ ᎮᎾ, ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏳᏰᎵ,Ꮧ, Ꮿ-ᏯᏕᎰᏍᎬ, ᏙᏳ ᎪᎱ,ᏍᏗ, ᏣᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ ᏱᏣᏚᎵ
segments.transliteration: yi’ada--yi’ada wanisdvnv’wu widvna,dayosv dana,deyohvsgv dvyohuseli, … tla-tla wutli yigohida, yidvtliilidoli, gayula, nowu, hena, tsigi, this generation nowu tsigi, tali,du tso’adu tsuna,detiyvda, diniyotli, tla hena, even some in [their] 20’s tsuna,detiyvda, tla-tla tsalagi, yaniwonihi, … tla yawanv,ta, … tla yawanv,ta, yana,dehosgi, “nudale yinotsiwi,” yane-yaneli sgi hena, ugvwiyu una-una,tludi nana,delo,quasgvna, tsigi, … ana,dehosgv “dayo’iyetsastani,’dv” anelisgv “nudale yinogiwesa, dayo-“ sgi hena, ugvwiyu una,tludi nana,delo,quasgvna, tsigi, … tla hena, gohu,sdi, yuyeli,di, ya-yadehosgv, doyu gohu,sdi, tsadelo,quasdi yitsaduli
segments.translation: I say that if they quit teaching or give up teaching, we are going to lose it. And it’s not going to take long because already, this generation, the children that are 12 or 13 years old. Or even some in their 20s, they are not speaking Cherokee. I don’t know. I don’t know if they’re embarrassed. That they think “We will not be saying our words right.” That’s the reason they are not learning. They are embarrassed, they think “We will talk wrong or say something wrong.” They feel left out and they don’t want to be laughed at. That’s the main reason why they’re not learning it and they feel excluded. They’re embarrassed, shy, thinking, “They’re going to laugh at us. If we say it wrong,” That’s why they’re feeling excluded. There’s no need to be embarrassed if you want to learn something.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎢᎦᏓ,’Ꮫ Ꮭ ᏳᎵ,ᏍᎨᏗ, ᏯᏁᎵᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ ᎠᏬᎯᏳ ᎤᏁᎳᏅ ᎠᎩᏁᎸ ᎠᎩᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, ᏍᎩ-ᏍᎩ-ᏍᎩᏴ ᏭᎵ,ᏍᏛ Ꭴ-ᎤᎵ,ᏍᎨᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎩᏂᏅᎾᎳᏁᎸ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏄᏰᎵ,Ꮫ ᎠᏩᏚᎸᏓ, … ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ,
segments.transliteration: igada,’dv tla yuli,sgedi, yanelisgo sginana tsalagi, gawonihisdi, ayv, hena awohiyu unelanv aginelv agiwonihisdi, sgi-sgi-sgiyv wuli,sdv u-uli,sgedi gehv gininvnalanelv sginana nuyeli,dv awadulvda, … yuli,sdodi,
segments.translation: Some don’t think it’s important, sacred to learn to speak Cherokee. I believe that God gave me this language to talk with. I think it is really important that He made this path for us. That’s why I want it to happen.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᏙᎯᏳᏐᏍᎪ, … ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ, ᏱᎩ, ᏃᏭ’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᏳᏓᏅᏌ,’Ꮄ ᏱᎩ, ᎤᏔᎾ, ᏙᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᏳᏪᏙᎳ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ, ᎤᏲᎱ,ᏎᏗ Ꮎ’Ꮫ ᎤᏮᎨᏩ,Ꮜ,-ᎤᏮᎨᏩ,Ꮟ ᏦᎯᏳᏐᏍᎪ,?
segments.transliteration: sdohiyusosgo, … atsalagi, osda, gawonisgi, yigi, nowu’le yigi, yudanvsa,’le yigi, utana, dodigaduhv yuwedola, atsalagi, gawonihisdi, uyohu,sedi na’dv uwvgewa,sa,-uwvgewa,si tsohiyusosgo,?
segments.translation: Do you all believe that if somebody that speaks Cherokee well and they moved to a big city, do you believe that they will lose the language? Or forget how to talk? Do you believe that?

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎠᏴ Ꮭ’Ꮫ ᏯᏬᎯᏳ ᎢᏳ’Ꮫ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎯᎦ,ᏔᎭ ᏣᏅ,Ꮤ, ᎤᏠᏱ’Ꮫ it’s just like riding a bike, Ꮭ ᏱᎦᏨᎨᏩ, … ᎠᏴ, ᎮᎾ, ᎨᎲ ᎠᏬᎯᏳ ᎠᎵ,ᏍᎪᎢ ᏴᏫ, “ᎠᏮᎨᏩ,’Ꮫ” ᏳᏛᎾ,
segments.transliteration: ayv tla’dv yawohiyu iyu’dv tsalagi, higa,taha tsanv,ta, utloyi’dv it’s just like riding a bike, tla yigatsvgewa, … ayv, hena, gehv awohiyu ali,sgoi yvwi, “awvgewa,’dv” yudvna,
segments.translation: Me, I don’t think so. If you know how to speak Cherokee, y’know, it’s just like riding a bike. You won’t forget it. I believe that if someone says, “I forgot,” they’re lying.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Me too. I believe that too.

segments.speaker: edward-bunch
segments.translation: I tell them, “What are you saying?”
[laughter]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꮓ ᏴᏫ, ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎩ, ᏴᏛᎾ, ᎤᏩᏌ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ ᏱᎩ, ᎢᎦᏓ, ᎮᎾ, ᎦᏥᎵᏃᎮᏔᏅ ᎤᏩᏌ, ᏰᎲ ᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎩ, “ᎠᏮᏌ’Ꮽ ᎦᏓᏝᏃᎮᏗᏍᎪ ᎠᏴ’Ꮫ ᎾᏮᎨᏫ,ᏍᏗ ᏂᎨᏒᎾ,”
segments.transliteration: na’no yvwi, hena, tsigi, yvdvna, uwasa, gawonisgi yigi, igada, hena, gatsilinohetanv uwasa, yehv tsalagi, gawonisgi, “awvsa’wu gadatlanohedisgo ayv’dv nawvgewi,sdi nigesvna,”
segments.translation: When a person talks and is by himself. I talk to people that speaks Cherokee and they say they talk to themselves so they won’t forget it. “I talk to myself, so I won’t forget”

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᏍᏊ’Ꮫ ᎿᏓᏝᏃᎮᏗᎲᎾ ᏱᎩ, ᎠᎭᏂ, ᎮᎾ, ᎭᏓᏅ,ᏖᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: squu’dv hnadatlanohedihvna yigi, ahani, hena, hadanv,tesgo
segments.translation: Even if you don’t talk to yourself, you think about it.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏙᏳᎢ ᏍᏊ ᏍᏊ ᎩᏟ, Ꮣ-ᏓᎩᎾᏝ Ꭸ-ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎨᏥᎵᏃᎮᏗ ᎢᎦᏓ’Ꮕ, ᎠᏃᎵ,Ꭼ, ᏳᏍᏗ, Ꮒ,ᏥᏪᏍᎬ “ᏦᏞᏍᏗ!” ᏯᏩᏛᎾ, ᏯᎾᎵ,ᏍᏛᏡᎦ, “ᎣᏍᏓ, ᎭᏂ,ᏒᎦ,!” ᏃᏭᎴ ᏯᏂ,ᏒᎦ, -- “ᏣᏲᏏᏍᎪ,?” ᏯᏩᏛᎾ, “Mhm,” ᏯᎾᏓ,
segments.transliteration: doyui squu squu gitli, da-daginatla ge-atsalagi getsilinohedi igada’nv, anoli,gv, yusdi, ni,tsiwesgv “tsotlesdi!” yawadvna, yanali,sdvtluga, “osda, hani,svga,!” nowule yani,svga, -- “tsayosisgo,?” yawadvna, “Mhm,” yanada,
segments.translation: That’s true. Also, I have dogs that I talk Cherokee to them. Some of them understand what I’m saying. When I tell them to sit, they sit. Or if I say “lay down,” they’ll lay down. If I say “Are you hungry? “Mm-hmm,” they’ll say.
[laughter]

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.text: ᎨᏥᏲᏎᎲ “Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᎩᏟ, ᏓᎩᎧᎭ, ᏤᏥ-- ᎤᎪᏓ, ᏙᏳ,’Ᏺ ᎠᏃᎯᏳᎲ ᏏᎾ, ᏗᏂᏲᏟ, ᎨᎲ” ᎨᏥᏲᎮᎲ
segments.transliteration: getsiyosehv “na’e gitli, dagikaha, tsetsi-- ugoda, doyu,’yo anohiyuhv sina, diniyotli, gehv” getsiyohehv
segments.translation: That’s what I was telling them. “My dogs understand Cherokee better than the children,” I told them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, … ᎠᏲᏟ, ᏲᎨᏲᎲᏍᎬ, ᎠᏣᎳᎩ, ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ “ᎠᎩᏲᏏ”’Ꮫ ᎠᎯᏗ’Ꮽ, ᎤᎾ,ᏕᎶ,ᏆᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ “ᎠᎩᏲᏏ Grandma” ᏯᎾᏓ, ᎮᎾ, … Well, ᎦᎵᎡᎵᎦ!
segments.transliteration: atsalagi, … ayotli, yogeyohvsgv, atsalagi, gawonihisdi “agiyosi”’dv ahidi’wu, una,delo,quasdi sgina “agiyosi Grandma” yanada, hena, … Well, galieliga!
segments.translation: If you’re teaching a child to speak Cherokee, say “agiyosi – I’m hungry,” that’s easy for them to learn. [ᎤᏰᏥ,ᏍᎬ] They’ll say “agiyosi, Grandma.” Well, I’m glad that we got to visit for a little while.

segments.speaker: mack-flynn
segments.translation: Me, too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: --that we got to visit for a little while.
